#### [Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227855 .Subheading}

- **[[1.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.22
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Parts 3 to 5 and 17 do not apply to
  the handling, offering for transport or transporting of dangerous
  goods on a road vehicle if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} dangerous goods included in Class 2, Gases, they
      are in one or more means of containment in compliance with the
      requirements for transporting gases in Part 5 (Means of
      Containment), or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} dangerous goods not included in Class 2, they
      are in one or more means of containment designed, constructed,
      filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal
      conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no
      release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are transported solely on land
    between a retail place of purchase and place of destination and the
    distance on public roads is less than or equal to 100 km;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the gross mass of all dangerous goods on the road
    vehicle is less than or equal to 3 000 kg;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are to be or have been used by
    a farmer for farming purposes; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods do not include

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} Class 1, Explosives, other than explosives
      included in Class 1.4S,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, in a cylinder with a
      capacity greater than 46 L,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} Class 2.3, Toxic Gases,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} Class 6.2, Infectious Substances, or

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} Class 7, Radioactive Materials.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite the exemption from Part 3 (Documentation) in
  subsection (1), when an ERAP is required under Part 7 (Emergency
  Response Assistance Plan) the dangerous goods for which the plan is
  required must be accompanied by a shipping document.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 11
- SOR/2019-101, s. 22
- [SOR/2023-155, s. 16](#1407950-1418196){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1407950-1418196.html"
  role="button"}

  role="button"}

#### [Agriculture: Pesticide Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227873 .Subheading}

- **[[1.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.23
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Part 3 (Documentation), the
  requirements for the display of a UN number in section 4.15 of Part 4
  (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) and Part 6 (Training) do not apply to a
  solution of pesticides in transport on a road vehicle if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are transported solely on land
    for a distance less than or equal to 100 km;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are in a large means of
    containment that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} has a capacity that is less than or equal to
      6 000 L, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is used to prepare the dangerous goods for
      application or to apply the dangerous goods; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} only one large means of containment containing the
    solution of pesticides is in transport on the road vehicle.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite the exemption for documentation in subsection
  (1), when an ERAP is required under Part 7 (Emergency Response
  Assistance Plan), the dangerous goods must be accompanied by a
  shipping document.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 12
- SOR/2019-101, s. 22
:::

#### [Agriculture: Anhydrous Ammonia Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227884 .Subheading}

**[[1.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.24 .sectionLabel}** Part 3
(Documentation) and Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance Plan) do not
apply to UN1005, ANHYDROUS AMMONIA, if it is

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in transport solely on land and the distance on
  public roads is less than or equal to 100 km; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in a large means of containment with a capacity that
  is less than or equal to 10 000 L and is used for the field
  application of anhydrous ammonia.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 8
- SOR/2008-34, s. 13
:::

#### [Transportation within a Facility]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227890 .Subheading}

**[[1.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.25 .sectionLabel}** These Regulations do
not apply to dangerous goods that are transported solely within a
manufacturing or processing facility to which public access is
controlled.

#### [Emergency Response Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227892 .Subheading}

**[[1.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.26 .sectionLabel}** These Regulations do
not apply to dangerous goods that are in quantities necessary to respond
to an emergency that endangers public safety and that are in transport
in a means of transport that is dedicated to emergency response, unless
the dangerous goods are forbidden for transport in Schedule 1, Schedule
3 or, for transport by aircraft, the ICAO Technical Instructions.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 14
:::

#### [Operation of a Means of Transport or a Means of Containment Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227896 .Subheading}

- **[[1.27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.27
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} These Regulations do not apply to
  dangerous goods on a means of transport that are required for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the propulsion of the means of transport and that
    are

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} intended to remain on the means of transport
      until used, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} contained in a fuel tank permanently installed
      on the means of transport;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the safety of individuals on board the means of
    transport;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the operation or safety of the means of transport
    including, while installed in the means of transport and used or
    likely to be used for purposes related to transport, air bags, air
    brakes, flares, lighting, shock absorbers or fire extinguishers; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} ventilation, refrigeration or heating units that
    are necessary to maintain environmental conditions within a means of
    containment in transport on the means of transport and are intended
    to remain with the units or on the means of transport until used.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The exemption in subsection (1) does not apply to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} ammunition; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} dangerous goods being delivered to a destination
    and from which a portion is drawn off during transport for
    propulsion of the means of transport.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 14
:::

#### [Transportation between Two Properties]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227910 .Subheading}

**[[1.28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.28 .sectionLabel}** These Regulations do
not apply to dangerous goods, other than Class 1, Explosives, or
Class 7, Radioactive Materials, that are in transport on a road vehicle
between two properties owned or leased by the manufacturer, producer or
user of the dangerous goods if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are transported a distance less
  than or equal to 3 km on a public road;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the road vehicle has displayed on it

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the placard for the primary class of each of the
    dangerous goods, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the DANGER placard;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are in one or more means of
  containment designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and
  maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including
  handling, there will be no release of the dangerous goods that could
  endanger public safety; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the local police are advised, in writing, of the
  nature of the dangerous goods no more than 12 months in advance of the
  transport.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 15
- [SOR/2023-155, s. 17](#1407955-1418198){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1407955-1418198.html"
  role="button"}
:::

#### [Ferry Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227921 .Subheading}

**[[1.30]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.30 .sectionLabel}** Paragraph 3.6(3)(a)
of Part 3 (Documentation), and subsection 4.16(3) and paragraph
4.16.1(2)(d) of Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) do not apply to
dangerous goods in transport on a road vehicle or railway vehicle that
is being transported on board a vessel that is operating over the most
direct water route between two points that are not more than 5 km apart.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 17
- SOR/2017-253, s. 6
:::

#### [Propane and Gasoline in Highway Tanks on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227925 .Subheading}

**[[1.30.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.30.1 .sectionLabel}** Subsection 1.6(1)
and paragraph 3.6(3)(a) do not apply to dangerous goods that are UN1203,
GASOLINE, or UN1978, PROPANE, that are in a highway tank that is being
transported by a tank truck on board a passenger carrying vessel that is
operating over the most direct water route between two points that are
not more than 5 km apart if the following conditions are met:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} no more than two tank trucks transporting dangerous
  goods that are UN1203, GASOLINE or UN1978, PROPANE are on board the
  passenger carrying vessel;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} before the tank truck is placed on board the
  passenger carrying vessel, the highway tank is visually inspected by
  its driver for dents or evidence of leakage;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the tank truck is located on an open deck;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a safety perimeter of at least 1 m is established
  around the tank truck while it is on board the passenger carrying
  vessel;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the tank truck's parking brakes are set securely
  throughout the journey until the passenger carrying vessel has
  completed docking;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the tank truck's engine is either left running at all
  times or is shut off and not restarted until the passenger carrying
  vessel has completed docking;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the tank truck's driver remains with the tank truck
  while it is on board the passenger carrying vessel;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} notices prohibiting smoking, the use of an open flame
  and the use of spark-producing equipment on the passenger carrying
  vessel are placed in full view of passengers;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} fixed extinguishing equipment, including foam cannon
  units that are capable of reaching the highway tank, is installed on
  board the passenger carrying vessel;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} absorbent material that is compatible with flammable
  liquids is available on board the passenger carrying vessel;

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} a flammable gas detector is available on board the
  passenger carrying vessel; and

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} the passenger carrying vessel's master ensures that
  the tank truck is constantly monitored by a crew member while it is on
  board the passenger carrying vessel.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-253, s. 6
- [SOR/2023-155, s. 18](#1407957-1418200){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1407957-1418200.html"
  role="button"}
:::

Version](section-1.30.1-20200219.html "Link to previous version of section 1.30.1"){.PITLink}

#### [Class 1, Explosives, Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227941 .Subheading}

**[[1.31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.31 .sectionLabel}** Part 3
(Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), Part 6
(Training), Part 9 (Road) and Part 10 (Rail) do not apply to the
handling, offering for transport or transporting on a road vehicle or a
railway vehicle dangerous goods included in Class 1, Explosives, if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of each explosive in the road vehicle or
  railway vehicle that is not subject to special provision 85 or 86 is
  less than or equal to the number shown in column 6(a) of Schedule 1
  for that explosive;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of each explosive in the road vehicle or
  railway vehicle that is subject to special provision 85 or 86 is less
  than or equal to the number shown in special provision 85 or 86 for
  that explosive;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} each means of containment has displayed on it the
  class, compatibility group and UN number of the explosives contained
  inside it; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a placard is displayed in accordance with Part 4
  (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) if the explosives are included in
  Class 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 or 1.5

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in any quantity exceeding 10 kg net explosives
    quantity, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in any number of articles exceeding 1 000 for
    explosives subject to special provision 85 or 86.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 18
- SOR/2014-159, s. 7
- SOR/2014-306, s. 11
- [SOR/2023-155, s. 19](#1407959-1418203){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1407959-1418203.html"
  role="button"}
:::

#### [Class 2, Gases, or Ammonia Solutions (Class 8) in Refrigerating Machines Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227951 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2012-245, s. 10

\]
:::

**[[1.32]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.32 .sectionLabel}** Parts 3 to 10 and 17
do not apply to UN2857, REFRIGERATING MACHINES, and refrigerating
machine components containing gases included in Class 2.2 or UN2672,
AMMONIA SOLUTION, if the quantity of gas has a mass that is less than or
equal to 12 kg and the quantity of ammonia solution is less than or
equal to 12 L.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 18
- SOR/2016-95, s. 41

#### [Class 2, Gases, that May Be Identified as UN1075, LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227957 .Subheading}

- **[[1.32.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.32.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The following dangerous goods may be
  identified by the UN number UN1075 and the shipping name LIQUEFIED
  PETROLEUM GASES instead of the UN number and shipping name identified
  for them:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} UN1011, BUTANE;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} UN1012, BUTYLENE;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} UN1055, ISOBUTYLENE;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} UN1077, PROPYLENE;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} UN1969, ISOBUTANE; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} UN1978, PROPANE.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The shipping name of the dangerous goods listed in
  paragraphs (1)(a) to (f) may be shown on the shipping document, in
  parentheses, following the words "LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GASES".

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If either UN1077, PROPYLENE, or UN1978, PROPANE, is
  to be transported on a road vehicle or railway vehicle on board a
  vessel and is identified as LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GASES on the shipping
  document in accordance with subsection (1), the shipping name
  PROPYLENE or PROPANE, as appropriate, must be shown on the shipping
  document, in parentheses, following the words "LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM
  GASES".

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 18
- SOR/2012-245, s. 11(E)
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
:::

#### [Class 2, Gases, Absolute Pressure between 101.3 kPa and 280 kPa]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227970 .Subheading}

**[[1.32.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.32.2 .sectionLabel}** Gases that are at
an absolute pressure between 101.3 kPa and 280 kPa at 20°C, other than
gases included in Class 2.1 or Class 2.3, may be handled, offered for
transport or transported on a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a
vessel on a domestic voyage as Class 2.2, Non-flammable, Non-toxic gas.
In that case, the requirements of these Regulations that relate to gases
included in Class 2.2 must be complied with.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 18
- SOR/2012-245, s. 12
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
:::

#### [Class 2, Gases, in Small Means of Containment Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227974 .Subheading}

**[[1.32.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.32.3 .sectionLabel}** Part 3
(Documentation) and Part 6 (Training) do not apply to dangerous goods
that are transported in one or more small means of containment on a road
vehicle solely on land if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} UN1001, ACETYLENE, DISSOLVED,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} UN1002, AIR, COMPRESSED,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} UN1006, ARGON, COMPRESSED,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} UN1013, CARBON DIOXIDE,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} UN1060, METHYLACETYLENE AND PROPADIENE MIXTURE,
    STABILIZED,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} UN1066, NITROGEN, COMPRESSED,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} UN1072, OXYGEN, COMPRESSED, or

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} UN1978, PROPANE;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are contained in no more than
  five small means of containment;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the gross mass of the dangerous goods is less than or
  equal to 500 kg; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the labels displayed on the small means of
  containment can be seen from outside the road vehicle.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 18
- SOR/2012-245, s. 13(F)
:::

#### [Class 3, Flammable Liquids: General Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227990 .Subheading}

**[[1.33]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.33 .sectionLabel}** Part 3
(Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), Part 5 (Means of
Containment), Part 6 (Training), Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance
Plan), Part 9 (Road) and Part 10 (Rail) do not apply to the handling,
offering for transport or transporting of dangerous goods included in
Class 3, Flammable Liquids, on a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a
vessel on a domestic voyage if the dangerous goods

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} have no subsidiary class;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} are included in Packing Group III and have a flash
  point greater than 37.8°C; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} are in one or more small means of containment
  designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that
  under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will
  be no release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public
  safety.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 19
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
- [SOR/2023-155, s. 20](#1407961-1418205){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1407961-1418205.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1.33-20200219.html "Link to previous version of section 1.33"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Class 3, Flammable Liquids, Flash Point Greater Than 60°C but Less Than or Equal to 93°C]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1227997 .Subheading}

**[[1.34]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.34 .sectionLabel}** Despite section 6.1
of the Act and section 4.2 of Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) of
these Regulations, substances that have a flash point greater than 60°C
but less than or equal to 93°C may be transported on a road vehicle, on
a railway vehicle or on a vessel on a domestic voyage as Class 3,
Flammable Liquids, Packing Group III. In that case, the requirements of
these Regulations, except paragraph 7.2(1)(f) of Part 7 (Emergency
Response Assistance Plan), that relate to flammable liquids that have a
flash point less than or equal to 60°C must be complied with.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 19
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
:::

**[[1.34.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.34.1 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed,
SOR/2017-137, s. 9\]]{.Repealed}

#### [UN1202, DIESEL FUEL, or UN1203, GASOLINE, Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228002 .Subheading}

**[[1.35]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.35 .sectionLabel}** Part 3
(Documentation), the UN number requirements in sections 4.12 and 4.15.2
of Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) and Part 6 (Training) do not
apply to the offering for transport, handling or transporting on a road
vehicle of dangerous goods that are UN1202, DIESEL FUEL or UN1203,
GASOLINE, if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are in one or more means of
  containment, each of which is visible from outside the road vehicle
  and each of which has displayed on it

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the label or placard required for the dangerous
    goods by Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if a side or end of the means of containment is
    not visible from outside the road vehicle, the label or placard
    required for the dangerous goods by Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety
    Marks) on a side or end that is visible from outside the road
    vehicle;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} each means of containment is secured to the road
  vehicle so that the required label or at least one of the required
  placards displayed on it is visible from outside the road vehicle
  during transport; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the total capacity of all the means of containment is
  less than or equal to 2 000 L.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2003-273, s. 4
- SOR/2008-34, s. 19
- SOR/2017-137, s. 10
:::

#### [Class 3, Flammable Liquids, Alcoholic Beverage and Aqueous Solution of Alcohol Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228011 .Subheading}

**[[1.36]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.36 .sectionLabel}** Part 3
(Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), Part 5 (Means of
Containment), Part 6 (Training), Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance
Plan), Part 8 (Reporting Requirements), Part 9 (Road) and Part 10 (Rail)
do not apply to the handling, offering for transport or transporting on
a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a vessel on a domestic voyage of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} an alcoholic beverage if the alcoholic beverage

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} contains alcohol that is less than or equal to 24%
    by volume,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is included in Packing Group II and is in a means
    of containment with a capacity that is less than or equal to 5 L, or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} is included in Packing Group III and is in a
    means of containment with a capacity that is less than or equal to
    250 L; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} an aqueous solution of alcohol if the aqueous
  solution has a flash point greater than 23°C and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} contains alcohol that is less than or equal to 50%
    by volume and at least 50% by volume of a substance that is not
    dangerous goods, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is contained in a small means of containment.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 9
- SOR/2008-34, s. 19
- SOR/2016-95, s. 41
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
:::

**[[1.37]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.37 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed,
SOR/2008-34, s. 19\]]{.Repealed}

#### [Polyester Resin Kit Exception]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228023 .Subheading}

**[[1.38]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.38 .sectionLabel}** Part 3
(Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), Part 5 (Means of
Containment), Part 6 (Training), Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance
Plan), Part 8 (Reporting Requirements), Part 9 (Road) and Part 10 (Rail)
do not apply to the handling, offering for transport or transporting of
a polyester resin kit that consists of a substance included in Class 3,
Packing Group II or III and a substance included in Class 5.2, Type D, E
or F that does not require temperature control if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the kit is in transport on a road vehicle, a railway
  vehicle or a vessel on a domestic voyage;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the gross mass of the kit is less than or equal to
  30 kg;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of Class 3 substance in the kit is less
  than or equal to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} 1 L for Packing Group II substances, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} 5 L for Packing Group III substances; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of Class 5.2 substance in the kit is
  less than or equal to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} 125 mL for liquids, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} 500 g for solids.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 20
- SOR/2016-95, s. 41
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
:::

#### [Class 6.2, Infectious Substances, UN3373, BIOLOGICAL SUBSTANCE, CATEGORY B Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228035 .Subheading}

**[[1.39]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.39 .sectionLabel}** Parts 3 and 4, except
section 4.22.1, and Part 17 do not apply to the offering for transport,
handling or transporting of infectious substances that are included in
Category B if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} one external surface of the means of containment for
  the substances measures at least 100 mm × 100 mm;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the means of containment is in compliance with Part 5
  (Means of Containment) and has displayed on the external surface

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the mark illustrated in Part 4 (Dangerous Goods
    Safety Marks) for infectious substances included in Category B, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name, on a contrasting background,
    next to the mark in letters at least 6 mm high; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the 24-hour telephone number required under paragraph
  3.5(1)(f) is displayed next to the shipping name on the means of
  containment.

#### [Biological Products Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228045 .Subheading}

**[[1.41]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.41 .sectionLabel}** Parts 3 to 8 and 17
do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or transporting of
biological products if they

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} are prepared in accordance with the requirements set
  out under the [Food and Drugs Act](/eng/acts/F-27);

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} are in a means of containment that is designed,
  constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under
  normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no
  release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} are in a means of containment that is marked with the
  words "Biological Product" or "[Produit biologique]{.otherLang
  lang="fr"}" in black letters at least 6 mm high on a contrasting
  background.

#### [Human or Animal Specimens Believed Not to Contain Infectious Substances Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228052 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2023-206, s. 8(F)

\]
:::

- **[[1.42]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.42
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Parts 3 to 8 and 17 do not apply to
  the offering for transport, handling or transporting of human or
  animal specimens that are reasonably believed not to contain
  infectious substances.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The human or animal specimens referred to in
  subsection (1) must be in a means of containment that is marked with
  the words "Exempt Human Specimen" or "[spécimen humain
  exempté]{.otherLang lang="fr"}" or "Exempt Animal Specimen" or
  "[spécimen animal exempté]{.otherLang lang="fr"}" and that is
  designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that
  under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will
  be no release of the specimen.

**[[1.42.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.42.1 .sectionLabel}** These Regulations
do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or transport of
tissues or organs for transplant.

#### [Blood or Blood Components Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228062 .Subheading}

- **[[1.42.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.42.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Parts 3 to 8 and 17 do not apply to
  the offering for transport, handling or transporting of blood or blood
  components that are intended for transfusion or for the preparation of
  blood products and are reasonably believed not to contain infectious
  substances.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The blood or blood components referred to in
  subsection (1) must be in a means of containment that is designed,
  constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under
  normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no
  release of the blood or blood components.

#### [Medical or Clinical Waste]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228068 .Subheading}

**[[1.42.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.42.3 .sectionLabel}** Part 3, sections
4.10 to 4.12 and Parts 5 to 8 and 17 do not apply to the offering for
transport, handling or transporting of dangerous goods that are medical
waste or clinical waste if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are UN3291, (BIO) MEDICAL WASTE,
  N.O.S.;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are in a means of containment
  that is in compliance with CGSB-43.125; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the following information is displayed on the means
  of containment:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the biohazard symbol; and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the word "BIOHAZARD" or "[BIORISQUE]{.otherLang
    lang="fr"}".

#### [Class 7, Radioactive Materials, Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228077 .Subheading}

**[[1.43]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.43 .sectionLabel}** Parts 3 to 7, 9 to 12
and 17 do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or
transporting of dangerous goods included in Class 7 if the dangerous
goods

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} satisfy the conditions in the [Packaging and
  Transport of Nuclear Substances
  Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2000-208) to be transported in an
  excepted package;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} are in an excepted package; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} are accompanied by a document that includes the
  shipping name and UN number of the radioactive materials.

#### [Residue of Dangerous Goods in a Drum Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228084 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2014-152, s. 7

\]
:::

**[[1.44]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.44 .sectionLabel}** Part 2
(Classification), Part 3 (Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety
Marks), and Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance Plan) do not apply to
a residue of dangerous goods contained in a drum that is in transport on
a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a vessel on a domestic voyage,
except for dangerous goods included in Packing Group I or contained in a
drum otherwise requiring a label for Class 1, 4.3, 6.2 or 7, if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2019-101, s. 3\]]{.Repealed}

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the drum is being transported for the purpose of
  reconditioning or reuse in accordance with section 5.12 of Part 5
  (Means of Containment);

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} when more than 10 drums are on the road vehicle or on
  the railway vehicle, the road vehicle or railway vehicle has displayed
  on it the DANGER placard in accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods
  Safety Marks); and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the drums are accompanied by a document that includes
  the following information:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the primary class of each residue and the words
    "Residue Drum(s)" or "[fût(s) de résidu]{.otherLang lang="fr"}" when
    the primary class can be reasonably determined, preceded by the
    number of drums containing dangerous goods with that primary class,
    and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the words "Residue Drum(s) -- Content(s) Unknown"
    or "[fût(s) de résidu -- contenu inconnu]{.otherLang lang="fr"}" if
    there are any residues for which the primary class cannot be
    reasonably determined, preceded by the number of drums containing
    the residues.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 11
- SOR/2008-34, s. 22
- SOR/2014-152, s. 8
- SOR/2017-137, s. 15
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
- SOR/2019-101, s. 3
:::

#### [Fumigation of Means of Containment]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228096 .Subheading}

**[[1.45]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.45 .sectionLabel}** These Regulations,
except for subsection 3.5(3) of Part 3 (Documentation) and section 4.21
of Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), do not apply to a means of
containment, or the contents of a means of containment, that is being
fumigated with dangerous goods and that is in transport if the fumigant
is the only dangerous goods in transport in the means of containment.

#### [Marine Pollutants Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228098 .Subheading}

**[[1.45.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.45.1 .sectionLabel}** Part 3
(Documentation) and Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) do not apply
to substances that are classified as marine pollutants in accordance
with section 2.43 of Part 2 (Classification) if they are in transport
solely on land by road vehicle or railway vehicle. However, substances
may be identified as marine pollutants on a shipping document and the
required dangerous goods safety marks may be displayed when they are in
transport by road or railway vehicle.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 23
:::

#### [Miscellaneous Special Cases]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228102 .Subheading}

**[[1.46]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.46 .sectionLabel}** These Regulations do
not apply to the following dangerous goods:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} ammoniating fertilizer solutions with an absolute
  pressure of ammonia less than or equal to 276 kPa at 41°C;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} antimony oxides and antimony sulphides with 0.5% or
  less arsenic by mass;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} charcoal or carbons that are

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} non-activated carbon blacks of mineral origin,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} carbons made by a steam activation process, or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} activated or non-activated carbons that pass the
    self-heating test for carbon in section 33.3.1.3.3 of the Manual of
    Tests and Criteria;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} cinnabar;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} cyclohexanone peroxides with 70% or more inert
  inorganic solid, by mass;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} Di-4-chlorobenzoyl peroxide or *p*-chlorobenzoyl
  peroxide with 70% or more inert inorganic solid, by mass;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} 1,3-Di-(2-*tert*-butylperoxyisopropyl) benzene or
  1,4-Di-(2-*tert*-butylperoxyisopropyl) benzene, or mixtures of both,
  60% or more, by mass, of which consists of an inert solid, if the
  substance is in a means of containment in a total quantity less than
  or equal to 200 kg;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} dibenzoyl peroxide or benzoyl peroxide that is in a
  concentration less than 35.5%, by mass, with finely ground starch,
  calcium sulphate dihydrate or dicalcium phosphate dihydrate, or that
  is in a concentration less than 30%, by mass, with 70% or more, by
  mass, inert solid;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} dicumyl peroxide with 60% or more inert inorganic
  solid, by mass;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} ferricyanides and ferrocyanides;

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} fish-meal that is acidified and is wetted with 40% or
  more water, by mass;

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2017-253\]]{.Repealed}

- [(m)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2008-34\]]{.Repealed}

- [(n)]{.lawlabel} sodium dichloroisocyanurate dihydrate;

- [(o)]{.lawlabel} solvent extracted soya bean meal free of flammable
  solvent and containing 1.5% or less oil, by mass, and 11% or less
  moisture, by mass; or

- [(p)]{.lawlabel} wood or wood products treated with wood
  preservatives.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 24
- SOR/2017-253, s. 7
:::

#### [UN1044, FIRE EXTINGUISHERS, Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228125 .Subheading}

**[[1.47]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.47 .sectionLabel}** Subsections 5.10(1)
and (2) and Part 17 do not apply to the offering for transport, handling
or transporting of UN1044, FIRE EXTINGUISHERS, if the fire extinguishers

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} do not contain dangerous goods included in Class 2.3,
  Class 6.1 or Class 8;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} are contained in an outer means of containment;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} have a capacity less than 18 L or, if they contain
  liquefied gas, a capacity less than 0.6 L;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} have an internal pressure less than or equal to 1
  650 kPa at 21°C; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} are manufactured, tested, maintained, marked and used
  in accordance with ULC Standard S504, ULC Standard S507, ULC Standard
  S512 or ULC Standard S554.

#### [Air Ambulance Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228134 .Subheading}

**[[1.48]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.48 .sectionLabel}** These Regulations,
except for Part 8 (Reporting Requirements), do not apply to dangerous
goods required for patient care on an aircraft if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is configured as an air ambulance and is
  used only as an air ambulance;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the transport of the dangerous goods is not forbidden
  in Schedule 1, Schedule 3 or the ICAO Technical Instructions;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are under the control of a health
  care professional or a person who is trained in accordance with Part 6
  (Training);

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} dangerous goods included in Class 2, Gases, they
    are in one or more small means of containment in compliance with the
    requirements for transporting gases in Part 5 (Means of
    Containment), or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} dangerous goods not included in Class 2, Gases,
    they are in one or more small means of containment designed,
    constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under
    normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no
    accidental release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public
    safety; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the means of containment are secured to prevent
  unintended movement during transport.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 25
- SOR/2016-95, s. 41
:::

#### [Cylinder Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228145 .Subheading}

- **[[1.49]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.49
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subsection 5.1(1) and Section 5.10
  of Part 5 (Means of Containment) do not apply to the handling,
  offering for transport or transporting of dangerous goods in a
  cylinder on a road vehicle or an aircraft if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the cylinder is from or for a vessel or an
    aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the cylinder is transported solely for the purpose
    of refilling, exchanging or requalification;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the cylinder is accompanied by a shipping document
    that includes the words "Cylinder in transport for purpose of
    refilling, exchanging or requalification in compliance with section
    1.49 of the TDGR" or "[Bouteille à gaz en transport aux fins de
    remplissage, d'échange ou de requalification en conformité avec
    l'article 1.49 du RTMD]{.otherLang lang="fr"}";

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the cylinder is closed and secured so that under
    normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no
    release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a cylinder from or for a vessel that
    is a Canadian vessel as defined in section 2 of the [Canada Shipping
    Act, 2001](/eng/acts/C-10.15), the cylinder conforms, as applicable,
    to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the [Fire Detection and Extinguishing Equipment
      Regulations](/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._1422), as they read
      immediately before being repealed,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the [Life Saving Equipment
      Regulations](/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._1436),

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the [Large Fishing Vessel Inspection
      Regulations](/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._1435),

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the [Fishing Vessel Safety
      Regulations](/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._1486),

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the [Small Vessel
      Regulations](/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._1487), and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the [Vessel Fire Safety
      Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2017-14);

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a cylinder from or for a vessel that
    is a foreign vessel as defined in section 2 of the [Canada Shipping
    Act, 2001](/eng/acts/C-10.15) and that is a Safety Convention vessel
    as defined in that section, the cylinder is used for a purpose
    related to the operation or navigation of the vessel, including a
    life-saving or emergency purpose; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a cylinder from or for an aircraft,
    a flight authority, as defined in subsection 101.01(1) of the
    [Canadian Aviation Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-96-433), has
    been issued in respect of the aircraft and the cylinder serves an
    aeronautical purpose, including a life-saving or emergency purpose.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When the cylinder has been requalified or filled, the
  exemption set out in subsection (1) applies only if the cylinder was
  requalified in accordance with clause 6.5.1(b) of CSA B340 and filled
  in compliance with clause 6.5.1(c) of CSA B340.

#### [Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228164 .Subheading}

- **[[1.50]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1.50
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Sections 5.1, 5.2 and 5.5 and
  subsection 5.10(1) do not apply to the offering for transport,
  handling or transport of UN1978, PROPANE, in a cylinder on a road
  vehicle, a railway vehicle or a ship on a domestic voyage if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the cylinder is for use in a hot air balloon and is
    marked clearly and visibly, in letters at least 5 mm high, with the
    words "FOR USE IN HOT AIR BALLOONS ONLY" or "[POUR UTILISATION DANS
    LES BALLONS SEULEMENT]{.otherLang lang="fr"}";

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a flight authority, as defined in subsection
    101.01(1) of the [Canadian Aviation
    Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-96-433), has been issued in
    respect of the hot air balloon;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the cylinder is designed, constructed, filled,
    closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of
    transport, including handling, there will be no release of dangerous
    goods that could endanger public safety;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} subject to paragraph (e), the cylinder

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is manufactured, selected and used in accordance
      with CSA B340, except clause 5.3.1.4 of that standard,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is manufactured, selected and used in accordance
      with CSA B342,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} is manufactured, selected and used in
      accordance with 49 CFR and, in the case of a requalified cylinder,
      is marked with the requalification markings required by CSA B339
      or 49 CFR,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} is manufactured and selected in accordance with
      the ADR, is marked with the symbol π (Pi) in accordance with the
      TPED and is used in accordance with clauses 4.1.1.2, 4.1.3, 4.1.4,
      4.2, 4.3.1, 4.3.2, 4.3.7, 4.3.8, 4.3.9, 5.1.1, 5.1.2, 5.1.3(b) to
      (e), 5.1.8 and 5.3.1.1 of CSA B340, or

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} was manufactured before January 1, 2017, and is
      used in accordance with clauses 4.1.1.2, 4.1.3, 4.1.4, 4.2, 4.3.1,
      4.3.2, 4.3.7, 4.3.8, 4.3.9, 5.1.1, 5.1.2, 5.1.3(b) to (e), 5.1.8
      and 5.3.1.1 of CSA B340; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the liquid phase of the propane is less than or
    equal to 85% of the capacity of the cylinder at 15°C.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subparagraph (1)(d)(iv), ADR
  means the European Agreement concerning the International Carriage of
  Dangerous Goods by Road, published by the United Nations, as amended
  from time to time and TPED means the Transportable Pressure Equipment
  Directive, Directive 2010/35/EU, June 16, 2010, published by the
  Council of the European Union.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), a cylinder referred to in
  subparagraph (1)(d)(iv) or (v) must be requalified within

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 10 years after its date of manufacture; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 10 years after its most recent requalification date
    as marked on the cylinder.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A cylinder that must be requalified on or before
  January 1, 2018 may be requalified within a 12-month grace period that
  starts on the day on which this section comes into force.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} When it is requalified, a cylinder referred to in
  subparagraph (1)(d)(iv) or (v) must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} be requalified with a proof pressure retest and an
    internal and external visual inspection in accordance with clause 24
    of CSA B339 by a facility that holds a valid certificate of
    registration referred to in clause 25.3 of CSA B339; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} be subjected to a periodic inspection and test in
    accordance with clause 19 of CSA B341.

::: HistoricalNote

## [PART 2]{.HLabel1}[Classification]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1228187 .Part}

### [Determining When Substances Are Dangerous Goods]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228188 .Subheading}

**[[2.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.1 .sectionLabel}** A substance is
dangerous goods when

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} it is listed by name in Schedule 1 and is in any
  form, state or concentration that meets the criteria in this Part for
  inclusion in at least one of the nine classes of dangerous goods; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is not listed by name in Schedule 1 but meets the
  criteria in this Part for inclusion in at least one of the nine
  classes of dangerous goods.

::: HistoricalNote

### [Responsibility for Classification]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228192 .Subheading}

- **[[2.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Before allowing a carrier to take
  possession of dangerous goods for transport, the consignor must
  determine the classification of the dangerous goods in accordance with
  this Part.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When importing dangerous goods into Canada, the
  consignor must ensure that they have the correct classification before
  they are transported in Canada.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A consignor must use the following classifications:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for substances included in Class 1, Explosives, the
    classification determined in accordance with the [Explosives
    Act](/eng/acts/E-17); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for radioactive materials, the classification
    determined in accordance with the [Packaging and Transport of
    Nuclear Substances Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2000-208).

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2014-152\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2014-152\]]{.Repealed}

- [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} For substances included in Class 6.2, Infectious
  Substances, a consignor may use a classification determined by the
  Public Health Agency of Canada or the Canadian Food Inspection Agency.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A consignor may use the appropriate classification in
  the ICAO Technical Instructions, the IMDG Code or the UN
  Recommendations to transport dangerous goods within Canada by a road
  vehicle, a railway vehicle or a vessel on a domestic voyage if these
  Regulations or the document from which the classification is taken
  does not forbid their transport.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} If an error in classification is noticed or if there
  are reasonable grounds to suspect an error in classification, the
  consignor must not allow a carrier to take possession of the dangerous
  goods for transport until the classification has been verified or
  corrected.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} A carrier who notices an error in classification or
  has reasonable grounds to suspect an error in classification while the
  dangerous goods are in transport must advise the consignor and must
  stop transporting the dangerous goods until the consignor verifies or
  corrects the classification. The consignor must immediately verify or
  correct the classification and ensure that the carrier is provided
  with the verified or corrected classification.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 28
- SOR/2014-152, s. 11
- SOR/2014-306, s. 17
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
:::

### [Proof of Classification]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228207 .Subheading}

- **[[2.2.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.2.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A consignor who allows a carrier to
  take possession of dangerous goods for transport or who imports
  dangerous goods into Canada must, during a five-year period that
  begins on the date that appears on the shipping document, make a proof
  of classification available to the Minister on reasonable notice given
  by the Minister.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, a proof of
  classification is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a test report;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a lab report; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a document that explains how the dangerous goods
    were classified.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A proof of classification must include the following
  information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the dangerous goods were
    classified;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the technical name of the dangerous
    goods;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the classification of the dangerous goods; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the classification method used under
    this Part or under Chapter 2 of the UN Recommendations.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-152, s. 12
:::

### [Classifying Substances That Are Listed by Name in Schedule 1]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228221 .Subheading}

**[[2.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.3 .sectionLabel}** If a name of dangerous
goods is shown as a shipping name in column 2 of Schedule 1, that name
must be used as the shipping name. That shipping name and the
corresponding data for that shipping name in columns 1, 3 and 4 of
Schedule 1 must be used as the classification of the dangerous goods.

### [Classifying Substances That Are Included in Only One Class and One Packing Group]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228223 .Subheading}

**[[2.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.4 .sectionLabel}** If, in accordance with
the criteria and tests in this Part, a substance is included in only one
class and one packing group, the substance is dangerous goods and the
shipping name in column 2 of Schedule 1 that most precisely describes
the dangerous goods and that is most consistent with the class and the
packing group determined by the criteria and tests must be selected as
the shipping name. That shipping name and the corresponding data for
that shipping name in columns 1, 3 and 4 of Schedule 1 must be used as
the classification of the dangerous goods.

### [Classifying Substances That Are Included in More Than One Class or Packing Group]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228225 .Subheading}

**[[2.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.5 .sectionLabel}** If, in accordance with
the criteria and tests in this Part, a substance meets the criteria for
inclusion in more than one class or packing group, the substance is
dangerous goods and its classification is determined in the following
manner:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the classes in which the dangerous goods are included
  are ranked in order of precedence in accordance with section 2.8 to
  determine the primary class and the potential subsidiary class or
  classes;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the potential packing group is the one with the
  lowest roman numeral;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name in column 2 of Schedule 1 that most
  precisely describes the dangerous goods and for which the
  corresponding data in columns 1, 3 and 4 are the most consistent with
  the primary class, the potential subsidiary class or classes and the
  potential packing group is selected; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name and the corresponding data in
  columns 1, 3 and 4 of Schedule 1 are used as the classification of the
  dangerous goods.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 29(E)
:::

### [Descriptive Text Following a Shipping Name]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228233 .Subheading}

**[[2.5.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.5.1 .sectionLabel}** When applying
section 2.4 or 2.5, the descriptive text written in lower case letters
following a shipping name must be used in determining the shipping name
that most precisely describes the dangerous goods.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 30
:::

### [Classifying a Mixture or Solution]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228237 .Subheading}

**[[2.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.6 .sectionLabel}** A mixture or solution
of substances that are not dangerous goods and one substance that is
dangerous goods and that is listed by name in Schedule 1 has the
classification shown for the dangerous goods in that Schedule if the
mixture or solution is still dangerous goods in accordance with
paragraph 2.1(a) and the mixture or solution is not identified by a
shipping name in Schedule 1. However, if the classification for the
dangerous goods does not precisely describe the mixture or solution but
the mixture or solution meets the criteria in this Part for inclusion in
at least one of the nine classes of dangerous goods, then sections 2.4
and 2.5 must be used to determine its classification.

::: HistoricalNote

  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1408361-1418490.html"
  role="button"}
:::

### [Marine Pollutants]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228239 .Subheading}

- **[[2.7]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.7 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  substance is a marine pollutant if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the letter "P" (marine pollutant) is set out in
    column 4 of Schedule 3 for the substance; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the substance meets the criteria for classification
    as a marine pollutant in accordance with section 2.9.3 or chapter
    2.10 of the IMDG Code.

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2014-306, s. 18\]]{.Repealed}

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2014-306, s. 18\]]{.Repealed}

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2014-306, s. 18\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-306, s. 18
:::

### [Precedence of Classes]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228249 .Subheading}

- **[[2.8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.8 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When
  dangerous goods meet the criteria for inclusion in more than one class
  but meet the criteria for inclusion in only one of the following
  classes, that one class is the primary class. The classes are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Class 1, Explosives, except for the following
    dangerous goods for which Class 1 is a subsidiary class:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} UN3101, ORGANIC PEROXIDE TYPE B, LIQUID,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} UN3102, ORGANIC PEROXIDE TYPE B, SOLID,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} UN3111, ORGANIC PEROXIDE TYPE B, LIQUID,
      TEMPERATURE CONTROLLED,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} UN3112, ORGANIC PEROXIDE TYPE B, SOLID,
      TEMPERATURE CONTROLLED,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} UN3221, SELF-REACTIVE LIQUID TYPE B,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} UN3222, SELF-REACTIVE SOLID TYPE B,

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} UN3231, SELF-REACTIVE LIQUID TYPE B,
      TEMPERATURE CONTROLLED, and

    - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} UN3232, SELF-REACTIVE SOLID TYPE B,
      TEMPERATURE CONTROLLED;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Class 2, Gases, and within this class, Class 2.3,
    Toxic Gases, takes precedence over Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, and
    Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, takes precedence over Class 2.2,
    Non-flammable and Non-toxic Gases;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Class 4.1, Flammable Solids, desensitized
    explosives included in Packing Group I or self-reactive substances;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} Class 4.2, Substances Liable to Spontaneous
    Combustion, pyrophoric solids or liquids included in Packing Group
    I;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} Class 6.1, Toxic Substances, that are included in
    Packing Group I, due to inhalation toxicity;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} Class 6.2, Infectious Substances; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} Class 7, Radioactive Materials.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite paragraph (1)(f), Class 8 is the primary
  class when a substance meets the criteria for inclusion in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Class 8, Corrosives;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group I due to inhalation toxicity of dusts
    or mists; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group III due to oral or dermal toxicity.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A consignor must determine the order of precedence
  among classes that are not listed in subsection (1) in accordance with
  the following table, except that Class 6.1 takes precedence if a
  substance is a pesticide under the Pesticide Act and is included in
  Class 6.1, Packing Group III, and in Class 3, Packing Group III.

### [Class 1, Explosives]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228288 .Subheading}

#### [General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228289 .Subheading}

**[[2.9]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.9 .sectionLabel}** Substances are included
in Class 1, Explosives, if they are

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} capable, by chemical reaction, of producing gas at a
  temperature, pressure and speed that would damage the surroundings; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} designed to produce an explosive or pyrotechnic
  effect by heat, light, sound, gas or smoke or a combination of those
  means as a result of non-detonative, self-sustaining exothermic
  chemical reactions.

#### [Divisions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228293 .Subheading}

**[[2.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.10 .sectionLabel}** Class 1, Explosives,
has six divisions:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} Class 1.1, mass explosion hazard;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} Class 1.2, projection hazard but not a mass explosion
  hazard;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} Class 1.3, fire hazard and either a minor blast
  hazard or a minor projection hazard or both but not a mass explosion
  hazard;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} Class 1.4, no significant hazard beyond the package
  in the event of ignition or initiation during transport;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} Class 1.5, very insensitive substances with a mass
  explosion hazard; and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} Class 1.6, extremely insensitive articles with no
  mass explosion hazard.

#### [Compatibility Groups]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228301 .Subheading}

**[[2.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.11 .sectionLabel}** Explosives are
divided into 13 compatibility groups as described in Appendix 2,
Description of Compatibility Groups, Class 1, Explosives, to this Part.

#### [Packing Groups]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228303 .Subheading}

**[[2.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.12 .sectionLabel}** Explosives are
included in Packing Group II.

### [Class 2, Gases]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228305 .Subheading}

#### [General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228306 .Subheading}

**[[2.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.13 .sectionLabel}** A substance is
included in Class 2, Gases, if it is

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a gas included in one of the three divisions set out
  in section 2.14;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a mixture of gases;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a mixture of one or more gases with one or more
  vapours of substances included in other classes;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} an article charged with a gas;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} tellurium hexafluoride; or

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} an aerosol.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 31
:::

#### [Divisions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228316 .Subheading}

**[[2.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.14 .sectionLabel}** Class 2, Gases, has
three divisions:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, which consists of gases
  that, at 20°C and an absolute pressure of 101.3 kPa,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} are ignitable when in a mixture of 13% or less by
    volume with air, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} have a flammability range with air of at least 12
    percentage points determined in accordance with tests or
    calculations in ISO 10156;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} Class 2.2, Non-flammable and Non-toxic Gases, which
  consists of gases that are transported at an absolute pressure greater
  than or equal to 280 kPa at 20°C, or as refrigerated liquids, and that
  are not included in Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, or Class 2.3, Toxic
  Gases; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} Class 2.3, Toxic Gases, which consists of gases that

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} are known to be toxic or corrosive to humans
    according to CGA P-20, ISO Standard 10298 or other documentary
    evidence published in technical journals or government publications,
    or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} have an LC~50~ value less than or equal to
    5 000 mL/m^3^.

#### [Aerosols]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228325 .Subheading}

- **[[2.14.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.14.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Dangerous goods contained in an
  aerosol container must be transported under UN1950, AEROSOLS.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The dangerous goods are included

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, if the dangerous
    goods contain at least 85% by mass of flammable components and the
    chemical heat of combustion is greater than or equal to 30 kJ/g; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in Class 2.2, Non-flammable and Non-toxic Gases, if
    the dangerous goods contain not more than 1% by mass of flammable
    components and the heat of combustion is less than 20 kJ/g.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The dangerous goods must be classified in accordance
  with section 31 of Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The dangerous goods must not contain gases included
  in Class 2.3, Toxic Gases.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The dangerous goods must have a subsidiary class of
  6.1, Toxic Substances, or Class 8, Corrosive Substances, if the
  dangerous goods -- other than the propellant to be ejected from the
  aerosol container -- are included in Class 6.1, Toxic Substances,
  Packing Groups II or III, or Class 8, Corrosive Substances, Packing
  Groups II or III.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The dangerous goods are forbidden for transport when
  they are included in Packing Group I for toxicity or corrosiveness.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-306, s. 19
:::

#### [Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228337 .Subheading}

- **[[2.14.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.14.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} These Regulations, except for Part 1
  (Coming into Force, Repeal, Interpretation, General Provisions and
  Special Cases) and Part 2 (Classification) do not apply to gases
  included in Class 2.2, Non-flammable and Non-toxic Gases that are
  contained

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in foodstuffs, including carbonated beverages other
    than UN1950;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in balls intended for use in sports;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in tires; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in light bulbs.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The exemption set out in paragraph (1)(d) applies
  only if the light bulbs are packaged so that any pieces of a ruptured
  bulb are contained by the packaging.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-306, s. 19
:::

#### [Packing Groups]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228347 .Subheading}

**[[2.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.15 .sectionLabel}** There are no packing
groups for Class 2, Gases.

#### [Determination of LC~50~]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228349 .Subheading}

**[[2.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.16 .sectionLabel}** LC~50~ values for a
single or pure gas or for a mixture of gases must be determined

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} by using LC~50~ values published in CGA P-20, ISO
  Standard 10298, technical journals or government publications;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with paragraphs 2.2.3(b) and (c) of
  Chapter 2.2 of the UN Recommendations; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} for a mixture of gases, in accordance with section
  2.17.

#### [Determination of LC~50~ of a Mixture of Gases]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228354 .Subheading}

**[[2.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.17 .sectionLabel}** To determine the
LC~50~ of a mixture of gases when the LC~50~ of each of the gases is
known, use 5 000 mL/m^3^ as the toxic limit and,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the mixture contains only one gas with an LC~50~
  less than or equal to the toxic limit (called "Gas A"), use the
  following calculation:

  LC~50~ of the mixture = (LC~50~ of Gas A) ÷ (fraction by volume of Gas
  A in the mixture)

or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the mixture contains more than one gas with an
  LC~50~ less than or equal to the toxic limit (called "Gas A", "Gas B",
  etc.),

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} determine the contributing number (CN) of each of
    the gases with an LC~50~ less than or equal to the toxic limit using
    the formula

    ::: {#1228361 .Subparagraph}
    CN Gas A = (LC~50~ of Gas A) ÷ (fraction by volume of Gas A in the
    mixture)
    :::

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} combine the contributing numbers (CN) of each gas
    with an LC~50~ less than or equal to the toxic limit using the
    formula

    ::: {#1228364 .Subparagraph}
    T = 1 ÷ (CN Gas A) + 1 ÷ (CN Gas B) + (as needed)
    :::

  and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} obtain the LC~50~ of the mixture by dividing 1 by
    the number T (LC~50~ of the mixture = 1 / T).

### [Class 3, Flammable Liquids]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228368 .Subheading}

#### [General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228369 .Subheading}

- **[[2.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.18
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Substances that are liquids or
  liquids containing solids in solution or suspension are included in
  Class 3, Flammable Liquids, if they

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} have a flash point less than or equal to 60ºC using
    the closed-cup test method referred to in Chapter 2.3 of the UN
    Recommendations; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} are intended or expected to be at a temperature
    that is greater than or equal to their flash point at any time while
    the substances are in transport.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite paragraph (1)(a), liquids that have a flash
  point greater than 35°C are not included in Class 3, Flammable
  Liquids, if they

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} do not sustain combustion, as determined in
    accordance with the sustained combustibility test referred to in
    section 2.3.1.3 of Chapter 2.3 of the UN Recommendations;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} have a fire point greater than 100°C, as determined
    in accordance with ISO 2592; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} are water-miscible solutions with a water content
    greater than 90% by mass.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 32
:::

#### [Packing Groups]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228380 .Subheading}

- **[[2.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.19
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Flammable liquids included in
  Class 3, Flammable Liquids, are included in one of the following
  packing groups:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group I, if they have an initial boiling
    point of 35°C or less at an absolute pressure of 101.3 kPa and any
    flash point;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group II, if they have an initial boiling
    point greater than 35°C at an absolute pressure of 101.3 kPa and a
    flash point less than 23°C; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group III, if the criteria for inclusion in
    Packing Group I or II are not met.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), for dangerous goods included
  in Class 3, Flammable Liquids,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} when the packing group is unknown, the consignor
    may include the dangerous goods in Packing Group I; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} when the packing group is reasonably believed or is
    known to be Packing Group II or III, the consignor may include the
    dangerous goods in Packing Group II but, if the substance has the
    same characteristics as UN1203, GASOLINE, it may also be transported
    as Packing Group II.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite paragraph (1)(b), a viscous flammable liquid
  that has a flash point less than 23°C may be included in Packing Group
  III if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the liquid or any separated solvent does not meet
    the criteria for inclusion in Class 6.1 or Class 8;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} less than 3% of the clear solvent layer separates
    when the solvent separation test set out in subsection 32.5.1 of
    Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria is carried out;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the viscosity and flash-point of the liquid are in
    accordance with the table to this subsection; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the viscosity test is carried out in accordance
    with the procedure set out in subsection 32.4 of Part III of the
    Manual of Tests and Criteria or the procedure set out in ISO 2431.
