- [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} If a liquid referred to in subsection (3) is a
  non-Newtonian substance or a flow cup method of viscosity
  determination is unsuitable, a variable shear-rate viscometer must be
  used to determine the dynamic viscosity coefficient of the liquid, at
  23°C, at a number of shear rates. The values obtained must be plotted
  against shear rate and then extrapolated to zero shear rate. The
  dynamic viscosity value thus obtained, divided by the density, gives
  the apparent kinematic viscosity at near-zero shear rate.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 33(F)
- SOR/2017-137, s. 19
:::

### [Class 4, Flammable Solids; Substances Liable to Spontaneous Combustion; Substances That on Contact with Water Emit Flammable Gases (Water-reactive Substances)]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228403 .Subheading}

#### [General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228404 .Subheading}

**[[2.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.20 .sectionLabel}** Substances are
included in Class 4 if they are flammable solids, substances liable to
spontaneous combustion or substances that on contact with water emit
flammable gases (water-reactive substances) and meet the criteria for
inclusion in one of the divisions and packing groups of Class 4.

#### [Divisions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228406 .Subheading}

- **[[2.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.21
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Class 4 has three divisions:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Class 4.1, Flammable Solids, which consists of
    substances that are

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} readily combustible, as determined in accordance
      with section 2.4.2.2 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} under normal conditions of transport, liable to
      cause fire through friction,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} solid desensitized explosives, which are solid
      explosives desensitized through wetting with water or alcohols or
      diluted with other substances to form a homogeneous solid mixture
      to suppress their explosive properties so that they are not
      included in Class 1, Explosives,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} self-reactive substances that are liable to
      undergo a strongly exothermic decomposition even without the
      participation of oxygen (air), as determined in accordance with
      section 2.4.2.3 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations, but
      Class 4.1 does not include substances that have

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} a primary class of Class 1, Explosives,
        Class 5.1, Oxidizing Substances, or Class 5.2, Organic
        Peroxides,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} a heat of decomposition less than 300 J/g, or

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} a self-accelerating decomposition temperature
        (SADT) that is greater than 75°C for a 50 kg means of
        containment, as determined in accordance with section 2.4.2.3.4
        of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations,

    - [(iv.1)]{.lawlabel} polymerizing substances that, without
      stabilization, are liable to undergo a strongly exothermic
      reaction resulting in the formation of larger molecules or
      resulting in the formation of polymers under conditions normally
      encountered in transport,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} identified by one of the following UN numbers:
      UN2956, UN3241, UN3242 or UN3251, or

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} are in the list of currently assigned
      self-reactive substances in section 2.4.2.3.2.3 of Chapter 2.4 of
      the UN Recommendations;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Class 4.2, Substances Liable to Spontaneous
    Combustion, which consists of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} pyrophoric substances that spontaneously ignite
      within 5 minutes after coming into contact with air, as determined
      in accordance with section 2.4.3.2 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN
      Recommendations, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} self-heating substances that, when in large
      amounts (kilograms), spontaneously ignite on contact with air
      after long periods (hours or days), as determined in accordance
      with section 2.4.3.2 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Class 4.3, Water-reactive Substances, which
    consists of substances that, in tests performed in accordance with
    section 2.4.4.2 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations, emit a
    flammable gas at a rate greater than 1 L/kg of substance per hour or
    spontaneously ignite at any step in the test procedure.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subparagraph (1)(a)(iv.1), a
  substance is considered to be a polymerizing substance of Class 4.1 if
  it

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has a self-accelerating polymerization temperature
    (SAPT) that is less than or equal to 75°C under the conditions in
    which the substance or mixture is to be transported, with or without
    chemical stabilization as offered for transport, and in the means of
    containment in which the substance or mixture is to be transported;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} exhibits a heat of reaction of more than 300 J/g;
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} does not meet any other criteria for inclusion in
    Classes 1 to 8.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-137, s. 20
:::

#### [Polymerizing Substances]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228430 .Subheading}

**[[2.21.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.21.1 .sectionLabel}** A person must not
offer for transport, handle or transport the following polymerizing
substances unless they are stabilized by temperature control:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} polymerizing substance that is in a small means of
  containment prescribed by TP 14850 or Chapter 6.1 of the UN
  Recommendations or in an intermediate bulk container (IBC) and whose
  self-accelerating polymerization temperature (SAPT) is 50°C or less in
  the small means of containment or IBC; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a polymerizing substance that is in a large means of
  containment that is not an IBC and whose SAPT is 45°C or less in the
  large means of containment.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-137, s. 21
:::

#### [Packing Groups]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228436 .Subheading}

- **[[2.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.22
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Substances included in Class 4.1,
  Flammable Solids, are included in one of the following packing groups:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group I, if the substances meet the
    criterion in subparagraph 2.21(1)(a)(iii), except that substances
    that have one of the following UN numbers are included in Packing
    Group II: UN2555, UN2556, UN2557, UN2907, UN3270, UN3319 or UN3344;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group II, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the substances meet the criteria for inclusion in
      Class 4.1 in subparagraph 2.21(1)(a)(iv) or (v), except that
      substances that have one of the following UN numbers are included
      in Packing Group III: UN2956, UN3241 or UN3251,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in tests referred to in section 33.2.1 of Part
      III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria for readily combustible
      solids, excluding metal powders, the burning time of the
      substances is less than 45 seconds and the flame passes the wetted
      zone, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in tests referred to in section 33.2.1 of Part
      III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria, for readily combustible
      solids that are powders of metals or metal alloys, the zone of
      reaction of the substances spreads over the whole length of the
      sample in 5 minutes or less; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group III, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in tests referred to in section 33.2.1 of Part
      III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria, for readily combustible
      solids, excluding metal powders, the burning time of the
      substances is less than 45 seconds and the wetted zone stops the
      flame propagation for at least 4 minutes,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in tests referred to in section 33.2.1 of Part
      III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria, for readily combustible
      solids that are powders of metals or metal alloys, the zone of
      reaction of the substances spreads over the whole length of the
      sample in more than 5 minutes but not more than 10 minutes, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the substances are solids that are liable to
      cause fire through friction.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Substances included in Class 4.2, Substances Liable
  to Spontaneous Combustion, are included in one of the following
  packing groups:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group I, if the substances are pyrophoric
    solids or liquids;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group II, if the substances are
    self-heating substances that give a positive result, as determined
    in accordance with section 2.4.3.2 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN
    Recommendations using a 25 mm sample cube at 140°C; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group III for all other substances.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Substances included in Class 4.3, Water-reactive
  Substances, are included in one of the following packing groups:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group I, if the substances

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} react vigorously with water at ambient
      temperatures and demonstrate a tendency for the gas produced to
      ignite spontaneously, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} react readily with water at ambient temperatures
      so that the rate of evolution of flammable gas is greater than or
      equal to 10 L/kg of substance over any one minute;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group II, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the substances react readily with water at
      ambient temperatures so that the rate of evolution of flammable
      gas is greater than or equal to 20 L/kg of substance per hour, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I
      are not met; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group III, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the substances react slowly with water at ambient
      temperatures so that the rate of evolution of flammable gas is
      greater than or equal to 1 L/kg of substance per hour, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I or
      II are not met.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-137, s. 22
:::

### [Class 5, Oxidizing Substances and Organic Peroxides]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228464 .Subheading}

#### [General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228465 .Subheading}

**[[2.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.23 .sectionLabel}** Substances are
included in Class 5 if they are oxidizing substances or organic
peroxides and meet the criteria for inclusion in one of the divisions of
Class 5.

#### [Divisions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228467 .Subheading}

**[[2.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.24 .sectionLabel}** Class 5 has two
divisions:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} Class 5.1, Oxidizing Substances, which consists of
  substances that yield oxygen thereby causing or contributing to the
  combustion of other material, as determined in accordance with section
  2.5.2 of Chapter 2.5 of the UN Recommendations; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides, which consists of
  substances that

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} are thermally unstable organic compounds that
    contain oxygen in the bivalent "-O-O-" structure, as determined in
    accordance with section 2.5.3 of Chapter 2.5 of the UN
    Recommendations,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} are liable to undergo exothermic self-accelerating
    decomposition,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} have one or more of the following
    characteristics:

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} they are liable to explosive decomposition,

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} they burn rapidly,

    - [(C)]{.lawlabel} they are sensitive to impact or friction,

    - [(D)]{.lawlabel} they react dangerously with other substances, or

    - [(E)]{.lawlabel} they cause damage to the eyes, or

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} are in the list of currently assigned organic
    peroxides in section 2.5.3.2.4 of Chapter 2.5 of the UN
    Recommendations.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-137, s. 23(E)
:::

#### [Packing Groups]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228482 .Subheading}

- **[[2.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.25
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The packing group for a substance
  that is included in Class 5.1, Oxidizing Substances, must be
  determined by using a test sample of the substance that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a solid, is prepared in accordance
    with section 2.5.2.2 of Chapter 2.5 of the UN Recommendations; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a liquid, is prepared in accordance
    with section 2.5.2.3 of Chapter 2.5 of the UN Recommendations.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a solid substance included in
  Class 5.1, Oxidizing Substances, the test procedure set out in either
  subsection 34.4.1 (test O.1) or subsection 34.4.3 (test O.3) of Part
  III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria must be carried out on the
  test sample. The substance is included in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group I, if the test sample exhibits an
    average burning time that is

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} less than the mean burning time of a 3:2
      potassium bromate/cellulose mixture by mass when test O.1 is used,
      or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} greater than the mean burning rate of a 3:1
      calcium peroxide/cellulose mixture by mass when test O.3 is used;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group II, if the criteria for Packing Group
    I are not met and the test sample exhibits an average burning time
    that is

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} less than or equal to the mean burning time of a
      2:3 potassium bromate/cellulose mixture by mass, when test O.1 is
      used, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} equal to or greater than the mean burning rate
      of a 1:1 calcium peroxide/cellulose mixture by mass, when test O.3
      is used; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group III, if the criteria for Packing
    Groups I and II are not met and the test sample exhibits an average
    burning time that is

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} less than or equal to the mean burning time of a
      3:7 potassium bromate/cellulose mixture by mass, when test O.1 is
      used, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} equal to or greater than the mean burning rate
      of a 1:2 calcium peroxide/cellulose mixture by mass, when test O.3
      is used.

- [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a liquid substance included in
  Class 5.1, Oxidizing Substances, the test procedure set out in
  sub-section 34.4.2 (test O.2) of Part III of the Manual of Tests and
  Criteria must be carried out on the test sample. The substance is
  included in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group I, if the test sample in a 1:1
    mixture by mass of substance and cellulose spontaneously ignites or
    the mean pressure rise time is less than that of a 1:1 mixture by
    mass of 50% perchloric acid and cellulose;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group II, if the mean pressure rise time is
    less than or equal to the mean pressure rise time of a 1:1 mixture
    by mass of 40% aqueous sodium chlorate solution and cellulose and
    the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I are not met; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group III, if the mean pressure rise time
    is less than or equal to the mean pressure rise time of a 1:1
    mixture by mass of 65% aqueous nitric acid solution and cellulose
    and the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I or II are not met.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides, are included in Packing
  Group II.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The type, B to F, of organic peroxides must be
  determined in accordance with section 2.5.3.3 of Chapter 2.5 of the UN
  Recommendations.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-137, s. 24
:::

### [Class 6, Toxic and Infectious Substances]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228505 .Subheading}

#### [General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228506 .Subheading}

**[[2.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.26 .sectionLabel}** Substances are
included in Class 6 if they are

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} liable to cause death or serious injury or to harm
  human health if swallowed or inhaled or if they come into contact with
  human skin; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} infectious substances.

#### [Divisions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228510 .Subheading}

**[[2.27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.27 .sectionLabel}** Class 6 has two
divisions:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} Class 6.1, Toxic Substances, which consists of
  substances that are liable to cause death or serious injury or to harm
  human health if swallowed or inhaled or if they come into contact with
  human skin; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} Class 6.2, Infectious Substances, which consists of
  infectious substances.

#### [Criteria for Inclusion in Class 6.1, Toxic Substances]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228514 .Subheading}

**[[2.28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.28 .sectionLabel}** A substance is
included in Class 6.1

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} due to oral toxicity if its LD~50~ (oral) is less
  than or equal to 300 mg/kg;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} due to dermal toxicity if its LD~50~ (dermal) is less
  than or equal to 1 000 mg/kg; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} due to inhalation toxicity

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} by dust or mist if dust or mist is likely to be
    produced in a transport accident and its LC~50~ (inhalation) is less
    than or equal to 4 mg/L, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} by vapour if its LC~50~ (inhalation) is less than
    or equal to 5 000 mL/m^3^.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 34
:::

#### [Packing Groups]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228523 .Subheading}

- **[[2.29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.29
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When a substance is known to be
  included in Class 6.1 and that knowledge is based on documentary
  evidence published in technical journals or government publications
  and testing is not done to determine the packing group, the substance
  must be included in Packing Group I.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Substances that are included in Class 6.1 due to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} oral toxicity are included in one of the following
    packing groups:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group I, if the LD~50~ (oral) is less
      than or equal to 5 mg/kg,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group II, if the LD~50~ (oral) is
      greater than 5 mg/kg but less than or equal to 50 mg/kg, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group III, if the LD~50~ (oral) is
      greater than 50 mg/kg but less than or equal to 300 mg/kg;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} dermal toxicity are included in one of the
    following packing groups:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group I if the LD~50~ (dermal) is less
      than or equal to 50 mg/kg,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group II if the LD~50~ (dermal) is
      greater than 50 mg/kg but less than or equal to 200 mg/kg, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group III if the LD~50~ (dermal) is
      greater than 200 mg/kg but less than or equal to 1 000 mg/kg;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} inhalation toxicity by dust or mist are included in
    one of the following packing groups:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group I if the LC~50~ (inhalation) is
      less than or equal to 0.2 mg/L,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group II if the LC~50~ (inhalation) is
      greater than 0.2 mg/L but less than or equal to 2 mg/L, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group III if the LC~50~ (inhalation) is
      greater than 2 mg/L but less than or equal to 4 mg/L; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} inhalation toxicity by vapour are included in one
    of the following packing groups, where "V" is the saturated vapour
    concentration in millilitres per cubic metre of air at 20°C and at
    101.3 kPa:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group I, if

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} V is greater than or equal to 10 multiplied by
        the LC~50~, and

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the LC~50~ is less than or equal to
        1 000 mL/m^3^,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group II, if

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} V is greater than or equal to the LC~50~,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the LC~50~ is less than or equal to
        3 000 mL/m^3^, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} the criteria for Packing Group I are not met,
        or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group III, if

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} V is greater than or equal to 0.2 multiplied by
        the LC~50~,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the LC~50~ is less than or equal to
        5 000 mL/m^3^, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I
        or II are not met.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 35
- SOR/2012-245, s. 16(E)
:::

#### [Determination of LD~50~ (oral or dermal)]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228553 .Subheading}

**[[2.30]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.30 .sectionLabel}** LD~50~ (oral or
dermal) values for solid or liquid substances or for a mixture of solid
or liquid substances must be determined

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} by using the LD~50~ values published in technical
  journals or in government publications;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with section 2.6.2.3 of Chapter 2.6 of
  the UN Recommendations; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} for a mixture of solid or liquid substances, in
  accordance with section 2.31.

#### [Determination of LD~50~ (oral or dermal) of a Mixture of Substances]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228558 .Subheading}

**[[2.31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.31 .sectionLabel}** To determine the
LD~50~ of a mixture of solid or liquid substances when the LD~50~ of
each of the substances is known, use 1 000 mg/kg as the toxic limit and

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the mixture contains only one substance with an
  LD~50~ less than or equal to the toxic limit (called "Substance A"),
  use the following calculation:

  LD~50~ of the mixture = (LD~50~ of Substance A) ÷ (fraction by mass of
  Substance A in the mixture)

or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the mixture contains more than one substance with
  an LD~50~ less than or equal to the toxic limit (called "Substance A",
  "Substance B", etc.),

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} determine the lowest LD~50~ of all substances,
    assign that LD~50~ to all substances whose actual LD~50~ is less
    than or equal to the toxic limit, then use the calculation in
    paragraph (a) using that assigned LD~50~ and taking as the mass of
    Substance A in the formula the total of the masses of all substances
    whose actual LD~50~ is less than or equal to the toxic limit, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} use the following calculations:

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} determine the contributing number (CN) of each of
      the substances with an LD~50~ less than or equal to the toxic
      limit using the formula

      CN for Substance A= (LD~50~ of Substance A) ÷ (fraction by mass of
      Substance A in the mixture)

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} combine the contributing numbers (CN) of each
      substance with an LD~50~ less than or equal to the toxic limit as

      ::: {#1228569 .Clause}
      T = 1 ÷ (CN Substance A) + 1 ÷ (CN Substance B) + (as needed)
      :::

    and

    - [(C)]{.lawlabel} obtain the LD~50~ of the mixture by dividing 1 by
      the number T (LD~50~ of the mixture = 1 / T).

#### [Determination of LC~50~ (dust, mist or vapour)]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228573 .Subheading}

**[[2.32]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.32 .sectionLabel}** LC~50~ values for a
substance in the form of a dust, mist or vapour or for a mixture of
substances in the form of a dust, mist or vapour must be determined

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} by using the LC~50~ values published in technical
  journals or in government publications;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with sections 2.6.2.2.4.2 to
  2.6.2.2.4.7 of Chapter 2.6 of the UN Recommendations; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} for a mixture of substances, in accordance with
  section 2.33.

#### [Determination of LC~50~ (dust, mist or vapour) of a Mixture of Substances]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228578 .Subheading}

**[[2.33]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.33 .sectionLabel}** To determine the
LC~50~ of a mixture of substances that are in the form of a dust, mist
or vapour, when the LC~50~ of each of the substances is known, make the
determination in accordance with section 2.17, except that for a dust
use 10 mg/L as the toxic limit and for a mist use 2 mg/L as the toxic
limit. For a substance in the form of vapour the toxic limit is the same
as for a gas, which is 5 000 mL/m^3^.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 13
:::

#### [Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228582 .Subheading}

- **[[2.34]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.34
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The first step in determining the
  packing group of a mixture of liquids with an inhalation toxicity by
  vapour when one or more of the substances has an LC~50~ (vapour) less
  than or equal to 5 000 mL/m^3^, and the LC~50~ of each substance is
  known, is to determine the following data:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} determine the LC~50~ (vapour) for the mixture in
    accordance with section 2.33;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where P~i~ is the vapour pressure of the i^th^
    substance in kPa at 20°C and an absolute pressure of 101.3 kPa,
    determine the volatility, V~i~, of each substance in the mixture as

    V~i~ = P~i~ multiplied by 10^6^ then divided by 101.3;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} determine the ratio of the volatility of a
    substance to its LC~50~ for each substance with an LC~50~ less than
    or equal to 5 000 mL/m^3^ as

    R~i~ = V~i~ divided by the LC~50~ of the i^th^ substance;

  and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} set R equal to the sum of the R~i~ for each of the
    substances with an LC~50~ less than or equal to 5 000 mL/m^3^ as

    R = R~1~ + R~2~ + \... + (as needed).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Using the data determined in accordance with
  subsection (1), the mixture is included in one of the following
  packing groups:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group I, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} R is greater than or equal to 10, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the LC~50~ (mixture) is less than or equal to
      1 000 mL/m^3^;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group II, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} R is greater than or equal to 1,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the LC~50~ (mixture) is less than or equal to
      3 000 mL/m^3^, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I
      are not met; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group III, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} R is greater than or equal to 0.2,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the LC~50~ (mixture) is less than or equal to
      5 000 mL/m^3^, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I
      or II are not met.

#### [Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity and an Unknown LC~50~]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228605 .Subheading}

- **[[2.35]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.35 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  mixture of liquids with an inhalation toxicity and an unknown LC~50~
  is included in Packing Group I if it meets the following criteria:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} when a sample of the mixture is vapourized and
    diluted with air to create a test atmosphere of 1 000 mL/m^3^ and 10
    young adult albino rats (5 male and 5 female) are exposed to the
    test atmosphere for 1 hour and observed for 14 days, the result is
    the death of 5 or more of the animals within the 14-day observation
    period; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} when a sample of the vapour in equilibrium with the
    mixture at 20°C is diluted with 9 equal volumes of air to form a
    test atmosphere and 10 young adult albino rats (5 male and 5 female)
    are exposed to the test atmosphere for 1 hour and observed for 14
    days, the result is the death of 5 or more of the animals within the
    14-day observation period.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A mixture of liquids with an inhalation toxicity and
  an unknown LC~50~ is included in Packing Group II if it meets the
  following criteria and the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I
  are not met:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} when a sample of the mixture is vapourized and
    diluted with air to create a test atmosphere of 3 000 mL/m^3^ and 10
    young adult albino rats (5 male and 5 female) are exposed to the
    test atmosphere for 1 hour and observed for 14 days, the result is
    the death of 5 or more of the animals within the 14-day observation
    period; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} when a sample of the vapour in equilibrium with the
    mixture at 20°C is used to form a test atmosphere and 10 young adult
    albino rats (5 male and 5 female) are exposed to the test atmosphere
    for 1 hour and observed for 14 days, the result is the death of 5 or
    more of the animals within the 14-day observation period.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A mixture of liquids with an inhalation toxicity and
  an unknown LC~50~ is included in Packing Group III if it meets the
  following criteria and the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I
  or II are not met:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} when a sample of the mixture is vapourized and
    diluted with air to create a test atmosphere of 5 000 mL/m^3^ and 10
    young adult albino rats (5 male and 5 female) are exposed to the
    test atmosphere for 1 hour and observed for 14 days, the result is
    the death of 5 or more of the animals within the 14-day observation
    period; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} when the vapour pressure of the mixture is
    measured, the vapour concentration is greater than or equal to
    1 000 mL/m^3^.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If only LC~50~ data relating to 4-hour exposures to
  dust or mist are available, those figures can be multiplied by 4 and
  the result taken as the LC~50~ data for 1 hour, that is LC~50~ 4 hours
  (dust or mist) multiplied by 4 is equivalent to LC~50~ 1 hour.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} If only LC~50~ data relating to 4-hour exposures to
  vapour are available, those figures can be multiplied by 2 and the
  result taken as the LC~50~ data for 1 hour, that is LC~50~ 4 hours
  (vapour) multiplied by 2 is equivalent to LC~50~ 1 hour.

#### [Infectious Substances]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228618 .Subheading}

- **[[2.36]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.36
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Substances are included in
  Class 6.2, Category A or Category B if they are infectious substances
  and are listed in Appendix 3 to this Part or exhibit characteristics
  similar to a substance listed in that appendix.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Infectious substances that are included in Category A
  and that are in a form other than a culture may be handled, offered
  for transport or transported as Category B in accordance with the
  conditions set out in paragraphs 1.39(a) to (c) of Part 1 (Coming into
  Force, Repeal, Interpretation, General Provisions and Special Cases).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), the following infectious
  substances included in Category A, and any substance that exhibits
  characteristics similar to these substances, must always be handled,
  offered for transport or transported as Category A:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic fever virus;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Ebola virus;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Flexal virus;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} Guanarito virus;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} Hantaviruses causing hemorrhagic fever with renal
    syndrome;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} Hantaviruses causing pulmonary syndrome;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} Hendra virus;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} Herpes B virus (Cercopithecine Herpesvirus-1);

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} Junin virus;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} Kyasanur Forest virus;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} Lassa virus;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} Machupo virus;

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} Marburg virus;

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} Monkeypox virus;

  - [(o)]{.lawlabel} Nipah virus;

  - [(p)]{.lawlabel} Omsk hemorrhagic fever virus;

  - [(q)]{.lawlabel} Russian Spring -- Summer encephalitis virus;

  - [(r)]{.lawlabel} Sabia virus; and

  - [(s)]{.lawlabel} Variola (smallpox virus).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 36
:::

#### [Medical or Clinical Waste]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228644 .Subheading}

**[[2.36.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.36.1 .sectionLabel}** Dangerous goods
that are medical or clinical waste must be classified

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} under UN2814 or, as applicable, under UN2900, if they
  contain Category A infectious substances;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} under UN3291, if they contain Category B infectious
  substances; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} under UN3291, if the shipper has reasonable grounds
  to believe that they have a low probability of containing infectious
  substances.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-306, s. 20
- SOR/2016-95, s. 7(E)
:::

### [Class 7, Radioactive Materials]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228651 .Subheading}

#### [General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228652 .Subheading}

**[[2.37]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.37 .sectionLabel}** Substances defined as
Class 7, Radioactive Materials in the [Packaging and Transport of
Nuclear Substances Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2000-208) are
included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 36
:::

#### [Divisions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228656 .Subheading}

**[[2.38]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.38 .sectionLabel}** There are no
divisions for Class 7.

#### [Packing Groups]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228658 .Subheading}

**[[2.39]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.39 .sectionLabel}** There are no packing
groups for Class 7.

### [Class 8, Corrosives]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228660 .Subheading}

#### [General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228661 .Subheading}

**[[2.40]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.40 .sectionLabel}** Substances are
included in Class 8, Corrosives, if they

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} are known to cause full thickness destruction of
  human skin, that is, skin lesions that are permanent and destroy all
  layers of the outer skin through to the internal tissues;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} cause full thickness skin destruction, as determined
  in accordance with OECD Guideline 430 or OECD Guideline 431; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} do not cause full thickness destruction of skin, but
  exhibit a corrosion rate that exceeds 6.25 mm per year at a test
  temperature of 55°C, as determined in accordance with section 37 of
  Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-306, s. 21
- SOR/2017-137, s. 25
:::

#### [Divisions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228668 .Subheading}

**[[2.41]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.41 .sectionLabel}** There are no
divisions for Class 8.

#### [Packing Groups]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228670 .Subheading}

- **[[2.42]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.42 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  a substance is known to be included in Class 8, Corrosives, and that
  knowledge is based on documentary evidence published in technical
  journals or government publications and testing is not done to
  determine the packing group, the substance must be included in Packing
  Group I.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Class 8, Corrosives, are included in one of the
  following packing groups:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group I, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} they are known to cause full thickness
      destruction of human skin, that is, skin lesions that are
      permanent and that destroy all layers of the outer skin through to
      the internal tissues, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} full thickness destruction of intact skin tissue
      occurs within an observation period of 60 minutes after an
      exposure time of 3 minutes or less, as determined in accordance
      with OECD Guideline 404 or OECD Guideline 435;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group II, if full thickness destruction of
    skin occurs within an observation period of 14 days after an
    exposure time of more than 3 minutes but not more than 60 minutes,
    as determined in accordance with OECD Guideline 404 or OECD
    Guideline 435; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Packing Group III, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} full thickness destruction of intact skin tissue
      occurs within an observation period of 14 days after an exposure
      time of more than 60 minutes but not more than 4 hours, as
      determined in accordance with OECD Guideline 404 or OECD Guideline
      435, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} they exhibit a corrosion rate that exceeds
      6.25 mm per year at a test temperature of 55°C on steel or
      aluminum surfaces as determined in accordance with subparagraph
      2.8.2.5(c)(ii) of the UN Recommendations.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An in vitro test may be used instead of the test in
  the OECD Guidelines.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-306, s. 22
:::

### [Class 9, Miscellaneous Products, Substances or Organisms]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228690 .Subheading}

#### [General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228691 .Subheading}

**[[2.43]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.43 .sectionLabel}** A substance is
included in Class 9, Miscellaneous Products, Substances or Organisms, if
it

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is included in Class 9 in column 3 of Schedule 1; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} is not included in Class 9 in column 3 of Schedule 1
  and does not meet the criteria for inclusion in any of Classes 1 to 8
  and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2014-306\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is a marine pollutant under section 2.7 of Part 2
    (Classification), or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} except for asphalt or tar, is offered for
    transport or transported at a temperature greater than or equal to
    100°C if it is in a liquid state or at a temperature greater than or
    equal to 240°C if it is in a solid state.

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2008-34\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2008-34\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 37
- SOR/2014-306, s. 23
:::

#### [Lithium Cells and Batteries]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228702 .Subheading}

- **[[2.43.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.43.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person must not handle, offer for
  transport or transport lithium cells and batteries under any of the
  following shipping names unless the cells and batteries meet the
  conditions set out in subsection (2):

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} UN3090, LITHIUM METAL BATTERIES;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} UN3091, LITHIUM METAL BATTERIES CONTAINED IN
    EQUIPMENT or LITHIUM METAL BATTERIES PACKED WITH EQUIPMENT;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} UN3480, LITHIUM ION BATTERIES; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} UN3481, LITHIUM ION BATTERIES CONTAINED IN
    EQUIPMENT or LITHIUM ION BATTERIES PACKED WITH EQUIPMENT.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The conditions are as follows:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the cell or battery type passes each test set out
    in subsection 38.3 of Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} each cell or battery has a safety venting device or
    is designed to prevent a violent rupture under normal conditions of
    transport;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} each cell or battery is equipped to prevent
    external short circuits; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} each battery containing cells or a series of cells
    connected in parallel is equipped with diodes, fuses or other
    devices that prevent dangerous reverse current flow.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-306, s. 24
- SOR/2017-137, s. 26
:::

#### [Divisions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228716 .Subheading}

**[[2.44]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.44 .sectionLabel}** There are no
divisions for Class 9.

#### [Packing Groups]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1228718 .Subheading}

**[[2.45]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2.45 .sectionLabel}** Substances included
in Class 9, Miscellaneous Products, Substances and Organisms, are
included in Packing Group III unless they are included in a different
packing group shown for them in column 4 of Schedule 1.

## [APPENDIX 5]{.scheduleLabel}[[\[Repealed, SOR/2008-34, s. 38\]]{.Repealed}]{.scheduleTitleText}  {#h-1228786 .scheduleLabel}
:::
::::
:::::

## [PART 3]{.HLabel1}[Documentation]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1228787 .Part}

### [Consignor Responsibilities]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228788 .Subheading}

- **[[3.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-3.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Before allowing a carrier to take
  possession of dangerous goods for transport, the consignor must
  prepare and give to that carrier a shipping document or, if the
  carrier agrees, an electronic copy of the shipping document.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When dangerous goods are imported into Canada, the
  consignor must, before the dangerous goods are transported in Canada,
  ensure that the carrier has a shipping document or, with the agreement
  of the carrier, an electronic copy of the shipping document that
  contains the information required by these Regulations.

### [Carrier Responsibilities]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228792 .Subheading}

- **[[3.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-3.2 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  carrier must not take possession of dangerous goods for transport
  unless the carrier has the shipping document for the dangerous goods.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A carrier who accepts an electronic copy of a
  shipping document must produce a shipping document from the electronic
  copy before taking possession of the dangerous goods for transport.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Dangerous goods in transport are in the possession of
  a carrier from the time the carrier takes possession of them for
  transport until another person takes possession of them.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} While the dangerous goods are in transport and in the
  possession of a carrier, the carrier must keep the shipping document
  in the location specified by sections 3.7 to 3.10.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} At or before the time another carrier takes
  possession of the dangerous goods, the carrier must give the shipping
  document or a copy of the shipping document to that other carrier or,
  with that other carrier's agreement, an electronic copy of it.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} At or before the time a person, other than another
  carrier, takes possession of the dangerous goods, the carrier of the
  dangerous goods must give to that person a document that identifies
  the dangerous goods or, with that person's agreement, an electronic
  copy of a document that identifies the dangerous goods.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} A carrier may replace a shipping document provided by
  the consignor with a new shipping document or with a copy of the
  shipping document in a different format.

### [Consist for Transport by Rail]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228801 .Subheading}

- **[[3.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-3.3 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When
  a train includes a railway vehicle containing dangerous goods for
  which a placard is required to be displayed in accordance with Part 4
  (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), the person in charge of the train must
  prepare and give a consist to a member of the train crew. The
  information on the consist must be kept up to date by the train crew
  and kept with the shipping document.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The consist must include, for each railway vehicle
  containing dangerous goods for which a placard is required to be
  displayed in accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the numerical location of the railway vehicle in
    the train, numbering the first vehicle at the head of the train as
    1, the next vehicle as 2 and so on, excluding the locomotive or
    locomotives wherever they are located in the train;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the reporting mark of the railway vehicle;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} for a tank car, the shipping name or UN number of
    the dangerous goods in the tank car; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} for a railway vehicle other than a tank car,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous
      goods, if the railway vehicle contains only dangerous goods with
      the same shipping name and UN number, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the words "Dangerous Goods" or "[Marchandises
      dangereuses]{.otherLang lang="fr"}", if the railway vehicle
      contains dangerous goods that have different shipping names or UN
      numbers.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A carrier must be able to immediately provide to
  CANUTEC a copy of a consist whenever the train to which the consist
  applies is in operation or is involved in an accident.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 16
:::

### [Legibility and Language]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228814 .Subheading}

- **[[3.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-3.4 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  information required on a shipping document and on a consist must be
  easy to identify, legible, in indelible print and in English or
  French.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When the information related to dangerous goods is on
  the same shipping document with information related to non-dangerous
  goods, the dangerous goods information must be shown

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} before the information related to the non-dangerous
    goods and under the heading "Dangerous Goods" or "[Marchandises
    dangereuses]{.otherLang lang="fr"}";

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} printed or highlighted in a colour that contrasts
    with the print or highlight used for the information related to the
    non-dangerous goods; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} following the letter "X" opposite the UN number in
    a column under the heading "DG" or "MD".

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2023-155, s. 27](#1407978-1418218){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1407978-1418218.html"
  role="button"}
:::

### [Information on a Shipping Document]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228821 .Subheading}

- **[[3.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-3.5 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  following information must be included on a shipping document:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the place of business in
    Canada of the consignor;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the date the shipping document or an electronic
    copy of it was prepared or was first given to a carrier;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the description of each of the dangerous goods, in
    the following order:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the UN number,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name and, immediately after the
      shipping name unless it is already part of it,

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} for dangerous goods that are subject to special
        provision 16, the technical name, in parentheses, of at least
        one of the most dangerous substances that predominantly
        contributes to the danger or dangers posed by the dangerous
        goods, and

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} for a liquefied petroleum gas that has not been
        odorized, the words "Not Odourized" or "Not Odorized" or "[Sans
        odorisant]{.otherLang lang="fr"}",

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the primary class, which may be shown as a
      number only or under the heading "Class" or "[Classe]{.otherLang
      lang="fr"}" or following the word "Class" or "[Classe]{.otherLang
      lang="fr"}",

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} for dangerous goods with a primary class of
      Class 1, Explosives, the compatibility group letter following the
      primary class,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the subsidiary class or classes, in parentheses,
      which may be shown as a number only or under the heading
      "subsidiary class" or "[classe subsidiaire]{.otherLang lang="fr"}"
      or following the words "subsidiary class" or "[classe
      subsidiaire]{.otherLang lang="fr"}", except that, for transport by
      aircraft or by vessel, the subsidiary class or classes may be
      shown after the information required by this paragraph,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the packing group roman numeral, which may be
      shown under the heading "PG" or "[GE]{.otherLang lang="fr"}" or
      following the letters "PG" or "[GE]{.otherLang lang="fr"}" or
      following the words "Packing Group" or "[Groupe
      d'emballage]{.otherLang lang="fr"}", and

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} for dangerous goods that are subject to special
      provision 23, the words "toxic by inhalation" or "toxic --
      inhalation hazard" or "[toxique par inhalation]{.otherLang
      lang="fr"}" or "[toxicité par inhalation]{.otherLang lang="fr"}";

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} for each shipping name, the quantity of dangerous
    goods and the unit of measure used to express the quantity which, on
    a shipping document prepared in Canada, must be a unit of measure
    included in the International System of Units (SI) or a unit of
    measure acceptable for use under the SI system, except that for
    dangerous goods included in Class 1, Explosives, the quantity must
    be expressed in net explosives quantity or, for explosives with UN
    numbers subject to special provision 85 or 86, in number of articles
    or net explosives quantity;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} for dangerous goods in one or more small means of
    containment that require a label to be displayed on them in
    accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), the number of
    small means of containment for each shipping name; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the words "24-Hour Number" or "[Numéro 24
    heures]{.otherLang lang="fr"}", or an abbreviation of these words,
    followed by a telephone number, including the area code, at which
    the consignor can be reached immediately for technical information
    about the dangerous goods in transport, without breaking the
    telephone connection made by the caller.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The telephone number of a person who is not the
  consignor, such as CANUTEC, but who is competent to give the technical
  information required by paragraph (1)(f) in English or in French may
  be used. However, to use CANUTEC's telephone number, the consignor
  must receive permission, in writing, from CANUTEC. A consignor who
  uses the telephone number of an organization or agency other than
  CANUTEC must ensure that the organization or agency has current,
  accurate information on the dangerous goods the consignor offers for
  transport and, if the organization or agency is located outside
  Canada, the telephone number must include the country code and, if
  required, the city code.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A means of containment, or the contents of a means of
  containment, that is being fumigated with dangerous goods and that is
  in transport must be accompanied by a shipping document that, despite
  subsections (1) and (5) and section 3.6, includes the following
  information if the fumigant is the only dangerous goods in transport
  in the means of containment:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name, "FUMIGATED CARGO TRANSPORT UNIT"
    or "[ENGIN DE TRANSPORT SOUS FUMIGATION]{.otherLang lang="fr"}";

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the class, Class 9;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the UN number, UN3359;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of the fumigant;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the date of fumigation; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} instructions for the disposal of residues of the
    fumigant or fumigation device.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Despite paragraph (1)(d), if the means of containment
  contains a residue, the words "Residue -- Last Contained" or "[Résidu
  -- dernier contenu]{.otherLang lang="fr"}" may be added before or
  after the description of the dangerous goods. These words must not,
  however, be used for dangerous goods included in Class 2, Gases, that
  are in a small means of containment or for dangerous goods included in
  Class 7, Radioactive Materials.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the quantity of dangerous goods required on a
  shipping document under paragraph (1)(d) or the number of small means
  of containment required under paragraph (1)(e) changes during
  transport, the carrier must show those changes on the shipping
  document or on a document attached to the shipping document.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2008-34, s. 40\]]{.Repealed}

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2014-306, s. 26\]]{.Repealed}

### [Additional Information on a Shipping Document]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228853 .Subheading}

- **[[3.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-3.6 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  addition to the information required by subsection 3.5(1), the
  shipping document for dangerous goods for which an approved ERAP is
  required under subsection 7(1) of the Act must include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the ERAP reference number issued by Transport
    Canada, preceded or followed by the letters "ERAP" or
    "[PIU]{.otherLang lang="fr"}"; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the ERAP telephone number required under paragraph
    7.3(2)(f).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the 24-hour number required by paragraph 3.5(1)(f)
  and the ERAP telephone number are the same, that number may be shown
  on the same line on the shipping document.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} In addition to the information required by subsection
  3.5(1), the following information must be included on a shipping
  document:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for dangerous goods in transport by vessel,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the flash point for dangerous goods included in
      Class 3, Flammable Liquids, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for dangerous goods that are marine pollutants
      under section 2.7 of Part 2 (Classification), the words "marine
      pollutant" or "[polluant marin]{.otherLang lang="fr"}" and, for a
      pesticide that is a marine pollutant, the name and concentration
      of the most active substance in the pesticide;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for dangerous goods included in Class 4.1,
    Flammable Solids, the control and emergency temperatures shown in
    section 2.4.2.3.2.3 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations, if
    applicable;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} for dangerous goods included in Class 5.2, Organic
    Peroxides, the control and emergency temperatures shown in section
    2.5.3.2.4 of Chapter 2.5 of the UN Recommendations, if applicable;
    and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} for dangerous goods included in Class 7, the
    additional information required for transport documents under the
    [Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations,
    2015](/eng/regulations/SOR-2015-145).

::: HistoricalNote

- SOR/2008-34, s. 41

### [Consignor's Certification]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228868 .Subheading}

- **[[3.6.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-3.6.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A shipping document must include,
  after the information required under section 3.5, one of the following
  certifications:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} "I hereby declare that the contents of this
    consignment are fully and accurately described above by the proper
    shipping name, are properly classified and packaged, have dangerous
    goods safety marks properly affixed or displayed on them, and are in
    all respects in proper condition for transport according to the
    Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations.";

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the certification set out in section 172.204 of
    49 CFR;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the certification set out in section 5;4.1.6 of the
    ICAO Technical Instructions;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the certification set out in section 5.4.1.6 of the
    IMDG Code; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the certification set out in section 5.4.1.6 of the
    UN Recommendations.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The certification must be made by an individual who
  is the consignor or by an individual acting on behalf of the consignor
  and must set out that individual's name.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in respect of a large
  means of containment that contains a residue.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-152, s. 15
- SOR/2016-95, s. 8(F)
- SOR/2017-137, s. 27
- SOR/2019-101, s. 6

### [Location of a Shipping Document: Road]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228880 .Subheading}

**[[3.7]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-3.7 .sectionLabel}** The driver of a power
unit that is attached to or is part of the cargo unit of a road vehicle
transporting dangerous goods must ensure that a copy of the shipping
document is kept, as follows:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the driver is in the power unit, in a pocket
  mounted on the driver's door or within the driver's reach; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the driver is out of the power unit, in a pocket
  mounted on the driver's door, on the driver's seat or in a location
  that is clearly visible to anyone entering through the driver's door.

### [Location of a Shipping Document and Consist: Rail]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228884 .Subheading}

**[[3.8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-3.8 .sectionLabel}** The person in charge of
a train transporting dangerous goods must ensure that a copy of the
shipping document and, when a consist is required, a copy of the consist
are kept,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} when one or more members of the train crew are
  present, in the possession of one of them; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} when no member of the train crew is present, in the
  first locomotive.

### [Location of a Shipping Document: Marine]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228888 .Subheading}

- **[[3.9]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-3.9 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  master of a vessel containing dangerous goods or the master in control
  of a vessel containing dangerous goods must have readily available on
  or near the bridge of the vessel a paper copy or electronic copy of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the shipping document; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a list that includes the classification of the
    dangerous goods.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If dangerous goods are transported by vessel on board
  a road vehicle that is accompanied by one or more drivers or a railway
  vehicle that is accompanied by one or more members of the train crew,
  a driver or a member of the train crew must notify the master of the
  vessel or the marine carrier of the presence of the dangerous goods
  and make available to the master a copy of the shipping document.
  However, the shipping document must be kept, for the road vehicle, in
  accordance with section 3.7 and, for the railway vehicle, in the
  possession of a member of the train crew.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 42
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
:::

### [Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1228896 .Subheading}

- **[[3.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-3.10 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  carrier must ensure that a shipping document is placed in a waterproof
  receptacle that is securely attached to or near the means of
  containment containing the dangerous goods, at a readily identifiable
  and accessible location, when the dangerous goods are in transport if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} they are left in an unsupervised area

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} after being unloaded from a means of transport,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} after the cargo unit of a road vehicle
      containing them has been disconnected from the power unit, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} when the railway vehicle containing them is no
      longer part of a train; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} possession of the dangerous goods has not been
    transferred to another person.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When dangerous goods in transport are left in a
  supervised area, the person in charge of the supervised area is
  considered to have taken possession of the dangerous goods. The
  carrier must leave a copy of the shipping document with that person,
  who must keep it and give it to the next person who takes possession
  of the dangerous goods.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} When the person in charge of a supervised area is
  absent from the area, that person must ensure that the copy of the
  shipping document is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} placed in a waterproof receptacle securely attached
    to or near the means of containment containing the dangerous goods,
    at a readily identifiable and accessible location; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} left in the possession of an employee who is
    present in the supervised area and is designated for this purpose by
    the person in charge of the supervised area.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Despite the locations specified in subsections (1) to
  (3), when dangerous goods that are in transport by road vehicle,
  railway vehicle or vessel are stored in a supervised or unsupervised
  area, the shipping document or an electronic copy of it may be left at
  the office of a person referred to in one of the following paragraphs
  if the conditions in subsections (5) and (6) are complied with:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the rail dispatcher for the area in which the
    railway vehicle is located;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person responsible for the port at which the
    dangerous goods are located; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the marine terminal manager at the terminal where
    the dangerous goods are located.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} When a shipping record is left at the office of a
  person referred to in subsection (4),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} use of the telephone number of that office must be
    approved in accordance with subsection (6); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that person or that person's representative must
    provide immediately, at the request of a federal, provincial or
    municipal official including a member of a fire department, a
    facsimile or electronic copy of the shipping record or, if
    requested, a voice description of the information on the shipping
    record.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The telephone number of the office of a person
  referred to in subsection (4) must not be used to comply with
  subsection (5), unless that person gives CANUTEC the following
  information and receives approval, in writing, from CANUTEC to use
  that telephone number:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the person;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the telephone number of the office of the person;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the physical area to which the telephone number
    applies and, in the case of a port or a marine terminal, evidence
    that public access to the area is controlled;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the period of time, not to exceed 5 years, for
    which CANUTEC's approval is requested; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods to which the approval applies.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may revoke, in writing, the approval to
  use a telephone number if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person referred to in subsection (4), or that
    person's representative, does not answer the telephone;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person referred to in subsection (4), or that
    person's representative, does not provide immediately, at the
    request of a federal, provincial or municipal official including a
    member of a fire department, a facsimile or an electronic copy of
    the shipping record or, if requested, a voice description of the
    information on the shipping record; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} public access to a port or marine terminal is not
    controlled.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52

  role="button"}
