### [Consolidation Bins]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229613 .Subheading}

#### [Consolidation Bins]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1229614 .Subheading}

**[[5.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-5.18 .sectionLabel}** A person must not use
a consolidation bin to handle or transport dangerous goods in a road
vehicle unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the capacity of the consolidation bin is less than or
  equal to 1.8 m^3^ (64 cubic feet);

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the consolidation bin is reusable and constructed of
  plastic, wood or metal; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the consolidation bin is blocked or braced within the
  road vehicle.

## [PART 6]{.HLabel1}[Training]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1229619 .Part}

### [Training Certificate Requirements]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229620 .Subheading}

- **[[6.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-6.1 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person who handles, offers for transport or transports dangerous goods
  must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} be adequately trained and hold a training
    certificate in accordance with this Part; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} perform those activities in the presence and under
    the direct supervision of a person who is adequately trained and who
    holds a training certificate in accordance with this Part.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An employer must not direct or allow an employee to
  handle, offer for transport or transport dangerous goods unless the
  employee

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is adequately trained and holds a training
    certificate in accordance with this Part; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} performs those activities in the presence and under
    the direct supervision of a person who is adequately trained and who
    holds a training certificate in accordance with this Part.

### [Adequate Training]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229628 .Subheading}

**[[6.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-6.2 .sectionLabel}** A person is adequately
trained if the person has a sound knowledge of all the topics listed in
paragraphs (a) to (m) that relate directly to the person's duties and to
the dangerous goods the person is expected to handle, offer for
transport or transport:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the classification criteria and test methods in Part
  2 (Classification);

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} shipping names;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the use of Schedules 1, 2 and 3;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the shipping document and train consist requirements
  in Part 3 (Documentation);

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods safety marks requirements in Part
  4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks);

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the certification safety marks requirements, safety
  requirements and safety standards in Part 5 (Means of Containment);

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the ERAP requirements in Part 7 (Emergency Response
  Assistance Plan);

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} the report requirements in Part 8 (Reporting
  Requirements);

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} safe handling and transportation practices for
  dangerous goods, including the characteristics of the dangerous goods;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} the proper use of any equipment used to handle or
  transport the dangerous goods;

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} the reasonable emergency measures the person must
  take to reduce or eliminate any danger to public safety that results
  or may reasonably be expected to result from an accidental release of
  the dangerous goods;

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} for air transport, the aspects of training set out in
  Chapter 4, Training, of Part 1, General, of the ICAO Technical
  Instructions for the persons named in that Chapter and the
  requirements in Part 12 (Air) of these Regulations; and

- [(m)]{.lawlabel} for marine transport, the requirements of the IMDG
  Code and the requirements of Part 11 (Marine) of these Regulations.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 29
- SOR/2016-95, s. 41
- SOR/2017-253, s. 17
- SOR/2019-101, s. 22
:::

### [Issuance and Contents of a Training Certificate]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229645 .Subheading}

- **[[6.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-6.3 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  employer who has reasonable grounds to believe that an employee is
  adequately trained and will perform duties to which the training
  relates must issue a training certificate to the employee that
  includes the following information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the place of business of
    the employer;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the employee's name;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date the training certificate expires, preceded
    by the words "Expires on" or "[Date d'expiration]{.otherLang
    lang="fr"}"; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the aspects of handling, offering for transport or
    transporting dangerous goods for which the employee is trained,
    including the specific topics set out in section 6.2.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A self-employed person who has reasonable grounds to
  believe that he or she is adequately trained and who will perform
  duties to which the training relates must issue to himself or herself
  a training certificate that includes the information required by
  subsection (1).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The training certificate must be signed

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} by the employee and by the employer or another
    employee acting on behalf of the employer; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a self-employed person, by that
    person.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), if the employer of a person
  who is a member of a vessel's complement has reasonable grounds to
  believe that the person's certificate of competency issued in
  accordance with the [Marine Certification
  Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-97-391) is acceptable evidence that
  the person is adequately trained, the employer is not required to
  issue the training certificate. The certificate of competency is a
  valid training certificate for the purposes of these Regulations when
  the certificate of competency is valid in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
:::

### [Foreign Carriers]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229659 .Subheading}

- **[[6.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-6.4 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  document that is issued to a driver of a road vehicle licensed in the
  United States or to a member of the crew of a train subject to 49 CFR
  for the transportation of dangerous goods and that indicates that the
  driver or the crew member is trained in accordance with sections
  172.700 to 172.704 of 49 CFR is a valid training certificate for the
  purposes of these Regulations when that document is valid in the
  United States.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A document that is issued to a foreign member of the
  flight crew of an aircraft registered in a country that is a Member
  State of the International Civil Aviation Organization and that
  indicates that the crew member is trained to transport dangerous goods
  by air is a valid training certificate for the purposes of these
  Regulations, in accordance with Article 33 of the Convention on
  International Civil Aviation, when that document is valid in the
  Member State.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A document that is issued to a foreign member of the
  crew of a vessel registered in a country that is a Member State of the
  International Maritime Organization and that indicates that the crew
  member is trained to transport dangerous goods by vessel is a valid
  training certificate for the purposes of these Regulations when that
  document is valid in the Member State.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
:::

### [Expiry of a Training Certificate]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229666 .Subheading}

**[[6.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-6.5 .sectionLabel}** A training certificate
expires

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} for transport by aircraft, 24 months after its date
  of issuance; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} for transport by road vehicle, railway vehicle or
  vessel, 36 months after its date of issuance.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
:::

### [Keeping Proof of Training: Employer's and Self-Employed Person's Responsibility]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229672 .Subheading}

**[[6.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-6.6 .sectionLabel}** An employer or a
self-employed person must keep a record of training or a statement of
experience, as well as a copy of a training certificate, in electronic
or paper form, beginning on the date the training certificate is issued
and continuing until two years after the date it expires.

### [Showing Proof of Training: Employer's and Self-Employed Person's Responsibility]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229674 .Subheading}

**[[6.7]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-6.7 .sectionLabel}** Within 15 days after
the date of a written request by an inspector, the employer of a person
who holds a training certificate or a self-employed person must provide
a copy of the training certificate to the inspector and, if applicable,
a copy of the record of training or the statement of experience and a
description of the training material used in the person's training.

### [Showing Proof of Training: Trained Person's Responsibility]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229676 .Subheading}

**[[6.8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-6.8 .sectionLabel}** A person who handles,
offers for transport or transports dangerous goods, or who directly
supervises another person engaged in these activities, must give his or
her training certificate, or a copy of it, to an inspector immediately
on request.

## [PART 7]{.HLabel1}[Emergency Response Assistance Plan]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1229678 .Part}

### [Application]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229679 .Subheading}

**[[7.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-7.1 .sectionLabel}** This Part sets out

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the requirement to have an approved ERAP;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the approval of an ERAP;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the authorization to use an approved ERAP;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the implementation of an approved ERAP; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the compensation for the authorized implementation of
  an approved ERAP.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 30
- SOR/2008-34, s. 74
- SOR/2011-239, s. 4
- SOR/2014-152, s. 25
- SOR/2014-306, s. 33 (Erratum, Vol. 149, No. 2, page 329)
- SOR/2015-100, s. 6
:::

### [Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229688 .Subheading}

- **[[7.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-7.2 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For
  the purposes of subsection 7(1) of the Act, an approved ERAP is
  required for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} dangerous goods that have the same UN number and
    that are contained in a single means of containment, if the quantity
    of those dangerous goods exceeds the ERAP index in column 7 of
    Schedule 1;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} dangerous goods, in a road vehicle or a railway
    vehicle, that have the same UN number and that are contained in more
    than one means of containment, if the total quantity of those
    dangerous goods exceeds the ERAP index in column 7 of Schedule 1 and
    are included in one of the following classes:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} Class 3, Flammable Liquids, with a subsidiary
      class of Class 6.1, Toxic Substances,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} Class 4, Flammable Solids; Substances Liable to
      Spontaneous Combustion; Substances That on Contact with Water Emit
      Flammable Gases (Water-reactive substances),

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides, that are Type B
      or Type C,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} Class 6.1, Toxic Substances, that are included
      in Packing Group I;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} dangerous goods, in a road vehicle or a railway
    vehicle, that have the same UN number, and that are contained in
    more than one large means of containment, if the total quantity of
    those dangerous goods exceeds the ERAP index in column 7 of Schedule
    1;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} dangerous goods, in a road vehicle or a railway
    vehicle, that are included in Class 1, Explosives, and that are
    contained in one or more means of containment, if the total quantity
    of those dangerous goods exceeds the ERAP index in column 7 of
    Schedule 1 for the explosives with the lowest index number in that
    column;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} dangerous goods that are included in Class 2,
    Gases, that have the same UN number, that are contained in more than
    one means of containment --- each of which has a capacity greater
    than 225 L --- that are a single unit as a result of being
    interconnected through a piping arrangement and that are permanently
    mounted on a structural frame for transport, if the total quantity
    of those dangerous goods exceeds the ERAP index in column 7 of
    Schedule 1;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} any of the following dangerous goods that are
    transported by rail in a tank car, if the quantity of those
    dangerous goods in the tank car exceeds 10 000 L:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} UN1170, ETHANOL with more than 24% ethanol, by
      volume, ETHANOL SOLUTION with more than 24% ethanol, by volume,
      ETHYL ALCOHOL with more than 24% ethanol, by volume, or ETHYL
      ALCOHOL SOLUTION with more than 24% ethanol, by volume,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} UN1202, DIESEL FUEL, GAS OIL, or HEATING OIL,
      LIGHT,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} UN1203, GASOLINE, MOTOR SPIRIT, or PETROL,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} UN1267, PETROLEUM CRUDE OIL,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} UN1268, PETROLEUM DISTILLATES, N.O.S., or
      PETROLEUM PRODUCTS, N.O.S.,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} UN1863, FUEL, AVIATION, TURBINE ENGINE,

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} UN1987, ALCOHOLS, N.O.S.,

    - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} UN1993, FLAMMABLE LIQUID, N.O.S.,

    - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} UN3295, HYDROCARBONS, LIQUID, N.O.S.,

    - [(x)]{.lawlabel} UN3475, ETHANOL AND GASOLINE MIXTURE, with more
      than 10% ethanol, ETHANOL AND MOTOR SPIRIT MIXTURE, with more than
      10% ethanol, or ETHANOL AND PETROL MIXTURE, with more than 10%
      ethanol, and

    - [(xi)]{.lawlabel} UN3494, PETROLEUM SOUR CRUDE OIL, FLAMMABLE,
      TOXIC; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} any quantity of dangerous goods that are Risk Group
    4 human pathogens within the meaning of the [Human Pathogens and
    Toxins Act](/eng/acts/H-5.67).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any substance that would require an ERAP if its
  classification were determined in accordance with Part 2
  (Classification) requires an approved ERAP if its appropriate
  classification in the ICAO Technical Instructions, the IMDG Code or
  the UN Recommendations is to be used under subsection 2.2(4).

### [Application for Approval of an ERAP]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229714 .Subheading}

- **[[7.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-7.3 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person must apply to the Minister in writing for the approval of an
  ERAP.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application for approval must be signed by the
  applicant and must include a copy of the ERAP and the following
  information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of the applicant;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a description of the applicant's operations;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of any third party
    who assisted in the preparation of the application;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the classification of the dangerous goods to which
    the ERAP relates and the mode of transport used;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} for each mode of transport used,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the frequency of the transportation of the
      dangerous goods,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the type and specification of the means of
      containment used to transport the dangerous goods, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the geographical area in which the dangerous
      goods are transported;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the ERAP telephone number, including the area code,
    at which a person identified in the ERAP can be reached at any time
    while the dangerous goods are handled or transported;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a description of the communications systems that
    will be available at the location of a release or anticipated
    release of dangerous goods;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of any third-party
    emergency responders, their role and a copy of the agreement between
    the applicant and the third party;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the following information regarding the ERAP
    response equipment:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a detailed list of the equipment,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the location of the equipment,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the name of the person responsible for the
      operation of the equipment at each location,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} for each location, the dangerous goods in
      respect of which the equipment is to be used during emergency
      measures, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the geographical areas where the equipment at
      each location is to be used;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the following information respecting the ERAP
    response personnel, including technical advisors, team leaders and
    response teams:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} their names and contact information,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} their responsibilities,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} any training they have taken, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} description of their knowledge and experience in
      respect of the dangerous goods;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} the response capability in respect of the dangerous
    goods, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the measures that can be taken in response to the
      release or anticipated release,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the persons responsible for taking the measures
      referred to in subparagraph (i), and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the ERAP equipment that will be used to take
      those measures;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} an estimate of the time required for the response
    personnel and equipment to reach the location of the release or
    anticipated release and a description of the mobilization and
    deployment steps in respect of the response personnel and equipment;
    and

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} a potential incident analysis, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the following scenarios:

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} an anticipated release of dangerous goods,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the release of less than 1% of the dangerous
        goods in a means of containment,

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} the release of more than 50% of the dangerous
        goods in a means of containment, and

      - [(D)]{.lawlabel} the exposure to fire of a means of containment
        that contains dangerous goods,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the possible consequences of the release or
      anticipated release for each scenario,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the measures, organized by tier in accordance
      with section 7.8, to be taken in response to the release or
      anticipated release for each scenario, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the identification of the persons responsible
      for taking the measures referred to in subparagraph (iii).

### [Application for Approval of an ERAP -- Emergency Response Contractors]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229754 .Subheading}

**[[7.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-7.4 .sectionLabel}** A person who is not
required to have an approved ERAP under subsection 7(1) of the Act, but
who is able to take measures to respond to a release or anticipated
release of dangerous goods for the purposes of paragraph 7.1(b) of the
Act, may apply to the Minister in writing for the approval of an ERAP.
The application must include a copy of the ERAP and the information
referred to in paragraphs 7.3(2)(a), (b), (d), (g) and (i) to (l).

### [Application for Approval of Changes to Approved ERAP]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229756 .Subheading}

- **[[7.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-7.5 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person with an approved ERAP must, as soon as possible, apply to the
  Minister in writing for an approval of changes if any of the
  information referred to in paragraphs 7.3(2)(a) to (l) has changed
  since its approval.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application referred to in subsection (1) must be
  signed by the applicant and include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a copy of the ERAP; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the information referred to in paragraphs 7.3(2)(a)
    to (l) that has changed.

### [Request for Review of Decision]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229762 .Subheading}

- **[[7.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-7.6 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person may request a review of the decision to refuse an application
  for approval of an ERAP or to revoke an ERAP approval within 30 days
  after being notified of the decision.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The request must be made to the Minister in writing
  and must include the reasons why the decision should be revised.

### [Authorization to Use an Approved ERAP]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229766 .Subheading}

- **[[7.7]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-7.7 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person who is required to have an ERAP under subsection 7(1) of the
  Act may use, as an authorized user, the ERAP of another person who
  received approval for the ERAP if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the authorized user is not the producer of the
    dangerous goods to which the ERAP relates;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the ERAP applies to the dangerous goods, the mode
    of transport, the means of containment and the geographical area in
    which the dangerous goods will be in transport;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person who received approval for the ERAP
    agrees to take measures to respond to a release or anticipated
    release of the dangerous goods to which the ERAP relates; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the person who received approval for the ERAP
    provides a written authorization to the authorized user before the
    information referred to in subsection 3.6(1) is entered on the
    shipping document.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The authorized user must be able to produce a copy of
  the authorization referred to in paragraph (1)(d)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for two years after the day on which the
    authorization is no longer in effect; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} within 15 days after the day on which the
    authorized user receives a written request from the Minister.

### [Implementation of an Approved ERAP]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229776 .Subheading}

- **[[7.8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-7.8 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person with an approved ERAP must implement it to tier 1 or tier 2 in
  response to a release or anticipated release of dangerous goods.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who implements an approved ERAP to tier 1
  must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide technical or emergency response advice as
    soon as possible after a request for the advice; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} remotely monitor the response to the release or
    anticipated release.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person who implements an approved ERAP to tier 2
  must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide technical or emergency response advice as
    soon as possible after a request for the advice;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} monitor the response to the release or anticipated
    release; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} send ERAP emergency response resources to the
    location of the release or anticipated release.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A person must not prevent another person who has an
  approved ERAP from taking emergency measures in response to a release
  or anticipated release.

### [Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229787 .Subheading}

- **[[7.9]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-7.9 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  person implements an approved ERAP in accordance with paragraph 7.1(b)
  of the Act, the following expenses are authorized for the purposes of
  compensation under section 7.2 of the Act:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} expenses related to the death, disability or injury
    of the person or to the death, disability or injury of any of the
    person's employees or contractors if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the person, the employee or the contractor is
      killed, disabled or injured during the implementation of the ERAP,
      and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the death, disability or injury is the result of
      an act or omission that was committed by the person in good faith
      and without negligence;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the cost of the person's employees or contractors
    who are reasonably required to implement the ERAP;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the cost of using the person's tools and other
    equipment, such as vehicles, pumps, hoses and generators, that are
    reasonably required to implement the ERAP;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} travel expenses, such as those incurred for meals,
    accommodation, fuel, oil and flights, for persons who are reasonably
    required to implement the ERAP;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} rental fees for heavy equipment, such as cranes,
    bulldozers, pumps, compressors and generators, that are reasonably
    required to implement the ERAP;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} other overhead costs that can reasonably be
    attributed to the implementation of the ERAP;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the cost of repairing tools and other equipment
    that are damaged during the implementation of the ERAP;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the cost of replacing

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} single-use equipment and supplies, such as
      packaging, personal protective equipment, personal protective
      clothing, chemicals and other consumables, that are reasonably
      required to implement the ERAP,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} tools and other equipment that are lost during
      the implementation of the ERAP, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} tools and other equipment that are damaged
      beyond repair during the implementation of the ERAP;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the cost of repairing or replacing personal
    property or movables or real property or immovables that have to be
    damaged to implement the ERAP;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the cost of defending any legal action for which
    there is no personal liability under paragraph 20(c) of the Act; and

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} the cost of cleaning up after an incident,
    including handling and disposal costs for dangerous goods and
    contaminated materials.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The following expenses are not authorized for the
  purposes of compensation under section 7.2 of the Act:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the cost of purchasing new equipment to implement
    the approved ERAP; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the cost of lost business or production during the
    implementation of the approved ERAP.

### [Compensation Limits]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229809 .Subheading}

- **[[7.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-7.10
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Compensation under paragraph
  7.9(1)(a) is limited to the compensation that would be paid in
  relation to the dead, disabled or injured person if the person were
  insured under

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the Public Service Management Insurance Plan;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the Public Service Health Care Plan, with hospital
    coverage at level III; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the Public Service Dental Care Plan.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Compensation under paragraph 7.9(1)(h) in relation to
  the replacement of the items listed in subparagraphs
  7.9(1)(h)(i), (ii) and (iii) is limited to the cost of an item of
  equivalent capability and quality.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Compensation under paragraph 7.9(1)(i) in relation to
  damaged property is limited to the fair market value of the property
  immediately before it is damaged by the person who implements the
  approved ERAP.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-210, s. 2
:::

### [Claims for Compensation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229819 .Subheading}

**[[7.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-7.11 .sectionLabel}** Claims for
compensation must be submitted with supporting documentation to the
Minister no later than three months after completion of the emergency
response work.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-210, s. 2
:::

## [PART 8]{.HLabel1}[Reporting Requirements]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1229823 .Part}

### [Application and Interpretation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229824 .Subheading}

**[[8.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.1 .sectionLabel}** This Part applies in
respect of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the release or anticipated release of dangerous goods
  that are being offered for transport, handled or transported by road
  vehicle, railway vehicle or vessel;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the release or anticipated release of dangerous goods
  that are being offered for transport, handled or transported by
  aircraft;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} undeclared and misdeclared dangerous goods that are
  being offered for transport, handled or transported by aircraft;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the loss or theft of dangerous goods; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} unlawful interference with dangerous goods.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2003-273, s. 8
- SOR/2008-34, ss. 75, 76
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
:::

### [Road, Rail and Marine Reports]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229833 .Subheading}

#### [Emergency Report --- Road, Rail or Marine]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1229834 .Subheading}

**[[8.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.2 .sectionLabel}** A person who is
required by subsection 18(1) of the Act to report a release or
anticipated release of dangerous goods that are being offered for
transport, handled or transported by road vehicle, railway vehicle or
vessel must, as soon as possible after a release or anticipated release,
make an emergency report to any local authority that is responsible for
responding to emergencies at the geographic location of the release or
anticipated release if the dangerous goods are, or could be, in excess
of the quantity set out in the following table:

#### [Information To Be Included in an Emergency Report --- Road, Rail or Marine]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1229844 .Subheading}

**[[8.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.3 .sectionLabel}** An emergency report
referred to in section 8.2 must include the following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of the person making
  the report;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the
  date, time and geographic location of the release;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an anticipated release of dangerous
  goods, the date, time and geographic location of the incident that led
  to the anticipated release;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the mode of transport used;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous
  goods;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of dangerous goods that was in the means
  of containment before the release or anticipated release;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the
  quantity of dangerous goods estimated to have been released; and

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the type of incident leading to the
  release or anticipated release, including a collision, roll-over,
  derailment, overfill, fire, explosion or load-shift.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
:::

#### [Release or Anticipated Release Report --- Road, Rail or Marine]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1229856 .Subheading}

- **[[8.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.4
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), a person
  who has made an emergency report referred to in section 8.2 must, as
  soon as possible after making it, make a report to the persons listed
  in subsection (4).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), the person is not required
  to make a report referred to in subsection (1) if the release or
  anticipated release did not result in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the death of a person;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a person sustaining injuries that required
    immediate medical treatment by a health care provider;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an evacuation of people or their shelter in place;
    or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the closure of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a facility used in the loading and unloading of
      dangerous goods, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a road, a main railway line or a main waterway.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The person is required to make a report referred to
  in subsection (1) if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a means of containment has been damaged to the
    extent that its integrity is compromised; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the centre sill or stub sill of a tank car is
    broken or there is a crack in the metal equal to or greater than
    15 cm (6 in.).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), the persons to
  whom a report must be made are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} CANUTEC, at 1-888-CANUTEC (1-888-226-8832) or
    613-996-6666;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the consignor of the dangerous goods;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of dangerous goods included in Class 7,
    Radioactive Materials, the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a vessel, a Vessel Traffic Services
    Centre or a Canadian Coast Guard radio station.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
:::

#### [Information To Be Included in a Release or Anticipated Release Report --- Road, Rail or Marine]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1229876 .Subheading}

**[[8.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.5 .sectionLabel}** A release or
anticipated release report referred to in section 8.4 must include the
following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of the person making
  the report;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the
  date, time and geographic location of the release;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an anticipated release of dangerous
  goods, the date, time and geographic location of the incident that led
  to the anticipated release;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the mode of transport used;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous
  goods;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of dangerous goods that was in the means
  of containment before the release or anticipated release;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the
  quantity of dangerous goods estimated to have been released;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the type of incident leading to the
  release or anticipated release, including a collision, rollover,
  derailment, overfill, fire, explosion or load-shift;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the name and geographic location of
  any road, main railway line or main waterway that was closed;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} a description of the means of containment containing
  the dangerous goods;

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, an estimate of the number of people
  evacuated or sheltered in place; and

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the number of deaths and the number of
  persons who sustained injuries that required immediate medical
  treatment by a health care provider.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
:::

#### [30-Day Follow-up Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1229892 .Subheading}

**[[8.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.6 .sectionLabel}** A person who has made a
report referred to in section 8.4, or the person's employer, must make a
follow-up report in writing to the Minister within 30 days after the day
on which the report was made.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
- SOR/2019-101, s. 24
:::

#### [Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1229896 .Subheading}

**[[8.7]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.7 .sectionLabel}** A follow-up report
referred to in section 8.6 must include the following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of the person making
  the report;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the names and contact information of the consignor,
  consignee and carrier;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the
  date, time and geographic location of the release;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an anticipated release of dangerous
  goods, the date, time and geographic location of the incident that led
  to the anticipated release;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the mode of transport used;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the classification of the dangerous goods;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of dangerous goods that was in the means
  of containment before the release or anticipated release;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the
  quantity of dangerous goods estimated to have been released;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} a description of the means of containment containing
  the dangerous goods;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, a description of any failure of or
  damage to the means of containment;

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} information about the events leading to the release
  or anticipated release of dangerous goods;

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} information as to whether there was an explosion or
  fire;

- [(m)]{.lawlabel} the name and geographic location of any facility used
  in the loading or unloading of the dangerous goods that was closed,
  and the duration of the closure;

- [(n)]{.lawlabel} the name and geographic location of any road, main
  railway line or main waterway that was closed, and the duration of the
  closure;

- [(o)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, an estimate of the number of people
  evacuated or sheltered in place and the duration of the evacuation or
  shelter in place;

- [(p)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the number of deaths and the number of
  persons who sustained injuries that required immediate medical
  treatment by a health care provider;

- [(q)]{.lawlabel} the ERAP reference number, if applicable, and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the name of the person who was required to have the
    ERAP under subsection 7(1) of the Act, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the date and time that the ERAP incident report
    referred to in section 8.20 was made;

- [(r)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the report referred to in section
  8.4 was made; and

- [(s)]{.lawlabel} an estimate of any financial loss incurred as a
  result of the release or anticipated release, and any emergency
  response cost or remediation costs related to it.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
- SOR/2019-101, s. 10
:::

#### [30-Day Follow-up Report --- Notice and Retention of Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1229921 .Subheading}

- **[[8.8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.8 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person who has made a follow-up report referred to in section 8.6
  must, as soon as possible, notify the Minister of any change to the
  information referred to in paragraph 8.7(f), (i), (j), (k), (l), (p)
  or (s) that occurs within one year after the day on which the
  follow-up report was made.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The person must keep a copy of the report for two
  years after the day on which it is made.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The person must make the report available to an
  inspector within 15 days after the day on which the person receives a
  written request from the inspector.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
- SOR/2019-101, s. 24
:::

### [Air Reports]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1229928 .Subheading}

#### [Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report --- Air]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1229929 .Subheading}

- **[[8.9]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.9
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), a person
  who is required by subsection 18(1) of the Act to report a release or
  anticipated release of dangerous goods that are being offered for
  transport, handled or transported at an aerodrome, at an air cargo
  facility or by aircraft must as soon as possible after a release or
  anticipated release, make a report if the dangerous goods are, or
  could be, in excess of the quantity set out in the following table:

  <figure id="1229932">
  <table
  class="table table-hover table-striped tablePointsize8 topdouble topbot">
  <thead>
  <tr class="topdouble">
  <th class="noBorderRight borderBottom top" scope="col">Class</th>
  <th class="borderBottom top" scope="col">Quantity</th>
  </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
  <tr>
  <td class="noBorderRight noBorderBottom">1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 or 9</td>
  <td class="noBorderBottom">Any quantity</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
  <td class="noBorderRight">7</td>
  <td>A level of ionizing radiation greater than the level established in
  section 39 of the <a href="/eng/regulations/SOR-2015-145">Packaging and
  Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations, 2015</a></td>
  </tr>
  </tbody>
  </table>
  <figcaption><p>TABLE</p></figcaption>
  </figure>

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The report referred to in subsection (1) must be made
  to CANUTEC, at 1-888-CANUTEC (1-888-226-8832) or 613-996-6666, and, in
  the case of dangerous goods included in Class 7, Radioactive
  Materials, to the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The person is not required to make the report
  referred to in subsection (1) if the release or anticipated release
  does not result in any of the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the death or injury of a person;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} damage to property or to the environment;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} signs that the integrity of a means of containment
    has been compromised, including signs of fire, of breakage or of
    fluid or radiation leakage;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} serious jeopardy to persons on an aircraft or to
    the aircraft itself;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} an evacuation of people or their shelter in place;
    or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the closure of an aerodrome, air cargo facility or
    runway.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
:::

#### [Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report --- Air]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1229948 .Subheading}

**[[8.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.10 .sectionLabel}** A report referred to
in section 8.9 must include the following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of the person making
  the report;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the
  date, time and geographic location of the release;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an anticipated release of dangerous
  goods, the date, time and geographic location of the incident that led
  to the anticipated release;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the name of the aircraft operator, aerodrome or air
  cargo facility;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous
  goods;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of dangerous goods that was in the means
  of containment before the release or anticipated release;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the
  quantity of dangerous goods estimated to have been released;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the type of incident leading to the
  release or anticipated release;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} a description of the means of containment containing
  the dangerous goods;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the number of deaths and the number of
  persons who sustained injuries; and

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, an estimate of the number of people
  evacuated or sheltered in place.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
:::

#### [30-Day Follow-up Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1229963 .Subheading}

**[[8.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.11 .sectionLabel}** A person who has made
a report referred to in section 8.9, or the person's employer, must make
a follow-up report in writing to the Minister within 30 days after the
day on which the report was made.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
- SOR/2019-101, s. 24
:::

#### [Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1229967 .Subheading}

**[[8.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.12 .sectionLabel}** A follow-up report
referred to in section 8.11 must include the following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of the person making
  the report;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the names and contact information of the consignor,
  consignee and aircraft operator;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the
  date, time and geographic location of the release;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an anticipated release of dangerous
  goods, the date, time and geographic location of the incident that led
  to the anticipated release;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the classification of the dangerous goods;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of dangerous goods that was in the means
  of containment before the release or anticipated release;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the
  quantity of dangerous goods estimated to have been released;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} a description of the means of containment containing
  the dangerous goods;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, a description of any failure of or
  damage to the means of containment;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} information about the events leading to the release
  or anticipated release of dangerous goods;

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} information as to whether there was an explosion or
  fire;

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} the name and geographic location of any aerodrome,
  air cargo facility or runway that was closed, and the duration of the
  closure;

- [(m)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, an estimate of the number of people
  evacuated or sheltered in place, and the duration of the evacuation or
  shelter in place;

- [(n)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the number of deaths and the number of
  persons who sustained injuries;

- [(o)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the ERAP reference number;

- [(p)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the report referred to in section
  8.9 was made;

- [(q)]{.lawlabel} an estimate of any financial loss incurred as a
  result of the release or anticipated release, and any emergency
  response costs or remediation costs related to it;

- [(r)]{.lawlabel} a description of the route by which the dangerous
  goods were to be transported, including the names of any aerodromes
  along the route;

- [(s)]{.lawlabel} a description of any serious jeopardy to persons on
  any aircraft or to the aircraft itself; and

- [(t)]{.lawlabel} a description of any damage to property or to the
  environment.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
:::

#### [30-Day Follow-up Report --- Notice and Retention of Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1229991 .Subheading}

- **[[8.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.13 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person who has made a follow-up report referred to in section 8.11
  must, as soon as possible, notify the Minister of any change to the
  information referred to in paragraph 8.12(e), (h), (i), (k), (n)
  or (q) that occurs within one year after the day on which the
  follow-up report was made.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The person must keep a copy of the report for two
  years after the day on which it is made.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The person must make the report available to an
  inspector within 15 days after the day on which the person receives a
  written request from the inspector.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
- SOR/2019-101, s. 24
:::

#### [Undeclared or Misdeclared Dangerous Goods Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1229998 .Subheading}

**[[8.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.14 .sectionLabel}** A person must make a
report to CANUTEC, at 1-888-CANUTEC (1-888-226-8832) or 613-996-6666, as
soon as possible after discovering, at an aerodrome or air cargo
facility or on board an aircraft, dangerous goods that are not
accompanied by the documentation or dangerous goods marks set out for
the dangerous goods in Parts 1 to 6 and 8 of the ICAO Technical
Instructions.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
:::

#### [Information To Be Included in an Undeclared or Misdeclared Dangerous Goods Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230002 .Subheading}

**[[8.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.15 .sectionLabel}** A report referred to
in section 8.14 must include the following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of the person making
  the report;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name of the aircraft operator, aerodrome or air
  cargo facility;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the names and contact information of the consignor
  and consignee;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the date of the discovery of the dangerous goods;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous
  goods;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} a description of the means of containment containing
  the dangerous goods;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the gross mass or capacity of the means of
  containment and, if applicable, the total number of means of
  containment; and

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} a description of the route by which the dangerous
  goods were to be transported, including the names of any aerodromes
  along the route.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
:::

#### [Dangerous Goods Occurrence Report (ICAO)]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230014 .Subheading}

**[[8.15.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.15.1 .sectionLabel}** A person must
make a dangerous goods occurrence report (ICAO) to the Minister within
seven days after discovering, at an aerodrome or air cargo facility or
on board an aircraft, dangerous goods that have been transported on
board an aircraft without

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} being loaded, segregated or secured in accordance
  with Chapter 2 of Part 7 of the ICAO Technical Instructions; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command having been informed in
  accordance with section 7;4.1 of the ICAO Technical Instructions.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-137, s. 55
- SOR/2019-101, s. 24
:::

#### [Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Occurrence Report (ICAO)]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230020 .Subheading}

**[[8.15.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.15.2 .sectionLabel}** A dangerous goods
occurrence report (ICAO) referred to in section 8.15.1 must be in
writing and include the following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of the person making
  the report;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name of the aircraft operator, aerodrome or air
  cargo facility;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the names and contact information of the consignor
  and consignee;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the date of the discovery of the occurrence referred
  to in paragraph 8.15.1(a) or (b);

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous
  goods;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} a description of the means of containment containing
  the dangerous goods;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the gross mass or capacity of the means of
  containment and, if applicable, the total number of means of
  containment;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} a description of the route by which the dangerous
  goods were, or were to be, transported, including the names of any
  aerodromes along the route; and

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} a detailed description of the circumstances that led
  to the discovery of the occurrence referred to in paragraph 8.15.1(a)
  or (b), as the case may be.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-137, s. 55
:::

### [Security Reports]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230033 .Subheading}

#### [Loss or Theft Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230034 .Subheading}

- **[[8.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.16 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person who is required by subsection 18(3) of the Act to report the
  loss or theft of dangerous goods must, as soon as possible after the
  loss or theft, report it by telephone to the persons listed in
  subsection (3) if the lost or stolen dangerous goods are in excess of
  the quantity set out in subsection (2).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), the quantities of
  dangerous goods are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any quantity, in the case of the following
    dangerous goods:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} UN1261, NITROMETHANE,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} UN1357, UREA NITRATE, WETTED, with not less than
      20% water, by mass,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} UN1485, POTASSIUM CHLORATE,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} UN1486, POTASSIUM NITRATE,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} UN1487, POTASSIUM NITRATE AND SODIUM NITRITE
      MIXTURE,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} UN1489, POTASSIUM PERCHLORATE,

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} UN1495, SODIUM CHLORATE,

    - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} UN1498, SODIUM NITRATE,

    - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} UN1499, SODIUM NITRATE AND POTASSIUM NITRATE
      MIXTURE,

    - [(x)]{.lawlabel} UN1511, UREA HYDROGEN PEROXIDE,

    - [(xi)]{.lawlabel} UN1796, NITRATING ACID MIXTURE with more than
      50% nitric acid,

    - [(xii)]{.lawlabel} UN1826, NITRATING ACID MIXTURE, SPENT, with
      more than 50% nitric acid,

    - [(xiii)]{.lawlabel} UN1942, AMMONIUM NITRATE with not more than
      0.2% combustible substances, including any organic substance
      calculated as carbon, to the exclusion of any other added
      substance,

    - [(xiv)]{.lawlabel} UN2014, HYDROGEN PEROXIDE, AQUEOUS SOLUTION
      with not less than 20% but not more than 60% hydrogen peroxide
      (stabilized as necessary),

    - [(xv)]{.lawlabel} UN2015, HYDROGEN PEROXIDE, AQUEOUS SOLUTION,
      STABILIZED with more than 60% hydrogen peroxide, or HYDROGEN
      PEROXIDE, STABILIZED,

    - [(xvi)]{.lawlabel} UN2031, NITRIC ACID, other than red fuming,

    - [(xvii)]{.lawlabel} UN2032, NITRIC ACID, RED FUMING,

    - [(xviii)]{.lawlabel} UN3149, HYDROGEN PEROXIDE AND PEROXYACETIC
      ACID MIXTURE with acid(s), water and not more than 5% peroxyacetic
      acid, STABILIZED, and

    - [(xix)]{.lawlabel} UN3370, UREA NITRATE, WETTED, with not less
      than 10% water by mass;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any quantity, in the case of dangerous goods in the
    following primary and subsidiary classes:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} explosives included in Class 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} toxic gases included in Class 2.3,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} organic peroxides included in Class 5.2, Type
      B, liquid or solid, temperature controlled,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} toxic substances included in Class 6.1 and
      Packing Group I,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} infectious substances included in Class 6.2, and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} radioactive materials included in Class 7; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a total quantity of 450 kg or more, in the case of
    dangerous goods in the following primary and subsidiary classes:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} explosives included in Class 1.4 (except for
      1.4S), 1.5 or 1.6,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} flammable gases included in Class 2.1,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} flammable liquids included in Class 3,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} desensitized explosives included in Class 3 or
      4.1,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} substances liable to spontaneous combustion,
      pyrophoric solids or liquids, included in Class 4.2 and Packing
      Group I or II,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} water-reactive substances included in Class 4.3
      and Packing Group I or II,

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} oxidizing substances included in Class 5.1 and
      Packing Group I or II, and

    - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} corrosives included in Class 8 and Packing
      Group I or II.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), the persons to
  whom the report must be made are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} CANUTEC, at 1-888-CANUTEC (1-888-226-8832) or
    613-996-6666;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of dangerous goods included in Class 1,
    Explosives, or referred to in paragraph (2)(a) or subparagraph
    (2)(b)(i) or (c)(i), a Natural Resources Canada inspector, at
    613-995-5555; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of dangerous goods included in Class 7,
    Radioactive Materials, the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A person who made the report referred to in
  subsection (1) must notify the persons referred to in subsection (3)
  if that person finds the dangerous goods that were lost or stolen.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
- SOR/2017-137, s. 56(F)
:::

#### [Information To Be Included in a Loss or Theft Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230081 .Subheading}

**[[8.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.17 .sectionLabel}** A loss or theft
report referred to in section 8.16 must include the following
information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of the person making
  the report;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the names and contact information of the consignor,
  the consignee and the carrier;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} information as to whether the dangerous goods were
  lost or stolen;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name or UN number of the lost or stolen
  dangerous goods;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of the lost or stolen dangerous goods;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} a description of the means of containment containing
  the lost or stolen dangerous goods; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the approximate date, time and geographic location of
  the loss or theft.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
:::

#### [Unlawful Interference Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230092 .Subheading}

- **[[8.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.18 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  there has been unlawful interference with dangerous goods while they
  were being imported, offered for transport, handled or transported,
  the person who had the charge, management or control of the goods
  must, as soon as possible after the discovery of the unlawful
  interference, report it by telephone to the persons listed in
  subsection (2).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), the persons to
  whom the unlawful interference must be reported are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} CANUTEC, at 1-888-CANUTEC (1-888-226-8832) or
    613-996-6666;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of dangerous goods included in Class 1,
    Explosives, or referred to in paragraph 8.16(2)(a) or subparagraph
    8.16(2)(b)(i) or (c)(i), a Natural Resources Canada inspector, at
    613-995-5555; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of dangerous goods included in Class 7,
    Radioactive Materials, the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
:::

#### [Information To Be Included in an Unlawful Interference Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230101 .Subheading}

**[[8.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.19 .sectionLabel}** A report referred to
in section 8.18 must include the following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of the person making
  the report;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the names and contact information of the consignor,
  the consignee and the carrier;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a detailed description of the unlawful interference;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous
  goods;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a description of the means of containment containing
  the dangerous goods, and the number of means of containment; and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the approximate date, time and geographic location of
  the unlawful interference.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 10
:::

### [ERAP Reports]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230111 .Subheading}

#### [ERAP Incident Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230112 .Subheading}

**[[8.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.20 .sectionLabel}** A person who is
required under subsection 18(1) of the Act to report a release or
anticipated release of dangerous goods in respect of which an approved
ERAP is required under subsection 7(1) of the Act must, as soon as
possible after the release or anticipated release, make an ERAP incident
report by telephone to the person at the ERAP telephone number required
to be included on the shipping document under paragraph 3.6(1)(b), if
the dangerous goods are, or could be, in excess of the quantity set out
in the following table:

<figure id="1230114">
<table
class="table table-hover table-striped tablePointsize8 topdouble topbot">
<thead>
<tr class="topdouble">
<th class="noBorderRight borderBottom top" scope="col">Class</th>
<th class="borderBottom top" scope="col">Quantity</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="noBorderRight noBorderBottom">1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 or 8</td>
<td class="noBorderBottom">Any quantity</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="noBorderRight">7</td>
<td>A level of ionizing radiation greater than the level established in
section 39 of the <a href="/eng/regulations/SOR-2015-145">Packaging and
Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations, 2015</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<figcaption><p>TABLE</p></figcaption>
</figure>

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2019-101, s. 11
:::

#### [Information To Be Included in an ERAP Incident Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230122 .Subheading}

**[[8.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.21 .sectionLabel}** An ERAP incident
report referred to in section 8.20 must include the following
information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of the person making
  the report;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the ERAP reference number;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the
  date, time and geographic location of the release;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an anticipated release of dangerous
  goods, the date, time and geographic location of the incident that led
  to the anticipated release;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the mode of transport used;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous
  goods;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of dangerous goods that was in the means
  of containment before the release or anticipated release;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a release, the quantity of dangerous
  goods estimated to have been released;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} a description of the means of containment containing
  the dangerous goods;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} an indication of whether a means of containment has
  been damaged to the extent that its integrity could be compromised;

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} an indication of whether a transfer of the dangerous
  goods to another means of containment is anticipated or required; and

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the type of incident leading to the
  release or anticipated release, including a collision, rollover,
  derailment, overfill, fire, explosion or load-shift.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2019-101, s. 11
:::

#### [ERAP Implementation Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230138 .Subheading}

**[[8.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.22 .sectionLabel}** Each time a person
implements an approved ERAP to tier 1 or tier 2, the person must, as
soon as possible, make an ERAP implementation report to CANUTEC, at
1-888-CANUTEC (1-888‑226‑8832) or 613‑996‑6666.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2019-101, s. 11
:::

#### [Information To Be Included in an ERAP Implementation Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230142 .Subheading}

**[[8.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8.23 .sectionLabel}** An ERAP
implementation report referred to in section 8.22 must include the
following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of the person making
  the report;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the ERAP reference number;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the person authorized under subsection
  7.7(1) to use the ERAP;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} whether the ERAP was implemented to tier 1 or 2;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the date and time that the ERAP was implemented to
  tier 1 or 2;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous goods
  in relation to which the ERAP was implemented; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the measures taken to respond to the release or
  anticipated release.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2019-101, s. 11
:::

## [PART 9]{.HLabel1}[Road]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1230153 .Part}

### [Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230154 .Subheading}

- **[[9.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-9.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite the requirements in Part 2
  (Classification), Part 3 (Documentation) and Part 4 (Dangerous Goods
  Safety Marks), a person may handle or transport dangerous goods by
  road vehicle from a place in the United States to a place in Canada or
  from a place in the United States through Canada to a place outside
  Canada in accordance with the classification, marking, labelling,
  placarding and documentation requirements of 49 CFR, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the information required on the shipping document
    is easy to identify, legible, in indelible print, in English or
    French and includes

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} when dangerous goods are transported to a place
      in Canada, the name and address of the place of business in Canada
      of the consignor,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} when dangerous goods are transported from a
      place in the United States through Canada to a place outside
      Canada, the name and the address of the place of business of each
      consignor, except that in this case the name and address may be
      shown on a separate document attached to the shipping document and
      is required only while that person is the consignor,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the classification in Schedule 1 or in the UN
      Recommendations, for dangerous goods that have the letter "D"
      assigned to them in column 1 of the table to section 172.101 of
      49 CFR, except for dangerous goods with the shipping name
      "Consumer commodity", and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the information relating to the
      approved ERAP referred to in subsection 3.6(1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person complies with the following sections in
    Part 3 (Documentation):

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 3.2, Carrier responsibilities,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} section 3.7, Location of a shipping document:
      road, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} section 3.10, Location of a shipping document:
      storage in the course of transportation; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} on or after August 31, 2008, the labels and
    placards displayed for dangerous goods included in Class 2.3 or
    Class 6.1 are the labels and placards required in these Regulations
    for the dangerous goods. The labels and placards may be displayed
    before August 31, 2008.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply to dangerous goods that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} are forbidden for transport by these Regulations;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} are not regulated by 49 CFR but are regulated by
    these Regulations; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2017-137, s. 57\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} are given dangerous goods safety mark or packaging
    exceptions in 49 CFR that are not permitted by these Regulations.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person who handles or transports dangerous goods by
  road vehicle in accordance with an exemption issued under Subpart B of
  Part 107 of 49 CFR may do so from a place in the United States to a
  place in Canada or from a place in the United States through Canada to
  a place outside Canada if the exemption number appears on the shipping
  document.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If there is a conflict between the requirements of
  Part 2 (Classification), Part 3 (Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous
  Goods Safety Marks) or Part 5 (Means of Containment) and an exemption
  referred to in subsection (3), the exemption prevails to the extent of
  the conflict.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 31
- SOR/2008-34, s. 78
- SOR/2017-137, s. 57
- SOR/2019-101, s. 12
:::

### [Transporting Dangerous Goods to or from an Aircraft, an Aerodrome or an Air Cargo Facility]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230176 .Subheading}

- **[[9.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-9.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite the requirements in Part 2
  (Classification), Part 3 (Documentation), and Part 4 (Dangerous Goods
  Safety Marks), if transport has been or is to be by aircraft, a person
  may handle or transport dangerous goods by road vehicle to or from an
  aircraft, an aerodrome or an air cargo facility in accordance with the
  classification, marking, labelling, and documentation requirements of
  the ICAO Technical Instructions, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the information required on the shipping document
    is easy to identify, legible, in indelible print, in English or
    French and includes, if applicable, the information relating to the
    approved ERAP referred to in subsection 3.6(1); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person complies with the following provisions
    in Part 3 (Documentation):

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 3.2, Carrier responsibilities,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 3.5(1)(f) and subsection 3.5(2),
      concerning a 24-hour number on a shipping document,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} section 3.7, Location of a shipping document:
      road, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} section 3.10, Location of a shipping document:
      storage in the course of transportation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply if these Regulations
  forbid the transport of the dangerous goods or if the dangerous goods
  are not regulated by the ICAO Technical Instructions but are regulated
  by these Regulations.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} When dangerous goods are transported to or from an
  aircraft, an aerodrome or an air cargo facility, by a road vehicle,
  the road vehicle, or any means of containment visible from outside the
  road vehicle, must have placards displayed on it in accordance with
  Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 32
- SOR/2008-34, s. 79
- SOR/2019-101, s. 13
:::

### [Transporting Dangerous Goods to or from a Vessel, a Port Facility or a Marine Terminal]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230189 .Subheading}

- **[[9.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-9.3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite the requirements in Part 2
  (Classification), Part 3 (Documentation), and Part 4 (Dangerous Goods
  Safety Marks), if transport has been or is to be by vessel, a person
  may handle or transport by road vehicle an international consignment
  of dangerous goods to or from a vessel, a port facility or a marine
  terminal in accordance with the classification, marking, labelling,
  placarding and documentation requirements of the IMDG Code if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the information required on the shipping document
    is easy to identify, legible, in indelible print, in English or
    French and includes, if applicable, the information relating to the
    approved ERAP referred to in subsection 3.6(1); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person complies with the following provisions
    in Part 3 (Documentation):

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 3.2, Carrier responsibilities,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 3.5(1)(f) and subsection 3.5(2),
      concerning a 24-hour number on a shipping document,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} section 3.7, Location of a shipping document:
      road, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} section 3.10, Location of a shipping document:
      storage in the course of transportation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply if these Regulations
  forbid the transport of the dangerous goods or if the dangerous goods
  are not regulated by the IMDG Code but are regulated by these
  Regulations.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} When dangerous goods are transported in a large means
  of containment to or from a vessel, a port facility or a marine
  terminal, the large means of containment must have placards displayed
  on it in accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) or the
  IMDG Code.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 33
- SOR/2008-34, s. 80
- SOR/2012-245, s. 23
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
- SOR/2019-101, s. 14
:::

### [Reshipping in Canada]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230202 .Subheading}

- **[[9.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-9.4 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When
  a consignment of dangerous goods is transported from a place outside
  Canada to a place in Canada and is reshipped within Canada by road
  vehicle, the dangerous goods safety marks displayed in accordance with
  49 CFR, the ICAO Technical Instructions or the IMDG Code at the time
  of entry into Canada may continue to be displayed, except that the
  large means of containment containing the dangerous goods must have
  placards displayed on it in accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods
  Safety Marks).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The shipping document that accompanies the dangerous
  goods must include a notation that the dangerous goods safety marks
  are in accordance with 49 CFR, the ICAO Technical Instructions or the
  IMDG Code, if they differ from the ones required to be displayed by
  Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2012-245, s. 24
:::

### [Maximum Net Explosives Quantity in a Road Vehicle]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230208 .Subheading}

**[[9.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-9.5 .sectionLabel}** The total net
explosives quantity of all explosives that are transported together in a
road vehicle must be less than or equal to the following limits:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} 25 kg if any of the explosives are UN0190, SAMPLES,
  EXPLOSIVE;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} 2 000 kg if any of the explosives are included in
  Class 1.1A; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} 20 000 kg.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 81
:::

## [PART 10]{.HLabel1}[Rail]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1230215 .Part}

### [Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230216 .Subheading}

- **[[10.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-10.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite the requirements in Part 2
  (Classification), Part 3 (Documentation) and Part 4 (Dangerous Goods
  Safety Marks), a person may handle or transport dangerous goods by
  railway vehicle from a place in the United States to a place in Canada
  or from a place in the United States through Canada to a place outside
  Canada in accordance with the classification, marking, labelling,
  placarding and documentation requirements of 49 CFR if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the information required on the shipping document
    is easy to identify, legible, in indelible print, in English or
    French and includes

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} when dangerous goods are transported to a place
      in Canada, the name and address of the place of business in Canada
      of the consignor,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} when dangerous goods are transported from a
      place in the United States through Canada to a place outside
      Canada, the name and the address of the place of business of each
      consignor, except that in this case the name and address may be
      shown on a separate document attached to the shipping document and
      is required only while that person is the consignor,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the classification in Schedule 1 or in the UN
      Recommendations, for dangerous goods that have the letter "D"
      assigned to them in column 1 of the table to section 172.101 of
      49 CFR, except for dangerous goods with the shipping name
      "Consumer commodity", and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the information relating to the
      approved ERAP referred to in subsection 3.6(1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person complies with the following sections in
    Part 3 (Documentation):

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 3.2, Carrier responsibilities,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} section 3.8, Location of a shipping document and
      consist: rail, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} section 3.10, Location of a shipping document:
      storage in the course of transportation, and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} on or after August 31, 2008, the labels and
    placards displayed for dangerous goods included in Class 2.3 or 6.1
    are the labels and placards required in these Regulations for the
    dangerous goods. The labels or placards may be displayed before
    August 31, 2008.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply to dangerous goods that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} are forbidden for transport by these Regulations;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} are not regulated by 49 CFR but are regulated by
    these Regulations; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2017-137\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} are given dangerous goods safety mark or packaging
    exceptions in 49 CFR that are not permitted by these Regulations.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person who handles or transports dangerous goods by
  railway vehicle in accordance with an exemption issued under Subpart B
  of Part 107 of 49 CFR may do so from a place in the United States to a
  place in Canada or from a place in the United States through Canada to
  a place outside Canada if the exemption number appears on the shipping
  document.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If there is a conflict between the requirements of
  Part 2 (Classification), Part 3 (Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous
  Goods Safety Marks) or Part 5 (Means of Containment) and an exemption
  referred to in subsection (3), the exemption prevails to the extent of
  the conflict.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 34
- SOR/2008-34, s. 83
- SOR/2017-137, s. 58
- replaced, SOR/2019-101, s. 15
:::

### [Railway Vehicle Reciprocity]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230238 .Subheading}

**[[10.1.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-10.1.1 .sectionLabel}** Despite the
requirements of Part 5 (Means of Containment), a person may offer for
transport, handle or transport dangerous goods by railway vehicle from a
place in the United States to a place in Canada or from a place in the
United States through Canada to a place outside Canada in accordance
with the requirements of Parts 172, 173, 174, 179 and 180 of 49 CFR,
except by tank car if the goods are Class 3, Flammable Liquids that are
referred to in section 10.5.6 of TP 14877.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2019-75, s. 10
:::

### [Location of Placarded Railway Vehicle in a Train]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230275 .Subheading}

- **[[10.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-10.6
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless it is likely to have a
  serious impact on train dynamics, a person must not, in a train,
  locate a railway vehicle that contains dangerous goods described in
  column 1 of the table to this subsection for which a placard is
  required to be displayed in accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods
  Safety Marks), next to a railway vehicle described in the same row in
  column 2.

  vehicles in a train from the United States to Canada or from the
  United States through Canada to a place outside Canada may be located
  in the train in accordance with sections 174.84 and 174.85 of 49 CFR.

:::

### [Coupling of Railway Vehicles]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230287 .Subheading}

- **[[10.7]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-10.7 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person must not couple a railway vehicle with another railway vehicle
  at a relative coupling speed greater than 9.6 km/h (6 mph) if either
  of the railway vehicles that make contact on coupling contains
  dangerous goods for which a placard is required to be displayed in
  accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a person may couple a single
  railway vehicle moving under its own momentum at a relative coupling
  speed less than or equal to 12 km/h (7.5 mph) when the ambient
  temperature is above -25ºC.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a person couples a tank car that contains
  dangerous goods for which a placard is required to be displayed in
  accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), with another
  railway vehicle and the three conditions in any one of the four rows
  set out in the table to this subsection apply, the person must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} visually inspect the underframe assembly and
    coupling and cushioning components of the tank car to ensure their
    integrity before the tank car is moved more than 2 km from the place
    where the coupling occurred; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} report, in writing, to the owner of the tank car
    within 10 days after the coupling and include a copy of the text of
    this section and information about any damage that compromises the
    integrity of the underframe assembly or draft gear of the tank car
    discovered as a result of the inspection.
