- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The owner of a tank car who receives the report must
  not use the tank car or permit the tank car to be used to transport
  dangerous goods, other than the dangerous goods that were contained in
  the tank car at the time of the coupling, until the tank car undergoes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a visual inspection and a structural integrity
    inspection in accordance with clause 9.5.6(a) and clause 9.5.7 of
    TP 14877; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for a tank car equipped with a stub sill, a stub
    sill inspection covering at least the following areas:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the termination of the stub sill reinforcement
      pad closest to the mid-point of the tank car and associated welds
      for a 30-cm length from that point back towards the other end of
      the pad,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} all welds

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} connecting the head brace to the stub sill,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} between the head brace and the head
        reinforcement pad, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} between the tank and the head reinforcement pad
        and, if the head reinforcement pad is connected to the stub sill
        reinforcement pad, 2.5 cm past that connection towards the
        centre of the tank,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} all metal of the stub sill assembly, other than
      welds, from the body bolster to the coupler, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the draft gear pocket.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply if either the tank car or
  the other railway vehicle that was coupled is equipped with a
  cushioning device designed for a displacement of 15 cm (6 in.) or more
  in compression and capable of limiting the maximum coupler force to
  4 448 kilonewtons (1,000,000 lbf) when impacted at 16.1 km/h (10 mph)
  by a railway vehicle having a gross mass of 99 790 kg (220,000 lb).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 37
- SOR/2008-34, s. 88
- SOR/2014-152, s. 26
- SOR/2019-75, s. 11
:::

### [Reporting]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230313 .Subheading}

**[[10.8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-10.8 .sectionLabel}** A consignor shall, on
reasonable notice given by the Minister, provide the Minister with the
following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the number of tank cars owned or leased by the
  consignor that meet the requirements of TP 14877 for TC117R tank cars;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of tank cars owned or leased by the
  consignor that meet the requirements of TP 14877 for TC117P tank cars;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the number of tank cars owned or leased by the
  consignor and used for importing, offering for transport or handling
  dangerous goods included in Class 3, Flammable Liquids, that meet the
  requirements of TP 14877 for Class 111 tank cars; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the number of tank cars owned or leased by the
  consignor and used for importing, offering for transport or handling
  dangerous goods included in Class 3, Flammable Liquids, that meet the
  requirements of TP 14877 for enhanced Class 111 tank cars.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2019-75, s. 12
:::

## [PART 11]{.HLabel1}[Marine]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1230321 .Part}

### [Marine Transport --- IMDG Code]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230322 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2017-253, s. 21

\]
:::

- **[[11.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-11.1 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person who imports, offers for transport, handles or transports
  dangerous goods by vessel must comply with the IMDG Code if the
  dangerous goods are in transport between

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} two points in Canada on a voyage during which

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the vessel goes more than 120 nautical miles from
      shore,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} on the Atlantic coast, the vessel goes south of
      the port of New York, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} on the Pacific coast, the vessel goes south of
      Portland, Oregon;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Canada and another country, if the voyage is not an
    inland voyage or a sheltered waters voyage that is within the waters
    described in paragraphs (a) and (b) of the definition [[inland
    voyage]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} in section 1 of the [Vessel Safety
    Certificates Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2021-135); or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} two points outside Canada on board a vessel
    registered in Canada.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In addition to the requirements in subsection (1), a
  person who offers for transport, handles or transports dangerous goods
  by vessel must do so in accordance with the following provisions of
  these Regulations:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the following provisions in Part 3 (Documentation):

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 3.2, Carrier responsibilities,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} subsection 3.4(1), Legibility and language,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 3.5(1)(f) and subsection 3.5(2),
      concerning a 24-hour number on a shipping document,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} section 3.9, Location of a shipping document:
      marine, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} section 3.10, Location of a shipping document:
      storage in the course of transportation;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the following provisions in Part 4 (Dangerous Goods
    Safety Marks):

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 4.2, Misleading dangerous goods safety
      marks,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} section 4.4, Consignor responsibilities,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} subsection 4.5(1), Carrier responsibilities,
      and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} section 4.6, Visibility, legibility and colour;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the following provisions in Part 5 (Means of
    Containment):

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 5.2, Requirements for a standardized
      means of containment to be in standard,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} section 5.3, Compliance marks on a means of
      containment,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} section 5.6, UN standardized means of
      containment, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} section 5.10, Means of containment for Class 2,
      Gases, and section 5.11, UN1950, AEROSOLS, and UN2037, GAS
      CARTRIDGES; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} Part 8 (Reporting Requirements).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The means of containment used to transport the
  dangerous goods must be designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured
  and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including
  handling, there will be no release of the dangerous goods that could
  endanger public safety.

### [Marine Transport --- Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230354 .Subheading}

**[[11.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-11.2 .sectionLabel}** A person who imports,
offers for transport, handles or transports dangerous goods by vessel
must comply with these Regulations if the dangerous goods are in
transport between

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} two points in Canada on a voyage during which the
  vessel is always within 120 nautical miles from shore and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} on the Atlantic coast, the vessel does not go south
    of the port of New York, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} on the Pacific coast, the vessel does not go south
    of Portland, Oregon; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} Canada and another country, if the voyage is an
  inland voyage or a sheltered waters voyage that is within the waters
  described in paragraphs (a) and (b) of the definition [[inland
  voyage]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} in section 1 of the [Vessel Safety
  Certificates Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2021-135).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-253, s. 22

  role="button"}

### [Transporting Dangerous Goods from One Country through Canada to Another Country]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230362 .Subheading}

**[[11.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-11.3 .sectionLabel}** A person who
transports dangerous goods by vessel from one country through Canada to
another country must comply with the IMDG Code and Part 8 (Reporting
Requirements) of these Regulations.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-95, s. 41
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
:::

SOR/2017-253, s. 23\]]{.Repealed}

## [PART 12]{.HLabel1}[Air]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1230367 .Part}

### [International and Domestic Transport by Aircraft]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230368 .Subheading}

#### [General Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230369 .Subheading}

- **[[12.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.1 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person who handles, offers for transport or transports dangerous goods
  by aircraft between Canada and another country must do so in
  accordance with the ICAO Technical Instructions and the following
  provisions of these Regulations:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in Part 1 (Coming into Force, Repeal,
    Interpretation, General Provisions and Special Cases),

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 1.7, Safety requirements, documents,
      safety marks,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} paragraphs 1.8(a) and (b), Prohibition:
      explosives,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2017-137\]]{.Repealed}

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2023-155, s. 46\]]{.Repealed}

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2023-155, s. 46\]]{.Repealed}

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2002-306\]]{.Repealed}

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} section 1.20, National Defence, and

    - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} section 1.43, Class 7, Radioactive Materials;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in Part 2 (Classification),

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 2.2, Responsibility for classification,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} section 2.36, Infectious substances,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} section 2.37, General, Class 7, Radioactive
      Materials, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} subparagraphs 2.43(b)(iv) and (v), concerning
      classifying in Class 9 dangerous goods that are environmentally
      hazardous substances;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in Part 3 (Documentation),

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 3.1, Consignor responsibilities,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} subsections 3.2(1), (2), (3), (5) and (6),
      Carrier responsibilities,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} subsection 3.4(1), Legibility and language,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 3.5(1)(f) and subsection 3.5(2),
      concerning a 24-hour number on a shipping document,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} subsections 3.6(1) and (2), which require the
      ERAP reference number and telephone number on a shipping document,
      and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} section 3.11, Keeping shipping document
      information;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks),

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 4.2, Misleading dangerous goods safety
      marks,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} section 4.4, Consignor responsibilities,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} subsection 4.5(1), Carrier responsibilities,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} subsection 4.7(1), Labels and placards: size and
      orientation, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} section 4.9, Removal of dangerous goods safety
      marks;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in Part 5 (Means of Containment),

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 5.2, Requirements for a standardized
      means of containment to be in standard,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} section 5.3, Certification safety marks on a
      means of containment,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} section 5.6, UN standardized means of
      containment, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} section 5.10, Means of containment for Class 2,
      Gases;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} Part 6 (Training);

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance Plan);

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} Part 8 (Reporting Requirements);

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} Part 13 (Protective Direction); and

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} Part 14 (Permit for Equivalent Level of Safety).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who handles, offers for transport or
  transports dangerous goods by aircraft within Canada must do so in
  accordance with the ICAO Technical Instructions and the provisions of
  these Regulations referred to in subsection (1).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), a person may handle, offer
  for transport or transport dangerous goods by aircraft within Canada
  in accordance with the requirements of sections 12.4 to 12.17.

#### [Shipping Document]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230413 .Subheading}

**[[12.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.2 .sectionLabel}** The shipping document
for dangerous goods transported by aircraft must

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} be completed in accordance with Chapter 4,
  Documentation, of Part 5, Shipper's Responsibilities, of the ICAO
  Technical Instructions; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} show the information required for the dangerous goods
  by the ICAO Technical Instructions on a document that has, on the left
  and right margins, red hatchings that are oriented to the right or to
  the left.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 40
- SOR/2008-34, s. 94
:::

#### [Information to Pilot-in-command]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230419 .Subheading}

**[[12.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.3 .sectionLabel}** Despite subsection
12.1(1), the following text replaces subsection 4.1.6 in section 4.1,
Information to the pilot-in-command, of Chapter 4, Provision of
information, of Part 7, Operator's Responsibilities, of the ICAO
Technical Instructions:

"4.1.6 The information provided to the pilot-in-command must be
presented on a dedicated form and not by means of air waybills,
dangerous goods transport documents, invoices, etc."

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 41
- SOR/2014-152, s. 29
- SOR/2017-253, s. 24
:::

### [Domestic Transport by Aircraft]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230424 .Subheading}

#### [Explosives, Class 1.4S]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230425 .Subheading}

- **[[12.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.4 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person may handle, offer for transport or transport by aircraft within
  Canada explosives included in Class 1.4S if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person complies with the ICAO Technical
    Instructions, other than Part 4, Packing Instructions, and sections
    1.1 to 1.3 of Chapter 1, General, sections 2.1 to 2.4.1 and 2.4.3 to
    2.5 of Chapter 2, Marking, Chapter 3, Labelling, and Chapter 4,
    Documentation, of Part 5, Shipper's Responsibilities;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} when the consignor is not the air carrier, the
    consignor notifies the air carrier of the presence of the explosives
    before offering them for transport;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the explosives are one or more of the explosives
    set out in the following table:

    <figure id="1230431">
    <table
    class="table table-hover table-striped tablePointsize8 topdouble topbot">
    <thead>
    <tr class="topdouble">
    <th class="noBorderRight borderBottom top" scope="col">UN Number</th>
    <th class="borderBottom top" scope="col">Shipping Name</th>
    </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
    <tr>
    <td class="noBorderRight noBorderBottom top">UN0012</td>
    <td class="noBorderBottom top">CARTRIDGES FOR WEAPONS, INERT PROJECTILE,
    or CARTRIDGES, SMALL ARMS</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
    <td class="noBorderRight noBorderBottom top">UN0014</td>
    <td class="noBorderBottom top">CARTRIDGES FOR WEAPONS, BLANK, or
    CARTRIDGES, SMALL ARMS, BLANK, or CARTRIDGES FOR TOOLS, BLANK</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
    <td class="noBorderRight noBorderBottom top">UN0055</td>
    <td class="noBorderBottom top">CASES, CARTRIDGE, EMPTY, WITH PRIMER</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
    <td class="noBorderRight noBorderBottom top">UN0323</td>
    <td class="noBorderBottom top">CARTRIDGES, POWER DEVICE</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
    <td class="noBorderRight top">UN0405</td>
    <td class="top">CARTRIDGES, SIGNAL</td>
    </tr>
    </tbody>
    </table>
    <figcaption><p>TABLE</p></figcaption>
    </figure>

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the calibre of cartridges with the UN number UN0012
    or UN0014 is

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} less than 50 calibres, in the case of cartridges
      for rifles or pistols, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} greater than or equal to 8 gauge, in the case of
      cartridges for shotguns;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the gross mass of each means of containment is less
    than or equal to 25 kg;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the explosives are placed in an inner means of
    containment that is a box, in metal or plastic clips or in
    partitions that fit snugly in an outer means of containment that is
    designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so
    that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there
    will be no accidental release of the dangerous goods that could
    endanger public safety;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the primers are protected from accidental
    initiation; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} each of the outer means of containment is marked
    with the gross mass in kilograms and the words "Explosives ---
    Excepted" or "[Explosifs --- Exceptés]{.otherLang lang="fr"}", in
    letters at least 25 mm high and in a colour that contrasts with the
    background colour of the means of containment.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite the restrictions that apply to item 19 of
  Table 8-1 to Chapter 1, Provisions for dangerous goods carried by
  passengers or crew, of Part 8, Provisions Concerning Passengers and
  Crew, of the ICAO Technical Instructions, ammunition, or ammunition
  loaded in a firearm, with the UN number and shipping name UN0012,
  CARTRIDGES FOR WEAPONS, INERT PROJECTILE or UN0012, CARTRIDGES, SMALL
  ARMS or UN0014, CARTRIDGES FOR WEAPONS, BLANK or UN0014, CARTRIDGES,
  SMALL ARMS, BLANK or UN0014, CARTRIDGES FOR TOOLS, BLANK, may be
  transported on board an aircraft by a [[peace
  officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in section 3 of the
  [Canadian Aviation Security Regulations,
  2012](/eng/regulations/SOR-2011-318), by a Canadian in-flight security
  officer or by a person described in item 22, column 1, of the table to
  subsection 78(2) of the [Canadian Aviation Security Regulations,
  2012](/eng/regulations/SOR-2011-318).

#### [Forbidden Explosives]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230447 .Subheading}

- **[[12.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.5 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person may handle, offer for transport or transport by aircraft within
  Canada explosives that are forbidden for transport in any of columns
  10 to 13 of Table 3-1, Dangerous Goods List, in Chapter 2, Arrangement
  of the dangerous goods list (Table 3-1), of Part 3, Dangerous Goods
  List, Special Provisions and Limited and Excepted Quantities, of the
  ICAO Technical Instructions if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person complies with

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} paragraphs 12.1(1)(a) to (j),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the quantity limits and the packing instructions
      set out in columns 10 to 13 of Table S-3-1, Supplementary
      Dangerous Goods List, in Chapter 2, Supplementary Dangerous Goods
      List (Class 1), of Part S-3, Dangerous Goods List, Special
      Provisions and Quantity Limitations, of the Supplement to the ICAO
      Technical Instructions, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the requirements of the ICAO Technical
      Instructions;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the explosives are

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} UN0030, DETONATORS, ELECTRIC for blasting,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} UN0042, BOOSTERS without detonator,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} UN0059, CHARGES, SHAPED without detonator,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} UN0065, CORD, DETONATING, flexible,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} UN0081, EXPLOSIVE, BLASTING, TYPE A,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} UN0082, EXPLOSIVE, BLASTING, TYPE B,

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} UN0083, EXPLOSIVE, BLASTING, TYPE C,

    - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} UN0084, EXPLOSIVE, BLASTING, TYPE D,

    - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} UN0241, EXPLOSIVE, BLASTING, TYPE E,

    - [(x)]{.lawlabel} UN0331, EXPLOSIVE, BLASTING, TYPE B; or AGENT,
      BLASTING, TYPE B,

    - [(xi)]{.lawlabel} UN0332, EXPLOSIVE, BLASTING TYPE E; or AGENT,
      BLASTING, TYPE E, or

    - [(xii)]{.lawlabel} UN0360, DETONATOR ASSEMBLIES, NON-ELECTRIC for
      blasting;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the explosives

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} are not included in compatibility group A,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} have not deteriorated or been damaged,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} do not have an active means of initiation and
      are not primed for use, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} are in a means of containment that is required
      for them by the packing instructions set out in Chapter 3, Class 1
      --- Explosives, of Part S-4, Packing Instructions, of the
      Supplement to the ICAO Technical Instructions; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} there are no other dangerous goods transported on
    board the aircraft at the same time as the explosives.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The consignor of the explosives must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} notify the air carrier, in writing, of the shipping
    name, UN number, primary class and compatibility group of the
    explosives at least 48 hours before the explosives are loaded on the
    aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} keep a copy of the notification to the air carrier
    for two years after the date the notification is sent to the air
    carrier; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} notify the consignee at least 24 hours before the
    explosives are transported of the expected time of transport unless
    the consignor and the air carrier agree that the air carrier will
    notify the consignee of the expected time of transport when the air
    carrier gives the consignor written agreement to transport the
    explosives.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The air carrier must, at least 24 hours before
  transporting the explosives,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} give the consignor written agreement to transport
    the explosives and keep a copy of this agreement for two years after
    the date the notification referred to in paragraph (2)(a) is sent to
    the consignor; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} notify each aerodrome operator listed on the flight
    plan of the intended time of departure, arrival and technical stops,
    if any.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The notification referred to in paragraph (2)(a) and
  the agreement referred to in paragraph (3)(a) are valid for any
  subsequent transport of the explosives for two years beginning on the
  date that the notification and the agreement were made unless any of
  the information required in them changes.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 43
- SOR/2014-152, s. 31
- SOR/2017-253, s. 26
:::

SOR/2017-253, s. 27\]]{.Repealed}

#### [Packing Instruction Y963]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230485 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2014-152, s. 32

\]
:::

- **[[12.8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.8 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person may handle, offer for transport or transport by aircraft within
  Canada dangerous goods that are aerosols included in Class 2.1 or 2.2,
  are UN3175, SOLIDS CONTAINING FLAMMABLE LIQUID, N.O.S., or are
  included in Class 3 and Packing Group II or III or in Class 6.1 and
  Packing Group III, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person complies with

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} paragraphs 12.1(1)(a) to (j), and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the ICAO Technical Instructions, other than
      Chapter 2, Markings, Chapter 3, Labelling, and Chapter 4,
      Documentation, of Part 5, Shipper's Responsibilities, and
      paragraphs (j) and (l) of Packing Instruction Y963 of Chapter 11,
      Class 9 --- Miscellaneous dangerous goods, of Part 4, Packing
      Instructions;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} when the dangerous goods are liquid,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the quantity for Class 3, Packing Group II, is
      less than or equal to

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} 1 L in a metal inner means of containment,
        except for UN1263, PAINT or PAINT RELATED MATERIAL, in which
        case the quantity may be less than or equal to 5 L, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} 500 mL in a glass, earthenware or plastic inner
        means of containment, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the quantity for Class 3, Packing Group III, and
      for Class 6.1, Packing Group III, is less than or equal to

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} 5 L in a metal inner means of containment, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} 500 mL in a glass, earthenware or plastic inner
        means of containment; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} when the dangerous goods are solid, the quantity is
    less than or equal to 5 kg in an inner means of containment.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The person who offers for transport the dangerous
  goods must, on each small means of containment that contains the
  dangerous goods,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} mark the words "Air Transport, 12.8, Consumer
    commodity" or "[Transport aérien, 12.8, produit de
    consommation]{.otherLang lang="fr"}" in letters at least 25 mm high
    and in a colour that contrasts with the background colour of the
    means of containment; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for liquids, except flammable liquids in a quantity
    less than or equal to 120 mL, display on two opposite sides of the
    means of containment a package orientation label illustrated in
    Figure 5-29 of Chapter 3, Labelling, of Part 5, Shipper's
    Responsibilities, of the ICAO Technical Instructions.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), the dangerous goods safety
  marks that are required by that subsection to be marked or displayed
  on a small means of containment are not required to be marked or
  displayed on a small means of containment that is inside another small
  means of containment if the other small means of containment is not
  opened during loading or unloading or while the dangerous goods are in
  transport.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 46
- SOR/2003-273, s. 9
- SOR/2017-253, s. 28
:::

#### [Limited Access]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230507 .Subheading}

##### [General]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1230508 .Subheading}

- **[[12.9]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.9 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  air carrier may handle, offer for transport or transport by aircraft
  within Canada the dangerous goods referred to in subsections (2)
  to (12) if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air carrier complies with subsections (2) to
    (14);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air carrier complies with the following
    requirements in the ICAO Technical Instructions:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} wherever practicable, section 5.1, Information to
      passengers, of Chapter 5, Provisions concerning passengers and
      crew, of Part 7, Operator's Responsibilities,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} section 2.4, Loading and securing of dangerous
      goods, and section 2.5, Damaged packages of dangerous goods, of
      Chapter 2, Storage and loading, of Part 7, Operator's
      Responsibilities,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} section 3.1, Inspection for damage or leakage,
      of Chapter 3, Inspection and decontamination, of Part 7,
      Operator's Responsibilities,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} when the person loading or supervising the
      loading of the dangerous goods on board the aircraft is not a crew
      member,

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} section 4.1, Information to the
        pilot-in-command, except for packing group, number of packages
        and identification of the aerodrome, of Chapter 4, Provision of
        information, of Part 7, Operator's Responsibilities, and

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} in the case of dangerous goods transported by
        helicopter, the information required in clause (A) is provided
        to a person identified in the air carrier's Operations Manual
        rather than the pilot-in-command,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} section 4.2, Information to be provided to
      employees, of Chapter 4, Provision of information, of Part 7,
      Operator's Responsibilities,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} wherever practicable, section 4.8, Cargo
      acceptance areas --- provision of information, of Chapter 4,
      Provision of information, of Part 7, Operator's Responsibilities,
      and

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} Table 7-1, "Segregation between packages", of
      Chapter 2, Storage and loading, of Part 7, Operator's
      Responsibilities;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} transported by cargo aircraft or passenger
      carrying aircraft referred to in Subpart 4 of Part VI and Subparts
      1 to 4 of Part VII of the [Canadian Aviation
      Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-96-433),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} transported to or from a location where access
      is limited and there is no other practical or readily available
      means of transport to transport the dangerous goods, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} contained in a means of containment that has
      displayed on it the package markings and labels required by
      Chapter 2, Marking, except for section 2.4.2, and required by
      Chapter 3, Labelling, except for section 3.2.12, of Part 5,
      Shipper's Responsibilities, of the ICAO Technical Instructions;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} when the dangerous goods are Class 2.1, Flammable
    Gases, or Class 3, Flammable Liquids, smoking is prohibited on board
    the aircraft and the aircraft and each area or compartment of the
    aircraft containing the dangerous goods is ventilated to prevent the
    accumulation of vapours;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} when the dangerous goods are transported on a
    passenger carrying aircraft, where practicable, they are secured in
    an area of the aircraft so that they are not readily accessible to
    the passengers;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the person who handles, offers for transport or
    transports the dangerous goods is trained in accordance with Part 6
    (Training) of these Regulations and Chapter 4, Training, of Part 1,
    General, of the ICAO Technical Instructions; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the person who has possession of the dangerous
    goods complies with Part 8 (Reporting Requirements) of these
    Regulations.

###### [Class 3, Flammable Liquids]{.HTitleText4} {#class-3-flammable-liquids-1 .SchedHeadL4}

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The requirements in subsections (3) to (6) apply to
  dangerous goods that are included in Class 3, Flammable Liquids, and
  that are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} UN1202, GAS OIL or DIESEL FUEL or HEATING OIL,
    LIGHT;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} UN1203, GASOLINE or MOTOR SPIRIT or PETROL;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} UN1219, ISOPROPANOL or ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} UN1223, KEROSENE;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} UN1268, PETROLEUM DISTILLATES, N.O.S., or PETROLEUM
    PRODUCTS, N.O.S., Packing Groups II and III only; or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} UN1863, FUEL, AVIATION, TURBINE ENGINE, Packing
    Groups II and III only.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} When the Class 3, Flammable Liquids, referred to in
  subsection (2) are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} contained in a small means of containment that is a
    drum, the drum must be securely closed and marked with one of the
    following manufacturer's permanent markings when the drum has a
    capacity greater than 25 L and less than or equal to 230 L: TC, CTC,
    DOT, ICC 5A, 5B, 5C, 17C, 17E, TC-34, CTC-34, DOT-34, UN 1A1, UN
    1B1, UN 1H1 or UN 6HA; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} contained in a small means of containment that is
    not a drum, the small means of containment must be securely closed
    and

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} marked with one of the following manufacturer's
      permanent markings when the small means of containment has a
      capacity less than or equal to 25 L: UN 3A1, UN 3H1, UL or ULC,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} marked in accordance with ASTM F 852, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} an unmarked steel marine fuel tank of a type
      that is used to supply fuel for an outboard motor.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The following means of containment may be reused to
  transport the Class 3, Flammable Liquids, referred to in subsection
  (2):

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a steel drum or jerrican, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} neither the body nor the top or bottom of the
      drum or jerrican is damaged by wear, scoring, dents or corrosion
      to the extent that the integrity of the drum or the jerrican is
      compromised,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any worn or leaking bung caps or seals are
      replaced,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the top and bottom of the drum are not bulging,
      and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} sufficient ullage is left to ensure that no
      leakage or permanent distortion will occur as a result of
      expansion of the liquid caused by any temperature that may be
      experienced during transport;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a plastic drum or jerrican, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the body of the drum or jerrican is not faded,
      discoloured, gouged, cracked or distorted to the extent that the
      integrity of the drum or jerrican is compromised,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the closure flange and bung of the drum show no
      evidence of cross-threading or thread wear,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} any worn gaskets are replaced, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} when the capacity of the jerrican exceeds 25 L,
      it is used only for flammable liquids that are included in Packing
      Group III and that have a flash point greater than 37.8°C; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a steel marine fuel tank, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} neither the body nor the bottom chimes of the
      tank is damaged by wear, scoring, dents or corrosion to the extent
      that the integrity of the tank is compromised,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any worn or leaking caps, attachments or seals
      are replaced, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} sufficient ullage is left to ensure that no
      leakage or permanent distortion will occur as a result of
      expansion of the liquid caused by any temperature that may be
      experienced during transport.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} When the Class 3, Flammable Liquids, referred to in
  subsection (2) are contained in a large means of containment, that
  large means of containment must be

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a tank, a container or an apparatus that is an
    integral part of the aircraft or that is attached to the aircraft in
    accordance with the Certificate of Airworthiness issued under the
    [Canadian Aviation Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-96-433);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a cylindrical collapsible rubber drum that is
    transported in or suspended from an aircraft and that is
    constructed, tested, inspected and used in accordance with
    MIL-D-23119G; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a collapsible fabric tank that is transported
    suspended from a helicopter and that is constructed of material and
    seamed in accordance with MIL-T-52983G.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} When the Class 3, Flammable Liquids, referred to in
  subsection (2) are transported

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} on board a passenger carrying aircraft, the total
    capacity of all the means of containment must be less than or equal
    to 230 L; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on board a cargo aircraft, the total capacity of
    each of the means of containment must be less than or equal to 230 L
    except for those means of containment referred to in subsection (5).

###### [Internal Combustion Engines, Vehicles and Machinery]{.HTitleText4} {#internal-combustion-engines-vehicles-and-machinery .SchedHeadL4}

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} Dangerous goods that are UN3166, VEHICLE, FLAMMABLE
  GAS POWERED or UN3166, VEHICLE, FLAMMABLE LIQUID POWERED or UN3166,
  VEHICLE, FUEL CELL, FLAMMABLE GAS POWERED or UN3166, VEHICLE, FUEL
  CELL, FLAMMABLE LIQUID POWERED or UN3528, ENGINE, FUEL CELL, FLAMMABLE
  LIQUID POWERED or UN3528, ENGINE, INTERNAL COMBUSTION, FLAMMABLE
  LIQUID POWERED or UN3528, MACHINERY, FUEL CELL, FLAMMABLE LIQUID
  POWERED or UN3528, MACHINERY, INTERNAL COMBUSTION, FLAMMABLE LIQUID
  POWERED or UN3529, ENGINE, FUEL CELL, FLAMMABLE GAS POWERED or UN3529,
  ENGINE, INTERNAL COMBUSTION, FLAMMABLE GAS POWERED or UN3529,
  MACHINERY, FUEL CELL, FLAMMABLE GAS POWERED or UN3529, MACHINERY,
  INTERNAL COMBUSTION, FLAMMABLE GAS POWERED or UN3530, ENGINE, INTERNAL
  COMBUSTION or UN3530, MACHINERY, INTERNAL COMBUSTION must be handled,
  offered for transport or transported in accordance with the following
  requirements of the ICAO Technical Instructions:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Special Provision A87 of Chapter 3, Special
    provisions, of Part 3, Dangerous Goods List, Special Provisions and
    Limited and Excepted Quantities;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Packing Instruction 950 of Chapter 11, Class 9 ---
    Miscellaneous dangerous goods, of Part 4, Packing Instructions, in
    the case of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} UN3166, VEHICLE, FLAMMABLE LIQUID POWERED, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} UN3166, VEHICLE, FUEL CELL, FLAMMABLE LIQUID
      POWERED;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Packing Instruction 951 of Chapter 11, Class 9 ---
    Miscellaneous dangerous goods, of Part 4, Packing Instructions, in
    the case of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} UN3166, VEHICLE, FLAMMABLE GAS POWERED, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} UN3166, VEHICLE, FUEL CELL, FLAMMABLE GAS
      POWERED;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} Packing Instruction 378 of Chapter 5, Class 3 ---
    Flammable liquids, of Part 4, Packing Instructions, in the case of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} UN3528, ENGINE, INTERNAL COMBUSTION, FLAMMABLE
      LIQUID POWERED,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} UN3528, ENGINE, FUEL CELL, FLAMMABLE LIQUID
      POWERED,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} UN3528, MACHINERY, FUEL CELL, FLAMMABLE LIQUID
      POWERED, or

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} UN3528, MACHINERY, INTERNAL COMBUSTION,
      FLAMMABLE LIQUID POWERED;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} Packing Instruction 220 of Chapter 4, Class 2 ---
    Gases, of Part 4, Packing Instructions, in the case of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} UN3529, ENGINE, INTERNAL COMBUSTION, FLAMMABLE
      GAS POWERED,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} UN3529, ENGINE, FUEL CELL, FLAMMABLE GAS
      POWERED,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} UN3529, MACHINERY, FUEL CELL, FLAMMABLE GAS
      POWERED, or

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} UN3529, MACHINERY, INTERNAL COMBUSTION,
      FLAMMABLE GAS POWERED; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} Packing Instruction 972 of Chapter 11, Class 9 ---
    Miscellaneous dangerous goods, of Part 4, Packing Instructions, in
    the case of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} UN3530, ENGINE, INTERNAL COMBUSTION, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} UN3530, MACHINERY, INTERNAL COMBUSTION.

###### [Fire Extinguishers]{.HTitleText4} {#fire-extinguishers .SchedHeadL4}

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} When dangerous goods are UN1044, FIRE EXTINGUISHERS,
  Class 2.2, they must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} be in compliance with section 5.10 of Part 5 (Means
    of Containment);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} have a capacity less than or equal to 18 L when
    they are transported on board a passenger carrying aircraft; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} be packed in accordance with Packing Instruction
    213 of Chapter 4, Class 2 --- Gases, of Part 4, Packing
    Instructions, of the ICAO Technical Instructions.

###### [Gases]{.HTitleText4} {#gases .SchedHeadL4}

- [(9)]{.lawlabel} The following dangerous goods that are included in
  Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, must be in a means of containment set out
  in subsection (10):

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} UN1011, BUTANE;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} UN1012, BUTYLENE;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} UN1055, ISOBUTYLENE;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} UN1075, LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GASES;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} UN1077, PROPYLENE;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} UN1969, ISOBUTANE; or

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} UN1978, PROPANE.

- [(10)]{.lawlabel} The dangerous goods referred to in subsection (9)
  must be contained in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a means of containment that is marked TC-51, DOT-51
    or CTC-51 and that is in standard with CSA B622 and Appendices A and
    B of CSA B620; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a cylinder that is in compliance with section 5.10
    of Part 5 (Means of Containment), and

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the cylinder has a capacity less than or equal to
      100 L,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the dangerous goods are transported in
      cylinders on board a passenger carrying aircraft, the total
      capacity of all the cylinders must be less than or equal to 120 L,
      and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the cylinder is secured in an upright position
      or in as near an upright position as possible to prevent movement
      during transport.

###### [Batteries]{.HTitleText4} {#batteries .SchedHeadL4}

- [(11)]{.lawlabel} Dangerous goods that are UN2794, BATTERIES, WET,
  FILLED WITH ACID, Class 8, UN2795, BATTERIES, WET, FILLED WITH ALKALI,
  Class 8, or UN2800, BATTERIES, WET, NON-SPILLABLE, Class 8, must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} be transported in accordance with

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the third sentence of Special Provision A123 of
      Chapter 3, Special provisions, of Part 3, Dangerous Goods List,
      Special Provisions and Limited and Excepted Quantities, of the
      ICAO Technical Instructions, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the following packing instructions of Chapter
      10, Class 8 --- Corrosives, of Part 4, Packing Instructions, of
      the ICAO Technical Instructions, except that, when the aircraft is
      not a pressurized aircraft, section 1.1.6 of Chapter 1, General
      packing requirements, of Part 4, Packing Instructions, of the ICAO
      Technical Instructions does not apply:

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} for batteries with the UN number UN2794 or
        UN2795, Packing Instruction 870, and

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} for batteries with the UN number UN2800,
        Packing Instruction 872; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the batteries are transported on board a
    passenger carrying aircraft, have a gross mass less than or equal to
    120 kg.

###### [Sodium Chlorite and Hypochlorite Solution]{.HTitleText4} {#sodium-chlorite-and-hypochlorite-solution .SchedHeadL4}

- [(12)]{.lawlabel} When dangerous goods are UN1496, SODIUM CHLORITE,
  Class 5.1, or UN1791, HYPOCHLORITE SOLUTION, Class 8,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the available chlorine must be 7% or less;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of the dangerous goods in an inner
    means of containment must be less than or equal to 5 L or 5 kg and,
    in an outer means of containment must be less than or equal to 20 L
    or 20 kg;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods must be placed in a leakproof
    inner means of containment that is a combination packaging, as
    defined in Chapter 3, General information, of Part 1, General, of
    the ICAO Technical Instructions; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the inner means of containment must be placed in an
    outer means of containment that is designed, constructed, filled,
    closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of
    transport, including handling, there will be no accidental release
    of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety.

###### [Pilot-in-command Responsibilities]{.HTitleText4} {#pilot-in-command-responsibilities .SchedHeadL4}

- [(13)]{.lawlabel} An air carrier must ensure that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command of an aircraft, other than a
    helicopter, transporting dangerous goods

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} briefs flight attendants, if any, on the nature
      and location of the dangerous goods that are in any compartment to
      which the flight attendants have access, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} completes and signs a manifest, journey log or
      flight record, or any other type of document designated for this
      purpose in the Operator's Manual, that includes the shipping name,
      UN number, class and quantity of dangerous goods transported that
      day;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at the end of each day, the pilot-in-command of a
    helicopter transporting dangerous goods completes and signs a
    manifest, journey log or flight record or any other type of document
    designated for this purpose in the Operator's Manual, that includes
    the words "Dangerous Goods Transported" or "[Marchandises
    dangereuses transportées]{.otherLang lang="fr"}";

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air carrier keeps the documents referred to in
    paragraphs (a) and (b) for 12 months after the date on which the
    dangerous goods are no longer in transport; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} when an in-flight emergency occurs and
    circumstances permit, the pilot-in-command

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} complies with section 4.3, Information to be
      provided by the pilot-in-command in case of in-flight emergency,
      of Chapter 4, Provision of information, of Part 7, Operator's
      Responsibilities, of the ICAO Technical Instructions, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for an external load of dangerous goods
      suspended from a helicopter, notifies the appropriate air traffic
      services unit that dangerous goods are in the external load.

###### [Records]{.HTitleText4} {#records .SchedHeadL4}

- [(14)]{.lawlabel} An air carrier must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the consignor, the person who accepts the
    dangerous goods or the person who loads the aircraft is not an
    employee of the air carrier, keep the following information for 12
    months after the date on which the dangerous goods are no longer in
    transport:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of each consignor of
      dangerous goods, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the person who

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} accepts each consignment of dangerous goods or
        directly supervises the acceptance of the dangerous goods, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} loads and secures the dangerous goods or
        directly supervises the loading and securing of the dangerous
        goods;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} keep a copy of the information referred to in
    clause (1)(b)(iv)(A) for 12 months after the date on which the
    dangerous goods are no longer in transport; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} for transport by helicopter, ensure that the
    following information is prepared before the dangerous goods are
    transported and is kept for 12 months after the date on which the
    dangerous goods are no longer in transport:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of each consignor of
      dangerous goods,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the approximate date of transport,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the locations to and from which the dangerous
      goods are to be transported,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the shipping name, the UN number, the class and
      the quantity of dangerous goods to be transported, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the name of the air carrier's employee who
      prepares the information.

- [(15)]{.lawlabel} An air carrier must produce a record, notice or
  report required by subsection (1) within 15 days after the day on
  which a written request is received from an inspector.

- SOR/2014-152, s. 33
- SOR/2016-95, s. 41
- SOR/2017-253, s. 29

#### [Private Aircraft]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230649 .Subheading}

**[[12.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.10 .sectionLabel}** A person may handle
or transport dangerous goods within Canada by small aircraft or
helicopter registered as private aircraft under sections 202.16 and
202.17 of the [Canadian Aviation
Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-96-433) if the dangerous goods

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} are intended for non-commercial recreational use; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} are not forbidden for transport by Schedule 1 or
  Schedule 3 to these Regulations or by the ICAO Technical Instructions.

#### [Geological Core Samples]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230653 .Subheading}

**[[12.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.11 .sectionLabel}** A person may
handle, offer for transport or transport by aircraft within Canada
dangerous goods that are contained in geological core samples less than
or equal to 100 mm in diameter if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} when the consignor is not the air carrier, the
  consignor notifies the air carrier of the presence of the core samples
  before offering them for transport;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the core samples are transported in wooden core
  sample boxes that are wrapped in a sealed plastic or polyethylene bag
  or in a means of containment that is equally leak-proof;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the core samples as well as the means of containment
  are secured to prevent movement during transport; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} where the core samples contain radioactive material,
  they are contained in a means of containment in accordance with the
  [Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances
  Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2000-208).

#### [Aerial Work]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230659 .Subheading}

- **[[12.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.12
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person may handle, offer for
  transport or transport dangerous goods by aircraft within Canada if
  the dangerous goods are being used at the location where the following
  aerial work takes place:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} active fire suppression;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} aerial cloud seeding;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} aerial drip torching;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} agriculture;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} avalanche control;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} forestry;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} horticulture;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} hydrographic or seismographic work; or

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} pollution control.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The dangerous goods must be contained in a means of
  containment that is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a tank, a container or an apparatus that is an
    integral part of the aircraft or that is attached to the aircraft in
    accordance with the Certificate of Airworthiness issued under the
    [Canadian Aviation Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-96-433);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a cylindrical collapsible rubber drum that is
    transported in or suspended from an aircraft and that is
    constructed, tested, inspected and used in accordance with
    MIL-D-23119G;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a collapsible fabric tank that is transported
    suspended from a helicopter and that is constructed of material and
    seamed in accordance with MIL-T-52983G; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a small means of containment designed, constructed,
    filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal
    conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no
    accidental release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public
    safety.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The air carrier must ensure that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person who loads and secures the dangerous
    goods on board the aircraft is trained, or works under the direct
    supervision of a person who is trained, in accordance with Part 6
    (Training) of these Regulations and Chapter 4, Training, of Part 1,
    General, of the ICAO Technical Instructions;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the dangerous goods are handled or transported
    by a person other than an employee of the air carrier, that person
    is trained in accordance with Part 6 (Training) of these Regulations
    and Chapter 4, Training, of Part 1, General, of the ICAO Technical
    Instructions;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air carrier complies with Part 8 (Reporting
    Requirements) of these Regulations;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if the pilot-in-command of the aircraft does not
    load or directly supervise the loading of the dangerous goods, the
    person who loads and secures the dangerous goods gives the
    pilot-in-command, in writing, the following information for each of
    the dangerous goods:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} its shipping name, UN number and class, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the gross mass of the dangerous goods and, in
      the case of explosives, the net explosives quantity;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} smoking is prohibited on board the aircraft and
    each area or compartment of the aircraft containing dangerous goods
    is ventilated to prevent the accumulation of vapour;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} when an in-flight emergency occurs and
    circumstances permit, the pilot-in-command complies with section
    4.3, Information to be provided by the pilot-in-command in case of
    in-flight emergency, of Chapter 4, Provision of information, of Part
    7, Operator's Responsibilities, of the ICAO Technical Instructions;
    and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the person who loads and secures or directly
    supervises the loading and securing of dangerous goods on board the
    aircraft

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} complies with section 3.1, Inspection for damage
      or leakage, of Chapter 3, Inspection and decontamination, of Part
      7, Operator's Responsibilities, of the ICAO Technical
      Instructions, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} segregates the means of containment that contain
      dangerous goods that could react dangerously with one another in
      case of a release, in accordance with Table 7-1, "Segregation
      between packages", of Chapter 2, Storage and loading, of Part 7,
      Operator's Responsibilities, of the ICAO Technical Instructions.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 48
- SOR/2008-34, s. 99
- SOR/2014-152, s. 34
- SOR/2016-95, s. 41
- SOR/2017-253, s. 30
:::

#### [Measuring Instruments]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230690 .Subheading}

**[[12.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.13 .sectionLabel}** A person may handle
or transport by aircraft within Canada a measuring instrument that
contains dangerous goods if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person who is responsible for the measuring
  instrument

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} ensures that the measuring instrument or its means
    of containment has displayed on it labels in accordance with Chapter
    3, Labelling, of Part 5, Shipper's Responsibilities, of the ICAO
    Technical Instructions,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} before transporting the measuring instrument on
    the aircraft, has the written agreement of the air carrier to use or
    transport the measuring instrument on board the aircraft, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} is trained in accordance with Part 6 (Training)
    of these Regulations and Chapter 4, Training, of Part 1, General, of
    the ICAO Technical Instructions and complies with all laws
    applicable to the measuring instrument;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the measuring instrument is placed or used in a
  location in the aircraft that is known to the pilot-in-command and the
  flight crew; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} when the measuring instrument contains radioactive
  materials,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the radiation level at 100 mm from any point of the
    external surface of the instrument is less than or equal to
    100 µSv/h (10 millirems per hour), and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the activity of the measuring instrument does not
    exceed the applicable exception limit set out in the column entitled
    "Item limits" in Table 2-14, "Activity limits for excepted
    packages", of Chapter 7, Class 7 --- Radioactive material, of Part
    2, Classification of Dangerous Goods, of the ICAO Technical
    Instructions.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 49
- SOR/2014-152, s. 35
- SOR/2017-253, s. 31
:::

#### [Medical Aid]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230702 .Subheading}

- **[[12.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.14
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person may handle, offer for
  transport or transport by aircraft within Canada dangerous goods,
  other than Class 2, Gases, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods will be used or part of the
    dangerous goods have been used for a person who will require or who
    has required medical aid during flight;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the transport of the dangerous goods is not
    forbidden by Schedule 1 or Schedule 3 of these Regulations or the
    ICAO Technical Instructions;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} before the dangerous goods are loaded, the person
    who offers them for transport receives the agreement of the air
    carrier to transport the dangerous goods on board the aircraft;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the air carrier

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} directly supervises the loading and securing of
      the dangerous goods on board the aircraft so that they do not move
      during transport,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} complies with section 3.1, Inspection for damage
      or leakage, of Chapter 3, Inspection and decontamination, of Part
      7, Operator's Responsibilities, of the ICAO Technical
      Instructions, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} provides to the pilot-in-command, in writing,
      the shipping name, the UN number and the class of the dangerous
      goods and their location on board the aircraft;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2002-306\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in the event of a change of aircraft or flight
    crew, the pilot-in-command communicates the information required by
    subparagraph (d)(iii) to the next pilot-in-command;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the air carrier's employees are trained, or work
    under the direct supervision of a person who is trained, in
    accordance with Part 6 (Training) of these Regulations and Chapter
    4, Training, of Part 1, General, of the ICAO Technical Instructions;
    and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the air carrier complies with Part 8 (Reporting
    Requirements) of these Regulations.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air carrier and the person who offers the
  dangerous goods for transport must ensure that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are contained in a means of
    containment that is designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured
    and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport,
    including handling, there will be no accidental release of the
    dangerous goods that could endanger public safety; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the means of containment has displayed on it the
    package markings and labels required by Chapter 2, Marking, and
    Chapter 3, Labelling, of Part 5, Shipper's Responsibilities, of the
    ICAO Technical Instructions.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person may handle, offer for transport or transport
  by aircraft within Canada UN1072, OXYGEN, COMPRESSED, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air carrier and the person who offers the
    dangerous goods for transport comply with the requirements of
    subsection (1) and paragraph (2)(b);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are in a cylinder that is in
    compliance with section 5.10 of Part 5 (Means of Containment) of
    these Regulations;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} each cylinder contains a quantity of UN1072,
    OXYGEN, COMPRESSED, that is less than or equal to 850 L or 30 ft^3^;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the number of cylinders containing UN1072, OXYGEN,
    COMPRESSED, does not exceed 6 owned by the air carrier and one
    additional cylinder for each passenger who needs the oxygen at
    destination; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command is advised of the number of
    cylinders loaded on board the aircraft.

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2014-152\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 50
- SOR/2008-34, s. 100
- SOR/2014-152, s. 36
- SOR/2016-95, s. 41
- SOR/2017-253, s. 32
:::

**[[12.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.15 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed,
SOR/2008-34, s. 101\]]{.Repealed}

**[[12.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.16 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed,
SOR/2008-34, s. 101\]]{.Repealed}

#### [Flight Deck Loading Restrictions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1230730 .Subheading}

**[[12.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12.17 .sectionLabel}** A person may handle
or transport within Canada, by an aircraft that does not have a Class B,
Class C or Class D cargo compartment, dangerous goods other than those
included in Class 4.3, Water Reactive Substances, if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person complies with

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} paragraphs 12.1(1)(a) to (j), and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the ICAO Technical Instructions, other than
    section 2.1, Loading restrictions on flight deck and for passenger
    aircraft, of Chapter 2, Storage and loading, of Part 7, Operator's
    Responsibilities;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a certificate was issued for the aircraft under
  Subpart 4 of Part VI or Subpart 3 or 4 of Part VII of the [Canadian
  Aviation Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-96-433);

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} transport of the dangerous goods is not forbidden by
  Schedule 1 or Schedule 3 of these Regulations or the ICAO Technical
  Instructions;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} transport of the dangerous goods is not restricted by
  the ICAO Technical Instructions to cargo aircraft only; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the dangerous goods are loaded and transported in a
  compartment that is accessible during flight so that the dangerous
  goods and any other cargo can be readily reached by a crew member
  using, if necessary, a hand-held fire extinguisher.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-306, s. 53
:::

## [PART 13]{.HLabel1}[Protective Direction]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1230741 .Part}

### [Effective Date and Expiry of a Protective Direction]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230742 .Subheading}

- **[[13.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-13.1 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  protective direction takes effect on the date on which it is signed by
  the Minister or at a later date indicated in the protective direction.
  However, after the effective date of the protective direction, any
  non-compliance with it must not be enforced against a person unless
  the person has received the original signed protective direction or an
  electronic copy of it, or reasonable steps have been taken to make the
  person aware of the protective direction.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A protective direction expires on the expiry date
  specified in it. If no expiry date is specified in the protective
  direction, it expires 12 months after the date on which it is signed.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2023-155, s. 47](#1408034-1418289){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1408034-1418289.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-13.1-20200219.html "Link to previous version of section 13.1"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Requesting a Review of a Protective Direction]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230746 .Subheading}

- **[[13.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-13.2 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person may request a review of a protective direction at any time
  after it is signed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The request must be made, in writing, to the Minister
  and must include the following information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the place of business of
    the person requesting the review;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the result the person expects from the review; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} all the information necessary to support the
    request for the review.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2023-155, s. 48](#1408036-1418292){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1408036-1418292.html"
  role="button"}
:::

## [PART 14]{.HLabel1}[Equivalency Certificate]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1230755 .Part}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2023-155, s. 50

\]
:::

### [Applying for an Equivalency Certificate]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230756 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2023-155, s. 50

\]
:::

**[[14.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-14.1 .sectionLabel}** A person must apply
to the Minister in writing for an equivalency certificate and must
include the following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the applicant is an individual, the name of the
  individual;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the applicant is a company or an association, the
  name of the company or association and each association member, as the
  names appear in letters patent, articles of incorporation or any other
  document that shows the legal identity of the company or the
  association and each association member;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the address of the place of business of the
  applicant;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the telephone number, including the area code, and,
  if applicable, the electronic mailing address and the facsimile number
  of the applicant;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} if a person submits an application on behalf of a
  company or an association, the person's name and position and the
  telephone number, including the area code, and address of the person's
  place of business;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the classification of the dangerous goods and, if the
  dangerous goods are in a solution or mixture, the composition and
  percentage (specified by volume, mass or net explosives quantity) of
  each chemical;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the method of packaging the dangerous goods,
  including a description of the means of containment and the quantity
  of dangerous goods in each means of containment;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} whether the equivalency certificate is requested for
  transport by road vehicle, railway vehicle, aircraft or vessel;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} a description of the proposal for an equivalency
  certificate, including

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the requirements of the Act or these Regulations
    that the applicant proposes not to comply with,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the manner in which the activity will be carried
    out and how that manner will provide a level of safety at least
    equivalent to that provided by compliance with the Act and these
    Regulations, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} drawings, plans, calculations, procedures, test
    results and any other information necessary to support the proposal;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} the length of time or the schedule of activities for
  which the equivalency certificate is requested; and

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} the name, position and business telephone number,
  including the area code, of the person who can be contacted regarding
  the application for an equivalency certificate and who is authorized
  by the applicant to speak on the applicant's behalf.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2008-34, s. 102
- SOR/2017-253, s. 52
- [SOR/2023-155, s. 51](#1408041-1418312){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1408041-1418312.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-14.1-20200219.html "Link to previous version of section 14.1"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Issuance or Refusal of an Equivalency Certificate]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230774 .Subheading}

**[[14.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-14.2 .sectionLabel}** If an application for
an equivalency certificate is refused, the Minister must notify the
applicant, in writing, of the refusal and the reasons for the refusal.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2023-155, s. 52](#1408050-1418316){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1408050-1418316.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-14.2-20200219.html "Link to previous version of section 14.2"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Applying for Renewal of an Equivalency Certificate]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230776 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2023-155, s. 53

\]
:::

**[[14.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-14.3 .sectionLabel}** A person must apply
to the Minister in writing to renew an equivalency certificate and must
include the following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the applicant is an individual, the name of the
  individual;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the applicant is a company or an association, the
  name of the company or association and each association member, as the
  names appear in letters patent, articles of incorporation or any other
  document that shows the legal identity of the company or the
  association and each association member;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the address of the place of business of the
  applicant;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the telephone number, including the area code, and,
  if applicable, the electronic mailing address and the facsimile number
  of the applicant;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} if a person submits an application on behalf of a
  company or an association, the person's name and position and the
  telephone number, including the area code, and address of the person's
  place of business;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} certification that the information provided in the
  original application in accordance with paragraphs 14.1(f) to (i) is
  still applicable and complete;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the length of time or the schedule of activities for
  which the renewal is requested; and

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} the name, position and business telephone number,
  including the area code, of the person who can be contacted regarding
  the application for a renewal and who is authorized by the applicant
  to speak on the applicant's behalf.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2023-155, s. 54](#1408054-1418323){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1408054-1418323.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-14.3-20200219.html "Link to previous version of section 14.3"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Renewal or Refusal of a Renewal of an Equivalency Certificate]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230786 .Subheading}

- **[[14.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-14.4
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may renew an
  equivalency certificate if the Minister is satisfied, on the basis of
  the information available and the information submitted with the
  application for a renewal, that the activity authorized by the
  equivalency certificate will provide a level of safety at least
  equivalent to that provided by compliance with the Act and these
  Regulations.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If an application for a renewal is refused, the
  Minister must notify the applicant, in writing, of the refusal and the
  reasons for the refusal.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2023-155, s. 55](#1408061-1418329){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1408061-1418329.html"
  role="button"}
:::

:::

### [Revoking an Equivalency Certificate]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230790 .Subheading}

**[[14.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-14.5 .sectionLabel}** The Minister must
notify a person, in writing, of the revocation of an equivalency
certificate under subsection 31(6) of the Act and the reasons for the
revocation.

- [SOR/2023-155, s. 56](#1408063-1418333){.wb-lbx

### [Requesting a Review of a Decision to Refuse or Revoke an Equivalency Certificate]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230792 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2023-155, s. 57

\]
:::

- **[[14.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-14.6 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person may request a review of a decision to refuse or revoke an
  equivalency certificate within 30 days after the day on which the
  notification of the decision is received.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The request must be made in writing to the Minister
  and must include the following information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the place of business of
    the person requesting the review;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the reasons why the decision should be reversed;
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} all of the information necessary to support the
    request for the review.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2023-155, s. 58](#1408067-1418340){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1408067-1418340.html"

### [Processing a Request for a Review]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230799 .Subheading}

**[[14.7]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-14.7 .sectionLabel}** The Minister may
issue an equivalency certificate that was refused or reissue an
equivalency certificate that was revoked if the Minister is satisfied,
on the basis of the information available and the information submitted
with the request for review, that the activity authorized by the
equivalency certificate will provide a level of safety at least
equivalent to that provided by compliance with the Act and these
Regulations.

### [Notification of a Decision]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230801 .Subheading}

**[[14.8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-14.8 .sectionLabel}** The Minister must
notify, in writing, the person who made the request for a review of the
decision and the reasons for the decision.

## [PART 15]{.HLabel1}[Court Order]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1230803 .Part}

### [Payment of Money for Research]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230804 .Subheading}

**[[15.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-15.1 .sectionLabel}** A person who is
subject to a court order that requires payment of an amount of money
under paragraph 34(1)(d) of the Act to be used to conduct programs of
research must

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide a summary of the order, in writing, to the
  Minister within 30 days after the day on which the order is made; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} give to the Minister the amount in the form of a
  certified cheque, money order or bank draft, payable to the Receiver
  General for Canada, within the period established by the court or, if
  no period is established, within 90 days after the day on which the
  order is made.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2023-155, s. 60](#1408074-1418351){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1408074-1418351.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-15.1-20200219.html "Link to previous version of section 15.1"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Inspection Certificate]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230815 .Subheading}

**[[16.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-16.2 .sectionLabel}** An inspection

### [Detention of Dangerous Goods or Means of Containment]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230821 .Subheading}

- **[[16.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-16.3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When an inspector detains dangerous
  goods or a means of containment under subsection 17(1) or (2) of the
  Act, the inspector must deliver a Detention Notice in the form
  following this section to the person who has charge, management or
  control of the dangerous goods or of the means of containment at the
  time they are detained.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The inspector must sign and date the Notice.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The detention takes effect when the Notice is signed
  and dated by the inspector. However, any non-compliance with the
  detention must not be enforced against a person until the person has
  received the Notice or a copy of it or a reasonable attempt has been
  made to give the person the Notice or a copy of it.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The detention expires 12 months after the day on
  which it takes effect, but it may be revoked earlier, in writing, by
  an inspector.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} A person may request a review of the detention at any
  time after it takes effect and the Notice is delivered to the person
  who has charge, management or control of the dangerous goods or of the
  means of containment. The request must be made in writing to the
  Minister or the Director General and must include the following
  information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the place of business of
    the person requesting the review;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a copy of the Notice;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the reasons why the detention should be revoked;
    and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} all of the information necessary to support the
    request for the review.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The Minister or the Director General must notify the
  person, in writing, of the decision made and the reasons for the
  decision.

### [Direction to Remedy Non-compliance]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230839 .Subheading}

- **[[16.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-16.4
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When an inspector directs a person,
  under subsection 17(3) of the Act, to take necessary measures to
  remedy non-compliance with the Act and these Regulations, the
  inspector must deliver to that person a Notice of Direction to Remedy
  Non-compliance in the form following this section.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The inspector must sign and date the Notice.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Notice must also be signed and dated by one of
  the following designated persons before it is delivered to the person
  directed by the inspector to take the necessary measures: the
  Director, Compliance and Response, the Chief, Response Operations, or
  the Chief, Enforcement, of the Transport Dangerous Goods Directorate,
  Department of Transport.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The direction takes effect when the Notice is signed
  and dated in accordance with subsections (2) and (3). However, any
  non-compliance with the direction must not be enforced against a
  person until the person has received the Notice or a copy of it or a
  reasonable attempt has been made to give the person the Notice or a
  copy of it.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The direction expires 12 months after the day on
  which it takes effect, but it may be revoked earlier, in writing, by
  an inspector.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} A person may request a review of the direction at any
  time after it takes effect and the Notice is delivered to the person
  who has charge, management or control of the dangerous goods or means
  of containment. The request must be made in writing to the Minister or
  the Director General and must include the following information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the place of business of
    the person requesting the review;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a copy of the Notice;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the reasons why the direction should be revoked;
    and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} all of the information necessary to support the
    request for the review.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} The Minister or the Director General must notify the
  person, in writing, of the decision made and the reasons for the
  decision.

### [Direction Not to Import or to Return to Place of Origin]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1230858 .Subheading}

- **[[16.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-16.5
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When an inspector directs, under
  subsection 17(4) of the Act, a person who has charge, management or
  control of dangerous goods or means of containment that the dangerous
  goods or means of containment not be imported into Canada or, if they
  are already in Canada, that they be returned to their place of origin,
  the inspector must deliver to that person a Notice of Direction Not to
  Import or to Return to Place of Origin in the form following this
  section.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The inspector must sign and date the Notice.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The direction takes effect when the Notice is signed
  and dated by the inspector. However, any non-compliance with the
  direction must not be enforced against a person until the person has
  received the Notice or a copy of it or a reasonable attempt has been
  made to give the person the Notice or a copy of it.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The direction expires 12 months after the day on
  which it takes effect, but it may be revoked earlier, in writing, by
  an inspector.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} A person may request a review of the direction at any
  time after it takes effect and the Notice is delivered to the person
  who has charge, management or control of the dangerous goods or means
  of containment. The request must be made in writing to the Minister or
  the Director General and must include the following information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the place of business of
    the person requesting the review;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a copy of the Notice;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the reasons why the direction should be revoked;
    and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} all of the information necessary to support the
    request for the review.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The Minister or the Director General must notify the
  person, in writing, of the decision made and the reasons for the
  decision.
